        Martin and Marie (Pleinis) Fiedler
Martin Karl Fiedler, brother of Gottfried Fiedler, was born in Rosenberg, near
Zurichtal, Crimea on Jan. 28, 1874. At the age of two years he came to the U.S.
with his parents, Johann Jacob and Helene Elizabeth (Martens) Fiedler.

The family settled in Yankton County, near Mission Hill. Martin was the youngest
of 11 children; all six who survived immigrated to SD. Martin's grandparents,
Michael Fiedler and Regina Renata, nee Faust, were born in Prussia and lived in
Rosenberg, Jekaterinoslaw, South Russia until moving to Crimea in about 1862.
Undoubtedly the lure of the Homestead Act and the threat of military induction
bore heavily on the decision to leave Crimea in 1876.

Mrs. Fiedler (nee Marie Pleinis) was born in Neudorf, South Russia on Oct. 14,
1884, and at the age of three years came to America with her parents, Jacob
Pleinis and Magdalena, nee Landenberger. They homesteaded five miles north of
Java. Marie was the oldest of 10 children. She married Martin in Java on Feb. 7,
1905, and they made their home on a farm near Mission Hill for 12 years before
moving back to Java.

In Mar. of 1917, Mr. Fiedler purchased the Jacob Pleinis Sr., farm north of
Java. The family then consisted of Mr. and Mrs. Fiedler and their five children,
Herman, Carl, Clara, Art and Harold. The move was a big ordeal, as it was done
by rail transportation. Each of the older children was responsible for taking
care of some of the personal belongings, while taking this long train ride.
Clara remembers carrying a little pail of water containing the goldfish, which
she proudly showed to every passenger that came on board.

It took a great deal of work to get settled. Two more children, Gerhardt and
Eileen, were born within the next six years. Many improvements were made on the
farm. The biggest one was the installation of a Delco light plant in 1927.

In 1939, Mr. and Mrs. Fiedler retired and moved to Java. Their son, Art,
purchased the home farm, and Art, Herman and Harold farmed the land surrounding
it. Since their retirement, Harold's sons, Arlo and Ronald, have farmed the
land.

Mr. Fiedler passed away Apr. 28, 1945, and Mrs. Fiedler passed away Aug. 21,
1970.

(Photo:) Carl, Gerhardt, Herman, Harold, Art, Eileen, Martin, Marie, and Clara
         Fiedler

Mr. and Mrs. Fiedler were the parents of eight children. Herman, who died Sept.
14, 1995, married Emma Stangl. Carl of Coeur d'Alene, ID married Adriane Kinney,
Clara of Java married Jake Nehlich, Arthur of Java married Irene Bieber, Harold
of Aberdeen married Clara Rosin, Gerhardt of Java married Viola Schadler, and
Eileen, who died July 30, 1989, married Reuben Schmierer. Agnes Ruth died in
infancy in Mission Hill.

        J. Herman and Emma (Stangl) Fiedler
J. Herman Fiedler was born to Martin and Marie (Pleinis) Fiedler on Nov. 17,
1905, near Mission Hill in Yankton County. As a youth, he attended school near
Mission Hill and near Java. His family moved from Yankton County to rural Java
in Walworth County in 1917. He helped on the family farm and worked for other
farmers until farming for himself. During the 1940's he operated the Grand
Theater in Java along with Ben Stiegelmeier.

Emma Stangl was born to Anton and Minnie (Brandt) Stangl on Dec. 29, 1909, at
the family home in Spring Lake Township, Walworth County. She began her
education in the rural grade school in that township. After attending two years
of high school in Bowdle, she graduated from Java High School in 1927. Emma
attended NSTC in Aberdeen to get her teaching certificate. She taught in rural
schools in Hand, Pennington, and Walworth Counties and in the towns of Leola,
Sisseton, and Java.

Emma and Herman married on Oct. 21, 1944, and established their home in Java.
Herman operated a small grain farm north of Java for many years. He also served
as the office manager for the Walworth County ASCS office in Selby for 25 years.
He was a member of the Walworth County Crop Improvement Association and served
on the board of directors of the Java Equity Exchange Co-op.

(Photo:) Marion, Carolyn, Diane, Emma, and Herman Fiedler

Emma taught St. Paul Lutheran Sunday School for 15 years and was the leader of
the Nimble Fingers 4-H club in Walworth County for 15 years. She was a charter
member of the Home Arts Extension Club in 1949 and remained a member for more
than 40 years. She was also involved as a parent in the school activities of her
daughters.

The couple had three daughters, all graduates of Java High School. Marion
graduated from SDSU in Brookings, the University of Chicago, and the University
of Connecticut. In 1969, she married Roger Ehrich. They currently reside in
Blacksburg, VA with their son, Daniel. Marion is a professor of Veterinary
Toxicology at the Virginia-Maryland College of Veterinary Medicine. Her husband
is a professor of Computer Science at Virginia Tech.

Carolyn graduated from NSC in Aberdeen and SDSU in Brookings. In 1968, she
married Roger Lind. The Linds reside in Jackson, MN, where Carolyn works in the
human service area as a youth counselor. Roger is a Vice-President with Bank
Midwest. Their two daughters, Carin and Dena, are professionally employed in the
Minneapolis area.

Diane graduated from SDSU in Brookings, Iowa State University, and the
University of WY. In 1980, she married Michael Smith. They reside in Laramie, WY
with their daughter, Emily. Diane is a self-employed attorney and Mike is a
professor of Renewable Resources at the University of WY.

In 1993, Emma and Herman sold the family home in Java and moved to an apartment
in Jackson, MN. Herman passed away in Jackson on Sept. 14, 1995, and is buried
in St. Paul Lutheran Cemetery in Java. Emma continues to live in her apartment
in Jackson, MN.

        Harold and Clara (Rosin) Fiedler
Harold was born Mar. 29, 1915, to Martin and Marie (Pleinis) Fiedler near
Mission Hill in Yankton County. In 1917 his family moved to a farm five miles
north of Java. He attended the Sunshine School in Highland Township, and helped
with the work on the farm until 1937.

Clara was born Nov. 9, 1913, to William and Dorothea (Stoecker) Rosin at a farm
four miles NW of Java, which is now the John Haux farm. When she was one year
old the family moved to a farm four miles NE of Selby, one-and-a-half miles west
of Lake Hiddenwood Park. She attended Selby Grade and High School. She dropped
out of school in her junior year to help with house and farm work until her
marriage to Harold Fiedler on Sept. 12, 1937, at St. John's Lutheran Church at
Selby. They moved to a farm five miles NW of Java where they lived for 19 years.
Due to a lack of water they sold the farm and in the fall of 1956 they moved
into Java. Harold worked for the ASC for 17 years until 1973 when his job with
the ASC was terminated.

(Photo:) Clara and Harold Fiedler

In 1973, they moved to Aberdeen where he was employed for 15 years at Ken's
Fairway Foods. Clara was a homemaker, and also helped with outdoor work. They
are now retired and living in Aberdeen.

Harold and Clara Fiedler are the parents of three sons: Arlo and Lorraine
Fiedler of Java; Kenneth and Deane Fiedler of Aberdeen; Ronald and Margie
Fiedler living on a farm three miles north of Java.

Harold and Clara are blessed with 9 grandchildren, one of which (a
granddaughter) is deceased. They have eight great-grandchildren.

        Arlo and Lorrain (Opheim) Fiedler
Arlo Fiedler, son of Harold and Clara (Rosin) Fiedler, was born in 1939. He
attended the first eight years of school in rural Sunshine and Helms Schools
near Java, and four years at Java High School, graduating in 1957. After
graduation, he attended railroad telegraphy school in Minneapolis, MN, then
worked for the Milwaukee Railroad as agent and telegraph operator in WI until
1960. He then served in the Army until 1962. After serving in the Army, he
returned home and started farming with his uncles on the original Martin Fiedler
farm. In 1963, he married Lorrain Opheim, who was born in 1942 and grew up on a
farm near Selby. She attended eight years of grade school in rural Lindberg
School near Selby, and four years in Selby High School, graduating in 1960. She
then attended a business college in Aberdeen and worked for an insurance agency
until her marriage to Arlo in 1963.

(Photo:) Arlo and Lorrain Fiedler Family

After their marriage, Arlo continued farming and driving school bus for the Java
school system. Lorrain worked part-time for the Walworth County Treasurer's
office until 1966, when she started working for Java Equity, now North Central
Farmers Elevator.

They have two daughters, Brenda and Lisa, and five grandchildren.

Brenda is an Opthalmolic Technician and is married to Steve Tryon, an Air
Traffic Controller. They have two daughters, Heather and Andrea. They are living
in Lansing, MI.

Lisa is married to Troy Beck, and are both farming in the Artas area. They have
three children, Colby, Robert, and Marissa.

Arlo and Lorrain continue living in Java; Arlo still farms and Lorrain is
working at North Central Farmers Elevator.

        Ronald and Marjorie (Mueller) Fiedler
Ron and Margie have known each other since they were very young, since they both
grew up in the Java area. The Fiedler and Mueller families were farm neighbors
and family friends. Ron and Margie both attended local schools and became high
school sweethearts.

Ron was born to Harold and Clara Fiedler on Apr. 14, 1947. He joined two
brothers, Arlo and Kenneth. Ron attended West Highland Country School for two
years before the family moved into town. Marjorie was born July 10, 1947 to Otto
and Anna Mueller. She has four sisters. Marlene Stadel, Shirley Spiry, Eloise
Lassle, and Susan May. One brother, Marvin, died at age 5 of Leukemia. She
attended West Highland Country School until the 5th grade, when the school
closed and the children were bussed to school in Java.

After their marriage on July 16, 1965, Ron worked for the local farm cooperative
and Margie was the school secretary. In 1967, Ron joined the farming operation
of his in-laws and the couple moved their mobile home three-and-a-half miles
north of town. In 1974 Otto and Anna retired and moved into town, and the
Fiedlers moved into the farmhouse.

Ron and Margie had four children:

Richard was born Feb. 8, 1966.  He was raised in the Java area and graduated
from Java High in 1984. He had the privilege of starting and ending his years at
Java Public School with basically the same classmates. After high school, he
attended college at SDSM&T, where he received a degree in Mechanical
Engineering. In 1989 he began full-time employment with Hutchinson Technology
(maker of computer components) in Hutchinson, MN, and is currently with HTI as
the Product Development Manager. In 1991, he married Beth Thorstenson of Selby.
Beth is currently a Registered Nurse working as the Coordinator for Cardiac
Rehabilitation at the Glencoe Area Hospital. Beth and Rich have two sons, Brady
and Collin. Rich spends his limited free time playing golf, fishing, hunting,
and returning to Java for farming. Beth spends her free time golfing and taking
care of their children.

Heidi, born Apr. 9, 1968, went to school in Java until her junior year, when the
high school closed in 1985. She was killed in a tragic automobile accident in
1986, just one week after her high school graduation from Selby Area High
School.

(Photo:) Jodi, Corey, Richard, Heidi (deceased), Ron and Marjorie Fiedler

Corey, born July 7, 1971, attended grade school in Java and graduated from Selby
Area High School in 1989. He has a Business degree from NSU and lives and works
in Sioux Falls.

Jodi, born Jan. 12, 1973, completed grade school in Java and graduated from
Selby Area High School in 1991. She has a Chemical Engineering degree from
SDSM&T. She and her husband, Timothy Elliott from Russellville, AL, make their
home in Hutchinson, MN. They have two sons, Adam and Andrew.

Ron has been active in the local Community Club, served on the North Central
Farmers Elevator Board, and the Farm Service Agency Board. If he has any spare
time in the summer, he likes fishing on Lake Oahe. Both Ron and Margie are
baptized and confirmed members of St. Paul Lutheran Church and have served on
the church council. Margie has taught Sunday school and belongs to WELCA, the
women's service group. She also is a member of the Home Arts Club. Both enjoy
attending high school athletic events and having their children and
grandchildren visit the farm.

The Fiedlers purchased the original farm and added acres to the small grain and
cow-calf operation. Margie worked in her home as a seamstress while the children
were young, then as a photographer for the Java Herald/Selby Record for five
years. In 1993 she began working for Marin-Biel Insurance Agency, first in Java,
then in the Selby office.

        Gerhardt and Viola (Schadler) Fiedler
Gerhardt Fiedler, youngest son of Martin and Marie (Pleinis) Fiedler, was born
June 17, 1919. He grew up on the family farm, graduating from Java High School
in 1937. He attended NSC in Aberdeen and taught country schools for four years
before entering the Army. He served in the Medical Corps, training at
Fitzsimmons Hospital in Denver, CO and later was stationed in OR. His unit went
overseas in 1944, landed in England and followed the invasion of Europe. They
had a thousand-bed tent hospital in Belgium during the "Battle of the Bulge." He
received his honorable discharge in 1945. He worked at Elmer's Market in Java
and as Deputy County Auditor in Selby before becoming a bulk tank salesman for
the Java Co-op in 1948.

Gerhardt is a charter member of the LaVerne Bauer Post of the American Legion,
where he has served as Adjutant for many years, and is secretary-treasurer of
the Volunteer Firemen. He was a member of the City Council for 31 years, past
Treasurer of the Java Chamber of Commerce, and a PTA member. He has been a
council member and on the finance committee of the St. Paul Lutheran Church
numerous times.

(Photo:) Gerhardt and Viola Fiedler

On Nov. 28, 1946, he was united in marriage with Viola Schadler, daughter of
John and Barbara Schadler. Viola was born Jan. 28, 1922 at Goodrich, ND. She
received her elementary and high school education in Java, graduating in 1939.
She attended Romily's Beauty School in Aberdeen. She worked in Selby and
Aberdeen before buying and managing the Java Beauty Shop until 1947. Viola is a
charter member of the Java American Legion Auxiliary and has been an officer
many years. She is a member and past officer of the ladies' organization of St.
Paul Lutheran Church (WELCA). She was a member and officer of the former So and
Sew Extension Club, PTA, and Band Mother.

Gerhardt and Viola have two daughters and one son (deceased). Judy is married to
James Schnaible and works for SD Social Services in Rapid City. She is a 1966
graduate of Java High and NSC of Aberdeen; Carol is married to Donley Bieber and
works at Dakota Eye Institute in Bismarck, ND. She graduated from Java High in
1967 and attended Commercial Business College in Bismarck. They have two sons,
Kyle, a golf pro in CA, and Mark, a student at Bismarck State College; Joel
graduated from Java High in 1976 and Spearfish College in 1980. He was a "disk
jockey" and later managed a Rent to Own store in Rapid City. He died in 1994. He
was married to Cynthia Savins. His wife, daughter Mikayla, and stepdaughter,
Nicole, live in Pendelton, OR.

        Philipp and Katharina (Schrum) Flemmer
Philipp Flemmer was born on Oct. 1, 1868, in Gluckstal, South Russia. He joined
the migration to America in 1889 with the Martin Grosz family, and filed on a
claim eight miles north of Java, in the Hiddenwood area. On Dec. 26, 1897, he
married Katharina Schrum at Ashley, N.D.

(Photo:) Philipp and Katharina Flemmer

Katharina Schrum Flemmer was born May 26, 1880 in Beresina, Bessarabia. She
accompanied her parents to America in 1888.

Having acquired a team of horses, Philipp Flemmer started the first dray line in
Java. At times, he drove to Ipswich, which was then the end of the railroad, and
brought settlers into the Java area, one of whom was Rev. Braun, the first
Pastor of the Lutheran church in Java.

In 1905, the Philipp Flemmer family moved to Eureka, where he worked for the
Serr and Quast dray line concern.

Six children were born to the Flemmers: Christian; Emma Becker; Adeline Stroup;
Mary Hepper; Ann (L.M.) Graves; and Gertrude (E.R.) Kary.

        Art Frank
Art was born Aug. 2, 1921 to William and Bertha Frank of rural Java. After his
mother passed away, his grandparents, John and Louise Krause, also of rural
Java, raised him. After retiring from farming, they moved to Java.

Art graduated from Java High School in 1939. He attended SDSU at Brookings,
where he took a course in Civil Engineering. During World War II Art served as a
radio transmitter repairman in the Army Air Corps in the South Pacific.

After the war, Art returned to Java and started work as a carpenter. He has
helped build and remodel many houses, barns, etc. in the area. He is also a
"handy man" at fixing plumbing and electrical problems.

Art has been very active in the Java community. He has served on the Java City
Council for many years. He is always willing to offer a helping hand to any
projects in the Java area.

        Earl and Maurene (Maxine Haux) Frank
Earl was born Aug. 16, 1936, at Java to William and Lydia (Krause) Frank. Earl
graduated from Java High School in 1954 and from NSC in 1958. He then joined the
Air Force and retired in 1980 after 22 years.

Maurene was born Nov. 2, 1936, at Java. Her parents were David and Frieda
(Christman) Haux. Maurene graduated from Java High School in 1954 and worked at

        The Freimark Family
Ernst Freimark was born in 1824, immigrated to Friedenstal, Bessarabia in 1834
by way of Poland, and settled in Russia.

Gottlieb Friemark was born July 7, 1862, in South Russia. In 1889, the family
came to the U.S. and homesteaded in the Sutley area of Campbell County north of
Java.

In 1895, Gottlieb's first wife, Rosina Ernst, died in childbirth. Children from
this marriage were Fred, Gottlieb, Elizabeth, Salomina, and two children that
died in childhood.

Gottlieb married Charlotte Geier Bader in 1896. She was born to the John Geiers
on July 28, 1870, in Odessa, Russia. Charlotte was married to Anton Bader and
they had two children, one of whom, a daughter, died. Their son is Christ Bader.

Charlotte and Gottlieb had: Emil, Lydia (died as a teen), Ameila (Molly),
Magdalena (Maggie), John, Gottlieb and Arthur. Gottleib was a merchant at Java
in the early 1900's. He passed away July 28, 1926 and Charlotte died June 13,
1941.

Arthur Freimark was born Apr. 26, 1905. He was united in marriage with Claudia
Balliet on Oct. 15, 1929. She was born Aug. 16, 1908, to Fred and Katie (Moser)
Balliet. The children of Arthur and Claudia are: Stanley, born in 1930 and died
as an infant; Betty, born Sept. 5, 1931; LeRoy, born Feb. 17, 1933; and Delbert,
born Aug. 15, 1936.

Betty taught country school before her marriage to Christ W. Hoffman of Ashley,
ND. They were married in Chicago, IL. Christ served in World War II in the
European Theater and was awarded the Purple Heart, Bronze Medal, and Good
Conduct Medal, among others.

(Photo:) Art, LeRoy, Betty, Delbert, and Cludia Freimark

LeRoy is married to Janet Elliot of Spokane, WA. He served for 20 years in the
Air Force, traveling almost all over the world, and is retired from the service.
They have two children: Teri, married to Tom Dix of Aberdeen, has two sons;
LeRoy, Jr., is single and lives in CO.

Del married Barbara Knudson of Bowdle. Their children are: Mitch, who is married
and lives in Minneapolis, MN; Todd, who lives in Watertown; and Shelly, who is
married to James McDonald from the country of Scotland, lives in NY. Del served
as a Paratrooper. He married Ramona Hanson Klein on Feb. 17, 1992. She has a son
in AZ.

After Arthur and Claudia retired from the farm, they moved into Java and
operated an egg and cream buying business for several years. Art died Dec. 14,
1967, and Claudia passed away Nov. 30, 1992.

        Martin and Tina (Stuart) Gehrki
Martin and Tina (Stuart) Gehrki were prominent residents of Java from the early
1900's to 1961.

Mr. Gehrki was born in Germany and his wife, Tina, in Detroit, MI. They were
married in Java. Mr. Gehrki passed away in 1961, and Mrs. Gehrki is also
deceased.

(Photos:) Martin Gehrki and Mrs. Tina Gehrki

During their residence in Java, they were most active in community affairs. For
many years, Mr. Gehrki managed the McCabe elevator in Java. He served as mayor
of Java, was a member of the school board and, for many years, served as city
auditor. Mrs. Gehrki was active in Presbyterian Church work, served as secretary
of the Eastern Star and, at one time, was dean of the girls' dormitory of the
Java High school.

They had two daughters, Elizabeth and Agnes, both graduates of Java High School.
Elizabeth married Erwin Kuhnert and Agnes married Frank Manders.

        Johann "Jacob" and Katherina (Sieler) Geigle
Among the earliest arrivals in the Java vicinity were the Geigles in 1885.
Johann "Jacob" Geigle and family came from Helenstal, South Russia. His
grandfather Balthasor Geigle left Cal-Wurttemberg as a colonist in 1804 and
settled in the colony of Bergdorf, located in the Grigoriopol district of the
Ukraine in South Russia. His father George Philip was born in Bergdorf and in
1838, moved to the newly formed colony of Helenstal. Johann Jacob was born May
11, 1848, to George Philip and Carolina (Heinzman) Geigle. He grew up in
Helenstal and in 1872, married Katherina Sieler, daughter of Adam Sieler.

In 1870, the Czar of Russia took away the rights that had been granted by his
grandfather Czar Alexander I. In 1872, two brothers of Katharina left for the
U.S. to escape the restrictions placed on them. Henry and Peter Sieler left for
Sandusky, OH, where the first settlement of Germans from Russia took place.

When Henry and his family arrived, he was selected to scout MI, WI, IA, NE and
Dakota Territory for ideal settlement for people who had come out of Russia.

(Photo:) Katherina and Johann "Jacob" Geigle

In 1873, the Henry and Peter Sielers, and others, moved to an area north of
Yankton. Mrs. Geigle's family moved in stages to the U.S. First, her oldest
brothers Adam, Philip and his grown sons Heinrich, Adam and Peter, and her
sister Johanna (Gottlieb) Schaeffer came to Menno before 1883. Johann Jacob,
Katherina and three children landed in New York and arrived in Menno on Sept.
30, 1884. They brought with them Magdalena, the mother, who was 65 years old. A
young couple, the Adam Lenos, came with them. The rest of the Sieler family came
early the next year. They were Kaspar Sieler, Eva (Conrad) Vollmer, and
Magdalena (Wilhelm) Ottmer. The Geigles and grandma Sieler spent the winter with
the Schaeffers. The next spring the entire group, consisting of Adam, Philip,
Kaspar, Vollmers, Ottmers, Lenos, Klemmers, the Schaeffer brothers, and the
Geigles shipped their goods to Ipswich, and from there headed west by wagon.
They followed the freight trail that led to Mound City. They all filed their
claims in Blessing Township, Campbell County, located north and NW of Salt Lake.
About 1887, the post office of Sutley was created and this became their address.

The Geigles began to break sod and plant crops. They built a sod house and barn
on their preempt claim and, by 1891, had moved into the sod house on their
homestead. This house was torn down around 1950. Ervin Rau bought the homestead
and Ervin's son, Alan and his family are presently residing there.

(Photo:) Back: Adam, Jacob. Front: Caroline (Fred) Hrining, Alvina (Simon)
         Schaefer, Rosina (Matt) Borth

Twelve children were born to Johann Jacob and Katherina, of which four died in
their infancy. Adam Geigle, the oldest child, homesteaded on a farm near the
family farm and in 1920, moved to Pollock. Katherina married Chris Huether and
in 1902 they moved to Java. Christ worked for the City of Java and in 1922, they
moved onto a farm south of Java. In 1929, they moved to North Hollywood, CA.
Johanna married Fred Hirning and died in 1904. She is buried in the Odessa
Reformed Cemetery north of Java. Carolina married Fred Hirning and they
homesteaded near Burt, ND and retired to Mott, ND. Jacob took over the family
farm in 1915. Rosina married Matt Borth and they lived in Gackle, ND. Her
husband passed away at an early age and she was left with three small boys. In
1942 she moved to WA. Christina married Herman Marshall, a schoolteacher, and
they both died of the flu in 1918 and are buried in Linton, ND. Alvina married
Simon Schaefer and the family resides in Tripp. She passed away at age 94.

In 1915, the Gieigles retired from farming and moved to a home on Main Street in
Java, where they resided until their death. Mrs. Geigle passed away in Mar.
1923, and Mr. Geigle passed away in June 1933. Both are buried in the Reformed
Cemetery in Java.

        Jacob Geigle
Jacob Geigle was born Oct. 1886 to Johann Jacob and Katherine (Seiler) Geigle in
Sutley, 11 miles north of Java. He attended the Ackerman #46 School. His parents
retired in 1915. He took over the family farm and was active until ill health
forced his retirement in 1945.

(Photos:) Carolina Geigle and Jacob Geigle

In Nov. 1916, he married Carolina Lechner, daughter of pioneer Nickolas and
Barbara (Heupel) Lechner, born on the farm west of Leola. Her father and mother
came to the U.S. in 1885 from Kassel, South Russia. They came to McPherson
County in 1886 and retired from farming around 1910 to Eureka. Mrs. Geigle came
from a large family. Elizabeth (Karl) Hoffman, John and Fred Lechner, all of
Leola; Katharina Schoop of Plevna, MT; Barbara (Andrew) Bertsch of Eureka;
Magdalena (Jake) Rueb of Leola; Jacob of Missoula, MT; Christina (John) Oster of
Denver, CO; and Martha (Kaspar) Vetter of Yakima, WA.

In 1945, they moved to Java, where they lived in retirement for 11 years, when
death came to Jacob on May 1956. He was buried in the Java Congregational
Cemetery. Mrs. Geigle remarried in 1961 to Gottlieb Zeller, who passed away in
1965. Carrie, as known to her friends, passed away Aug. 1989 at the age of 93
years, and was laid to rest beside her husband Jake. The Geigles were charter
members of the Sutley Congregational Church and Carrie was a charter member of
the Sutley Ladies Aid. Mr. Geigle served on the school board for many years.

The Geigles had no children of their own. They raised a nephew, Henry Geigle,
who farmed near Selfridge, ND. They adopted a son, Herbert.

(Photo:) Herbert Geigle

Herbert Geigle was born Oct. 18, 1927 on a farm three miles east of Mound City.
He was raised on the Geigle homestead and attended Ackerman #36 School and
worshiped in Sutley Congregational Church. He attended Java High School,
graduating in 1945. He enlisted in the Navy in 1945 and was discharged in 1948.
In 1949, he entered USD at Vermillion and received a BA degree in History. In
1953, he was employed by the U.S. Government in Washington, DC, and spent two
years in Germany. In 1969, he was employed in Puerto Rico for 9 years, and then
worked for Shelley Manufacturing in Miami, FL. He is presently retired and lives
in Pompano Beach, FL. He is a 50-year member of the American Legion Post in Java
and an active member of the Germans From Russia Heritage Society of Bismarck,
ND.

        Tom and Shirley (Gill) Heis by Shirley Heis
My parents, Edward and Kathryn (Hochstetter) Gill were very much a part of early
Java. I really don't know when Gill Hardware began, but I do remember two
locations. The first one I recall was south of the present grocery store. From
that location, it moved to a building just north of the present grocery store,
which is vacant but still remaining. Both locations turned into Job Cafes.

I remember that Christ Schnaible worked for my dad, and my cousin, DeLoyd
Hochstetter, worked for him while he was going to high school. Later, Roger
Schnaible, a grandson of Christ, worked there. My dad sold the store to Ervin
Wolf in 1954 and continued to work for him until 1958.

My mother was the Chief Telephone Operator for Northwestern Bell Telephone
Company. She trained several of her nieces to work as relief operators. The
building, which housed the office, was located across the street from the old
Post Office. The girls she trained were Adeline (Lutz) Port, who lives in FL,
and Verna (Lutz) Kunz, who is no longer living. The other niece she trained was
Erna (Hochstetter) Werre, who lives in Aberdeen. The approximate years of this
were about 1930 to 1940. When my mother quit, Erna became the Chief Operator, in
about 1940, and she trained Pauline (Schlepp) Stotz to be her relief operator.
Erna went to Eureka when the Java office closed.

My father passed away in 1966, and my mother passed away in 1988.

Although it doesn't seem possible, it has been 45 years since I called Java
"home." After graduating from Java High School in 1954, I enrolled at NSTC, as
Northern was then known. After two years there, I taught third grade in Aberdeen
for two years. Summers were spent working on the completion of my degree. I then
took a year off and completed my degree in elementary education. I graduated
from NSU in 1959 and returned to the classroom, this time as a Special Ed.
teacher for one year, again in Aberdeen.

Tom and I were married in 1960, incidentally, the first wedding in the new St.
Paul Church. We lived near Frederick and, the first two years there, I taught
first grade. This was the beginning of the next 30 plus years in education in
the same school, which changed names three times. I was either the kindergarten,
first or second grade teacher. When I wasn't teaching part time or full time, I
subbed.

Our family includes a daughter, Kristi, who lives in Maryland with her husband,
Mel. Our son, Jason, and his wife live in Bennington, KS. Tom is the SD Manager
for Royal Neighbors of America Insurance. He has been in the insurance business
for 16 years. At the end of the 1999 school year, I decided to retire from
teaching and will devote my time to helping Tom and who knows what else. I am
sure I will be subbing!

After 45 years, I still enjoy coming to Java and reminiscing as we drive around
town. I would like to congratulate the hard working residents for their
dedicated work. If it weren't for the many hours of planning, this event would
not be possible to come "home" to, to enjoy. Thank You!

        Dale and Carol (Seuer) Gill

The Gimbel Family by O.E. Carlson
Heinrich Gimbel was born in Russia in 1829, of Russian parents. He and his wife
Karoline grew up when Alexander II was ruler of Russia. Under that ruling Russia
was continually at war; first toward the west and later with the Chinese to the
east. Heinrich and Karoline's eldest son Jacob spent four years in the Russian
military service. It was this type of constant wars and poverty that prompted
Heinrich and Karoline to migrate to the U.S. in 1879. They left their eldest
married daughter and their two sons, Jacob, then 28 years old, and Simon, who
was 10, in the homeland, to come later if it was better in the U.S.

(Photo:) Left to right on harvesting picture: Simon Gimbel, Sr. on header; hired
         hand, Ernest Gimbel, and Elizabeth Gimbel (Mrs. Hans Carlson)

They first worked in the east till early spring when they migrated to Yankton,
which was then the capitol of Dakota Territory. From there they came to
Richmond, Dakota Territory, which was later called Columbia. It was there they
met people by the name of Shandoers, and they all came as far west as where the
old original homestead began, one-and-a-half miles south of the old farmstead
now occupied by the great grandson, O.E. Carlson. Shandoers lived just one-
quarter mile east of the farmstead. It is here where Heinrich and Karoline
continued to live until 1892, when their two sons, Jacob and his family, and
Simon Gimbel, came to this country. Jacob filed on land in the Long Lake area,
and lived there until the 1900's when they went to Canada.

In 1893 Heinrich Gimbel purchased a claim shack and 40 acres of land from an
English man (Andrew Lootz), a young bachelor who was the original owner of the
old farmstead. It was here Simon started farming. He married Rosina Schanzenbach
in Eureka in 1894. The Schanzenbachs were prominent citizens of the Akaska and
Selby area.

In the spring of 1895 Granddad was going to take his wife to Akaska to her
parents, where their first child was to have been born; but alas, time ran short
at the Hoefs farm about seven miles west of the home place. It was there that
this writer's mother, Elizabeth, was born on Mar. 4, 1895. The Hoefs were
parents of May Hoefs, who had a clothing store for many years in Selby.

Heinrich Gimbel passed away at the age of 73 in Sept. 1902. At his dying
request, he was buried close to his home and later two of Simon's children,
Henry, age 1, Jan. 2, 1907 and Maggie, age 7, on Dec. 21, 1907, were also buried
beside their grandfather. It is the hope that this writer may also someday be
buried there.

In 1908, Karoline Gimbel moved to Java, and later when Java began a building
boom, Simon also moved to Java, where he did carpentry work.

To Simon Gimbel and his wife, seven children were born: Elizabeth, Ernest,
Maggie, Bertha, Henry, Theodore, and Simon.

This writer's father, Hans O. Carlson, who came to this country at 19 years of
age from Goteborg, Sweden, worked in Montevideo, MN for some years before coming
to Java, where he worked on the Milwaukee road until his marriage to Elizabeth
Gimbel. They then lived on the old original homestead. One son, O.E. Carlson,
was born to this marriage. Hans Carlson passed away in 1947 and this writer has
lived on the old homestead since.

O.E. Carlson married Dorothy Thomas in 1948, and to this marriage four children
were born. (See Family History)

In looking at old pictures etc., many names have changed in our area: Alfred
Hingcliff used to be Heinrich Gimbel's neighbor; O.D. Buchecker, the man who
wore a buffalo headdress; the Nobles, who had 50' wooden silos; Herman Wosnuk;
Wm. Payne; the Hagadus (there is still part of their storehouse left); all these
helped to build this community and all are gone - only memories are left.

        John Goetz Sr.
John Goetz, Sr. was born in Gluckstal, South Russia on Aug. 15, 1870. On Jan.
31, 1895, he was united in marriage with Christine Unruh. To this couple were
born 11 children.

In 1905, the John Goetz family undertook the long voyage to the U.S. They
settled at Hillsview and later homesteaded near Akaska. Some years later the
family moved to a farm near Java, where they resided until 1925, when they
bought a home in the city of Java. The family members were very active Lutheran
church members. In 1927 John's wife passed away. He ran the dray line for a few
years and on July 2, 1929, he married Mrs. Justine (Henke) Wolf, also of Java.

(Photo:) Mr. and Mrs. John Goetz, Sr.

The children of John and Christine were as follows: Jacob married Katherine
Henne. They had one son and two daughters; John, Jr. married Ida Naasz. They had
one daughter; Fred married Kathryn Eisenbeisz. They had one child; George was
killed in a car accident in 1949. He was married to Emma Schafer and they had
two sons and two daughters;  Lt. Col. Carl married Neva. They had three
daughters; Barbara married Henry Lutz. They had one daughter, Elaine, who
drowned in 1940. Barbara passed away in 1948; Rose married Gerhardt Schafer and
had one son; Frieda married Robert Haux; and Kathryn married Ralph Carroll.

        John and Ida (Naasz) Goetz Jr.
John Goetz, Jr., was born in Gluckstal, South Russia on Apr. 13, 1901. He came
to the U.S. with his parents when he was a little boy at the age of four years.
He lived on the farm near Java until he married Ida Naasz in June 1928, and
moved to a farm east of Java. They farmed for many years until he bought a home
in Java in 1940. He was employed by Biel's Red Owl of Java for many years and,
later, was a meat cutter for Hank's Red Owl in Selby until his retirement.

(Photo:) John and Ida Goetz, Jr.

John passed away in Nov. 1971. Ida Naasz Goetz passed away in Nov. 1992. They
had one daughter, Geraldine Goetz Schmidtgall Biel, who married Leonard
Schmidtgall. Leonard passed away in June 1979. Geraldine moved to Mobridge in
June 1983 and was a substitute teacher at Wakpala School for eight years. She
started to work with SD Green Thumb in Nov. 1987. She now covers six counties
and is a Field Operations Assistant. Geraldine has four living children. Georgia
Kallenberger Bacon lives in Gettysburg and works for Logan Electric. She has two
children: Bryan Kallenberger, a college student at Brookings, and Nicole
Kallenberger, a student at Gettysburg school. Jay Schmidtgall lives in Brooklyn
Center, MN and works for C.J. Duffey Paper Co. as an inside sales representative
in Minneapolis. Joy Scheldon lives in Colorado Springs, CO and works for
American Telecasting, Inc. She takes care of the payroll for many states. She
has one daughter, KyAnna, who is five. Sherri Ostman lives in St. Louis Park, MN
and works for T.C.F. as a Commercial Loan Coordinator.

        George and Emma (Schafer) Goetz
George Goetz was born in Gluckstal, South Russia, on Oct. 1, 1902. In 1905 he
came to this country with his parents, Mr. and Mrs. John Goetz, Sr., and three
brothers.

George Goetz grew to manhood in the area, living in Hillsview, Akaska, and Java,
and playing baseball with the Java team in the early 1920's. After a brief stint
in the Merchant Marine, George married Emma Schafer in 1928. Emma was born in
Java on Apr. 25, 1908, and graduated from Java High School in 1927. They had a
double wedding with George's younger sister, Rose, marrying Emma's older
brother, Gerhart, during the same service. The parents of Emma and Gerhart were
Mr. and Mrs. Jacob Schafer, local farmers who later lived in Java, where Mr.
Schafer was the school custodian.

(Photo:) Gerhart and Rose (Goetz) Schafer and George and Emma (Schafer) Goetz

George and Emma had four children and lived at various times on a ranch near
Gettysburg, and in Onida, Timber Lake, and Aberdeen, returning often to Java to
visit friends and relatives. Neither lived to see their children grow to
adulthood. Emma had contracted scarlet fever as a child, and later complications
slowly destroyed her kidneys. She died on Sept. 11, 1945, at age 37. After her
death, her children (Kenneth, 13; Carol, 7; Betty, not yet 5; and Gary, just
turned 3) came to Java to live with their grandparents, Mr. and Mrs. Schafer.
Two years later, Carol and Betty went to live with their aunt and uncle, Mr. and
Mrs. Ted Buechler (Ella Schafer) of Aberdeen. George Goetz, 46, died Aug. 6,
1949, in an automobile accident.

All four children eventually left the state. Kenneth, who graduated from Java
High School in 1950, earned both Ph.D. and M.D. degrees and spent most of his
professional life in Kansas City, first on the faculty of the University of
Kansas Medical Center, and later as Director of Research and Head of the
Division of Experimental Medicine at St. Luke's Hospital of Kansas City. After
taking early retirement from the hospital, he spent several years as a visiting
professor in German and Finnish universities. He lives in the Kansas City area.
He is married to the former Shirley Caldwell, and they have two adult children,
Gregory and Anne.

Carol married Dr. Ronald Burmeister in Madison, WI, and now lives in Rockford,
IL, where her husband serves as head of a hospital's fertility clinic and still
practices gynecology. Carol heads the Rockford area group, Vegetarians in
Motion. She and Ron have twin adult children, Jeff and Julie, who both live in
Atlanta.

Betty is now married to Don Strong and lives in the Phoenix area, where she
works as a receptionist for a high-tech firm. She has four adult children,
Tammy, Tim, Tory, and Shawn, by her two previous husbands.

Gary married Becki Cochenet of Sturgeon Bay, WI, and worked for many years as a
quality control engineer for Mercury Marine in Fond du Lac, WI, before being
transferred to the company's MercCruiser division in Stillwater, OK, where he is
employed as a process engineer. He and Becki have two adult children, Trisha and
Tracey.

        Gottlieb and Christina (Oster) Goetz
Gottlieb Goetz was born in Hoffnungstal, South Russia on July 2, 1864. When he
reached young manhood, he married Christina Oster, who was also born in the
Hoffnungstal area on Nov. 30, 1864.

They came to America with their two oldest children, Gottlieb and Charlie. In
1889 they undertook the long journey, arriving at Eureka. They remained there
temporarily until they were able to file a claim of land eight miles NE of Java,
which they homesteaded. Gottlieb and Christina raised their family of eight
children, who were Gottlieb, Charlie, John, Christ, Sam, Magdelina (Sam)
Schlepp, Fred, and Edward. Edward married Margaret Bratzel.

(Photo:) The Gottlieb Goetz Family

Gottlieb passed away July 11, 1911, at the age of 47. Christina continued to
live on the homestead until 1919, when she married Christian Pfitzer and moved
to Java, and her son Charlie took over farming the homestead until he retired to
Java. Christina passed away Mar. 3, 1943, at the age of 79.

Fred Goetz, son of Gottlieb and Christina, had Lavina, who graduated from Java
High School in 1942. She married David Wattier on Sept. 27, 1944. They took over
his family farm in Webster, where they continue to reside. They had four
children, Michael, Jane, Maria and Kathy. Lavina retired from a local department
store after 25 years of service.

(Photo:) LaVina (Goetz) Wattier and Family

        Charlie and Magdelena (Horst) Goetz
Charlie Goetz, son of Gottlieb and Christina (Oster), was born Feb. 25, 1889, in
Bessarabia, South Russia. He came to New York Harbor by boat with his parents
and older brother, Gottlieb. The family arrived in Eureka with the train, but
they remained there only for a short time. A land agent helped them seek land to
their satisfaction, as they wanted land with rocks on which to build a house.
They found the ideal location eight miles NE of Java. Charlie worked and went to
school in Adams Township in Walworth County, and was confirmed Mar. 27, 1904, by
Rev. Geo. Kirchdoerfer, in the Java Lutheran Church.

(Photo:) The Charlie and Magdalena Goetz Family

On Apr. 10, 1913, Charlie married Magdelena Horst, who was born Jan. 17, 1890,
at Bessarabia, South Russia, to Gottlieb and Margaretha (Hindemeth) Gohring, and
was later adopted by Leonard and Christina Horst. The Horst family came to
America in 1898 and homesteaded seven miles NE of Java. Magdelena was confirmed
by Rev. Geo. Kirchdoerfer and grew to womanhood around the Java area, before
marrying Charlie. After their marriage, Charlie and his bride moved to Crow
Rock, MT and lived there for five years before returning to SD. They lived on
his father's farm until 1942 when they bought a farm 10 miles NE of Java, which
later was owned by son Oscar Goetz. In 1947 they bought a home and moved to
Java.

Charlie passed away Nov. 2, 1957 at the age of 68, and Magdelena continued to
live in Java until her death on Oct. 19, 1965, at the age of 75.

The Charlie Goetz family had 9 children and 17 grandchildren. The children and
their families are as follows:

Maggie married Albert Kary and lived in Java for many years, later moving to
Groton to be near their daughter, Vera. Maggie died Mar. 1, 1994 and Albert died
Mar. 12, 1994. (See Family History)

Oscar married Stella Jurief and has four sons, Gaylon, Dwight, Keith, and
Gordon. He lived on the home farm 10 miles NE of Java for many years. Now he
lives with Dwight in Aberdeen. Stella died Mar. 8, 1992. (See Family History)

Edward, known as "Whitie," passed away on Jan. 21, 1969. He was a farmer in the
Java area.

Ferdinand married Mary (Lou) Aldrich and has two daughters, LaDonna and Barbara.
He retired from the Air Force in 1966 and worked for Braniff Airlines as a
management consultant until 1981. Now he is retired in Dallas, TX.

Harold married Irene Hirsch and has two sons, Jerry and Dale. Harold is a farmer
living near Java. Irene died June 15, 1987. (See Family History)

Howard lived in Java and worked in the Java and Bowdle areas. He died Aug. 26,
1979.

Irene married Theo Oster and has two daughters, Chloe and Pamela. She lives in
Aberdeen. Theo died Sept. 3, 1984.

Erna married Ted Schmierer and has two sons, Lonnie and Dean, and one daughter,
Kimberly. She lives in Aberdeen and operates a beauty salon. Ted died July 3,
1962.

Calvin married Sylvia Walker (divorced) and has three sons, Dave, Steve, and
Tyson. He worked for the Milwaukee Railroad in MT for many years. Now he is
married to Rita and they are retired in Lemmon.

        Oscar and Stella (Jurief) Goetz
Oscar Goetz, the son of Charlie and Magdelena Goetz, was born in Crow Creek, MT
on Oct. 1, 1915.

He grew up with his family eight miles NE of Java, in a sod house. There he
shared his labor and amusing events with his brothers and sisters, Edward,
Ferdinand, Harold, Howard, Calvin, Maggie, Irene, and Erna.

Oscar enjoyed visiting with his neighbors, attending community picnics, and barn
dances. It was at these barn dances where he met Stella Jurief, who was born in
Onaka, NE on Sept. 20, 1914 to Jacob and Emelia (Walter) Jurief. Together they
waltzed and later were married on Sept. 4, 1938, in the St. Paul Lutheran Church
in Java by Rev. G. Kirchdoerfer.

After their honeymoon, they settled down for a few months in Montana and later
returned to SD. They repeated this move to Montana and SD several times during
their early-married life.

Deciding to establish a more permanent home, Oscar and Stella settled in a sod
house on the Gottlieb Zimmerman farm site. Here was the beginning of their
family when their first child, Gaylon, was born on Sept. 10, 1943.

(Photo:) Gordon, Dwight, Oscar, Stella, Keith, and Gaylon Goetz

Shortly thereafter, another move was made to the Warner Straub farm. This family
kept growing when Dwight was born on Feb. 8, 1946, and later Keith joined the
family on Aug. 25, 1947.

In the fall of 1950 Oscar and Stella, with their three sons, moved to the home
place of Oscar's parents, when his parents retired to the town of Java. It
wasn't long before another son, Gordon, born Sept. 20, 1953, joined the family.
Here they continued to live, raising their sons and farming the land.

Oscar's life centered around the care and enjoyment of horses. He and Stella
enjoyed having friends and family visit to ride horses, especially the latest
favorite, Danny Boy.

One incident that brings back a special memory is the day Gebhardt Pfitzer and
Oscar decided to ride in the parade for Java's celebration. Just to be funny,
Gebhardt and Oscar dressed up as clowns. They climbed into a single-hitched
buggy, which was pulled by Pfitzer's mare, Major. The clowns would jump off and
clown around while the horse, Major, just followed them around.

It wasn't all work on the farm, the family remembers vacations, driving in their
"55 Dodge" over the mountains and through the desert to the West Coast. They
drove to OR to visit Stella's parents, sister Martha, and brother Hilbert.

The family expanded as Gaylon married Connie Buechler from Bowdle. They now live
on a farm NW of Bowdle and have two children, Selena and Jarrod.

Dwight married Betty Berreth from Herreid, who lived on the same farm site where
Oscar and Stella lived. They have two children, Angela and Steven. At the
present time they live in Aberdeen where Dwight is employed with Twin City Fans.

Keith married Mary Kraft from Aberdeen. They live with their family in Warner.
They have four children, Nicole and triplets Matthew, Crystal, and Michael.
Keith is employed with Liebelt Homes.

Gordon married Sharon Krause from Aberdeen. They have two sons, Justin and
Travis. Gordon works for Grote Sheetmetal.

Oscar and Stella continued to live on the farm until, after a lengthy illness,
Stella died on Mar. 8, 1992. Oscar continued to live in his home on the same
site as Dwight and Betty. In the summer of 1996, the family moved to Aberdeen.
Oscar continues to live with them and daily attends a special day care for the
elderly. Although he is happy with his new home, Oscar's heart is still with his
hometown community of Java.

        Harold Gottlieb Goetz
Harold Goetz was born July 29, 1922, to Charlie and Magdelena (Horst) Goetz, who
migrated from Bessarabia, South Russia. Charlie was the son of Gottlieb and

        Robert and Viola (Ritter) Goetz Sr.
Robert Bernard Goetz was born Oct. 3, 1916 in Walworth County to Christoph and
Emilia (Wolff) Goetz. His mother passed away when he was one-and-a-half years
old and his father married Katherine Schuh. He attended school in Selby.

He was in the Civilian Conservation Corps from 1935 to 1939, where he helped
reconstruct the facilities on Harney Peak, in the Black Hills. From 1941 to 1945
he served with the Army's Company C First Armored Division. While in the Army,
he spent three-and-a-half years overseas  in North Africa and Italy, during
World War II. He drove a half-track, delivering supplies to the front. He was
awarded the Bronze Star for heroism and achieved the rank of TEC5. After peace
was declared, he was honorably discharged at Ft. Snelling, MN.

On June 1, 1947, Robert married Viola Lydia Ritter in Mobridge. She was born
Apr. 21, 1926. For a short time he worked for the railroad, and for farmers in
the area, before operating his own threshing crew outfit. He served 21 years as
Chief of Police in Java, was responsible for city maintenance, drove a bus for
the Java school and, for many years, was Chief of the Java Volunteer Fire
Department. He was a charter member of the LaVerne Bauer Post, No. 275 of the
American Legion in Java.

Robert died Oct. 29, 1986. Robert and Viola had 10 children.

Dennis Robert was born Oct. 16, 1947 and died Oct. 17, 1947.

Dorothy Marie (May 3, 1949) married Roger Fryett on Aug. 14, 1976. They have
Meghan Lea, born Jan. 11, 1980.

Jennifer Lynn (Sept. 25, 1973) and Jeffrey Douglas (May 21, 1975).

Rebecca Marie (Dec. 5, 1976), Valerie (Apr. 4, 1979), and Michael Thomas (Sept.
26, 1980).

Marijane Frances (Sept. 9, 1954) married David Borresen on Apr 21, 1979. They
have Lindsey Marie (Nov. 2, 1981) and Alison (May 22, 1983).

Elizabeth Ann (Mar. 22, 1956) married Richard Wadhams on June 25, 1959. Their

        Raymond and Viola (Horst) Goetz

        Ignatz Hajson
Ignatz Hajson was a long-time resident of the county, who was employed on farms
near Java for many years and was well known in this part of the country. He came
to the U.S. about 1917. Before he passed away, he was living at the Eureka

Pfitzer home. He died May 27, 1952, and was buried at Mobridge. Pallbearers were

        The Peter Hartman Family
Peter Hartman and Theresa Fichters were united in marriage in 1864, in the
colony of Landau in South Russia. This union was blessed with 11 children, five
of whom preceded their parents in death, in Russia.

Peter and Theresa and six children left Landau, South Russia on Mar. 16, 1889,
by train on a four-day trip to board the ship named Ems, for New York, which
took 9 days. It took another four days from New York to Eureka by train. The
entire fare totaled $350.

They homesteaded in the Sutley area north of Java and suffered many of the
trials and tribulations of the early pioneers who settled the Dakota prairies. A
sod house and barn were built. While leading a bull to the water tank, Peter was
gored by the bull. Peter lingered three days before his death. This happened in
1900.

Son Florian Hartman was united in marriage to Karolina Stiegelmeier in 1891, and
they continued to live on the homestead after his father's death.

There were seven children born to this union.

In 1920 they retired from the farm and moved into Java. After Karolina's death,
and many years later when Florian was no longer able to care for himself, he
made his home with his son, Peter (Pete), on the old homestead, where he spent
his remaining days.

(Photo:) The Peter Hartman Family

Peter (Pete) Hartman was united in marriage to Louise Kruger on Jan. 23, 1920.
As a schoolgirl, Louise worked at a hotel in McClusky, ND and became an
excellent cook.

Three children were born to Pete and Louise, who were Verna, Leo, and Aaron.

Verna married Howard Kunz and they live in Red Wing, MN. They have two
daughters, Vickie and Marsha.

Dr. Leo Hartman married Donalee Gladden and they live in Bellflower, CA. They
have six sons: Danny, who died in infancy, Connley, Steve, Greg, Gary, and Jim.

Aaron married Twila Voegele and they had two children, Kay and Leslie. Later
Aaron and Florence adopted Michelle and Daaron.

Aaron continued to live and farm the home place after his parents retired into
Bowdle in 1955. Aaron and Darlene Kurle Job were married in Nov. 1986.

Pete Hartman and brother John were drafted into the service during World War I.
John died in the service during the flu epidemic in 1918.

Peter was with the 306th Infantry in France and was wounded in action, suffering
with shrapnel in his leg the rest of his life.

Peter was laid to rest June 13, 1976, and Louise in Feb. 1986.

Theresa Hartman, Java's oldest resident, died Nov. 2, 1946, just three months
from her 102nd birthday. Ending a century of eventful living, Theresa had seen a
great array of history in her 101-year lifespan. She was in Russia in the days
of the dictatorial power of the Czar, saw the villages in the fruitful valley in
South Russia, was on the slow ship passage to America, and experienced the long,
eventful years of building a farm home on virgin land.

Theresa was exceptionally spry at her advanced age until she fell, breaking her
hip. Pneumonia ended her life.

The generations of Hartmans were active members in the Seventh Day Adventist
Church, which was located in the Sutley area near the Jacob Oswald farm a few
miles north of the Hartman farm.

        Carl and Elizabeth (Steinbach) Hauck
Katherine, the wife of Henry Schneider, was the daughter of Carl Hauck, Jr., and
Elizabeth Steinbach, who were married at Berlin, South Russia, and came to
America with his folks, Carl Hauck, Sr., because of the strict laws there. They
settled on a farm at Scotland, SD, for a short time, then moved to a farm 12
miles NW of Java. A sod house was built on their farm and as a small girl,
Katherine helped make the many mud blocks it took to build it.

(Photo:) Carl and Elizabeth Hauck

        Henry and Nettie (Kunz) Hauck
Nettie and Henry were married Aug. 21, 1933 with $40 in their pockets and a $90
voucher gift from her parents - and no one would buy a voucher during the
Depression. Together they attended summer school sessions and workshops toward
their college degrees, which they finally acquired from Northern College in
Aberdeen.

After having taught and assisted in coaching in the Mobridge schools for 15
years, Henry died in 1964. Their daughter, Chloe, was a victim of the polio
epidemic and died in 1949, at the age of seven.

Nettie's 50-plus years of teaching experience included two decades as elementary
music teacher in the Mobridge schools, eight years in the Little Eagle Day
School, on the Standing Rock Reservation, and several years in the Oakes, ND and
Veblen, SD schools. Nettie was elected Little Eagle Day School Teacher of the
Year in 1979.

Henry was born Dec. 1, 1908, to Karl and Elizabeth Hauck at his parents' farm
north of Java. Nettie was born Sept. 10, 1908, to William and Katherine
(Hirning) Kunz, at her parents' farm NE of Java.

They both attended school in Java and graduated from high school there. Their
married life began in Timber Lake where Henry taught and coached athletics. From
there they taught in the Erwin, SD schools where Henry became ill due to a
collapsed lung, from which he never fully recovered.

In 1940 Henry filled an opening in the Java school as manager of the high school
boys' dormitory, then went into teaching and coaching there. Nettie taught in
the grades.

Teaching positions were accepted in the Mobridge public schools in 1948. Teacher
of the Year awards were presented to both Nettie and Henry. Aside from teaching,
they were involved in various community and church activities.

To upgrade her education and for the enjoyment of it, Nettie traveled to various
places, beginning with educational tours of this country, parts of Mexico and
Canada, Central Europe, South America, Russia, Israel and northern Egypt, and
the Bahamas.

William Charles followed in his parents' footsteps, acquiring a Doctorate in the
field of education. The four grandchildren live in various parts of the country.

Nettie celebrated her 90th birthday in Mobridge, where she had resided until her
death on Mar. 25, 1999.

        Jacob and Margaretha (Mauch) Haux
Jacob Haux, Sr. was born Oct. 4, 1874, at Koscharke, South Russia, and at the
age of 21 years, came to America with his parents, George and Katherina (Merkel)
Haux, Sr. The Haux family arrived in Dakota Territory and settled on a farm one
and one-half miles NW of Java, which they later claimed as their homestead.
Jacob helped his father with the farming for several years.

(Photo:) Jacob and Margaretha Haux, Sr.

On Oct. 30, 1906, Jacob married Margaretha Mauch who was born Oct. 28, 1884 on
the ship to America. Margaretha and her parents homesteaded in the Freeman, SD
area for a few years before coming to the Java vicinity. After Jacob and
Margaretha's marriage, the young couple made their home with Jacob's parents,
and took over the homestead after they passed away. Farming was their livelihood
and this couple, while raising their eight children, endured many hardships. The
Hauxs were devout church members of St. Paul Lutheran Church of Java. Many
services were rendered whenever possible and generosity endeavored the family to
make a donation of land to the Lutheran church for the purpose of a cemetery
plot, which is still in existence.

Jacob farmed with the help of his sons until his death in 1948. A year later,
his wife built a home and moved to Java, where she lived until 1972, when she
sold her home to Otto Mueller and moved to the Good Samaritan Center at Selby.

Five sons and three daughters were born to Jacob and Margaretha who were:

John, born Aug. 16, 1907, married Emily Wolff, and resides on a farm five-and-a-
half miles NW of Java. They have one son, Larry, who lives with John. Emily is a
resident at Good Samaritan Center in Selby.

Jacob, born Apr. 27, 1909, married Johanna Weber and had one son, Jerry. Jacob
passed away in 1946.

Lydia (Berthold) Schnaible was born Jan. 7, 1911. They had 3 sons and one
daughter. (See Family History)

David, born Dec. 30, 1912 married Frieda Christman. They had a son and a
daughter. Dennis married Judy Chris-tenson and Maxine married Earl Frank. (See
Family History)

Otto, born Apr. 10, 1915, married Alvina Wolff.

Albert, born Apr. 1, 1911, married Jean Miller. Albert passed away in 1968 and
his wife resides at Reno, NV.

Minnie (Erhard) Beitelspacher was born Nov. 6, 1919 and resides on a farm 13
miles SE of Java. They had two daughters and one son. Lonita married Carmen
Kilber, Cynthia married Lyle Schock and lives near Bowdle, and LeRoy married
Carla Kilber.

Irene, born Dec. 6, 1921, graduated from the Java school and passed away in
1940.

        Frieda S. Haux

        George and Elizabeth (Merkel) Haux Sr.
George Haux, Sr., was the youngest of four sons born to Johonas Haux, who lived
in Russia near Odessa. Elizabeth was the daughter of George and Magdaline
Merkel, who also lived near Odessa Russia. George Haux, Sr., was born in Neu-
Gluckstal, Russia and migrated to the U.S. in 1889 on a ship named the F.
Messler, which sailed from Port Bremerhaven, Germany. They arrived in New York
and then traveled by train to Bowdle. With George and Elizabeth came four of
their children, Jacob, Katherine, Caroline, and Christian. Their eldest son,
George Jr., had migrated with his wife and family to the U.S. in 1893.

(Photo:) George and Elizabeth Haux, Sr.

George Haux, Sr., bought the Heerwald farm NW of Java. The purchase of the farm
included all the livestock, and with the help of his family, he farmed for many
years. George, a charter member of the Java Lutheran Church, donated the land
for the Java Lutheran Church Cemetery.

Some members of Elizabeth's family came to the U.S. One brother, Jacob, farmed
near Eureka and later moved west of the Missouri River, where he farmed.

George Haux, Sr., lived his last years with his daughter, Katherine (Gottlieb)
Bamesberger.

        George and Katherine (Jesser) Haux Jr.
George Haux, Jr., the son of George Haux, Sr., and Elizabeth Merkel, was born in
1864 and died in 1933. He married Katherine Jesser, who was born in 1865 and
died in 1925. They were both born in Russia and got married in Russia. They
immigrated to America in 1893 with their family of four: John, Rudolph, Jacob
and Katie, six weeks old. Four children were born in America: Henry, William,
Minnie and Lydia.

(Photos:) George Haux, Jr. and Katherine Haux

They homesteaded about five miles NW of Java moving a few years later to a farm
four miles NW of Java, one mile south of the homestead. They retired from active
farming in 1918 and moved to Java, where they remained for the rest of their
lives. After they retired, George did carpentry and cement work.

        Jacob J. and Ida (Hetterle) Haux
Jacob J. Haux was born in Neu-Gluckstal, Russia on Jan. 11, 1890. At the age of
three, he came to America with his parents, George and Katherine Haux, his
brothers, John and Rudolph, and sister, Katie. Two sisters, Minnie and Lydia and
brothers, William and Henry, were born in America.

His parents homesteaded four miles NW of Java, and there he helped with the
farming and also attended school, finishing the fourth grade.

(Photo:) Jacob J. and Ida Haux

In the summer of 1908, he worked for George Bender on the threshing machine.
Later he worked as a hired hand on a farm in Linton, N.D. In the fall of 1910,
he went to work on a farm two-and-a-half miles NW of Java as a hired hand for
his uncle Jacob Haux, Sr. In 1911 he worked as a hired hand for Mr. Jackson. In
1912 he went to Martin, ND, and worked on the threshing machine. In 1913 he
started farming for himself, six miles NE of Selby.

On Dec. 19, 1915, he was united in marriage to Ida Hetterle. Ida was born on May
16, 1895, to Emanuel and Christina Hetterle, on a farm five miles NE of Selby.
The family consisted of two boys and two girls. Ida, as a young girl, had to
help with the fieldwork and many were the days she had to walk behind the plows.

Jacob and Ida spent their married life on the farm until they retired and moved
into Java. They farmed two years on a farm six miles NE of Selby, then they
moved to another farm four miles north of Selby. In 1918 they moved onto Jacob's
parents' homestead and later bought it.

The Jacob Hauxs had a family of three children: Oscar, born Nov. 9, 1919,
married JoAnne Scriptnor, had two children, Danny, and Sandra. Helen was born
Aug. 30, 1924, and married Harold Pfitzer, who is deceased. They had three sons,
Rodney, born Dec. 7, 1942; Charles, born Oct. 6, 1946; and Randy, born Dec. 15,
1953. Frances was born Dec. 10, 1929, married Clifford Silveson and had five
children, Clifford Jr., Callie, Reed, Jan and Cody.

In 1944, Jacob and Ida purchased a home at Java.

        Henry and Emma (Pleinis) Haux
Henry Haux was born on a farm four and one-half miles NW of Java on Apr. 23,
1895, to Georg, Jr. and Katherine (Jesser) Haux.

He spent his life on his parents' farm and was employed for a short time at the
Equity elevator in Java under William Kunz as manager. On July 23, 1918 he was
inducted into the Army at Camp Dodge Iowa and served until Dec. 6, 1918, when he
received his honorable discharge, and then returned to his parents' farm.

In 1919, he bought a farm seven and one-half miles NW of Java. On Apr. 13, 1919,
he married Emma (Pleinis) Haux, the daughter of Jacob and Magdalina
(Landenberger) Pleinis. They made their home on his farm until Dec. 5, 1951,
when they moved into their home in Selby.

He was a member of the American Legion. On May 8, 1953, he passed away after
suffering a stroke.

Emma continued to live in Selby and enjoyed gardening and making patchwork
quilts. She passed away Oct. 1982.

They had six children: Ervin, of Selby; Esther (Haux) Haux of Java, deceased
Feb. 24, 1980; Virginia (Haux) Voeller of Bowdle, deceased June 1992; Leona
(Haux) Huft of Roscoe; Elmer of Shaun-avon, Sask., Canada; and Estella (Haux)
Bust of Flushing, NY.

They have 16 grandchildren, 26 great-grandchildren, and 5 great-great-
grandchildren.

        Christian and Katharina (Krause) Haux
Christian Haux was born Dec. 11, 1888 in New Gluckstal, South Russia, near the
city of Odessa. He was the youngest son of George and Elizabeth Haux, Sr., and
migrated to the U.S. in 1899 with his parents, when he was 11 years of age.

His parents, brother Jacob, and sisters Katherine and Caroline, took port at
Bremerhaven, Germany, and landed in New York. One married brother, George, Jr.,
had migrated with his wife and family in 1893. From New York they came to
Bowdle. His father, George Haux, Sr., purchased the Heerwald farm NW of Java.
Christian farmed with his parents, went to school to learn the English language,
read and write. He was also confirmed in the First Lutheran Church near Java.

(Photo:) Christian M. and Katharina Haux

On Oct. 29, 1912, he married Katharina Krause, the daughter of Johanas and
Louise Krause, who had homesteaded in Walworth County, where Katharina was born
on Apr. 10, 1890.

In 1913, they built a farm two miles NW of Java. Gottlieb Bamesberger, who was
married to Christian's sister Katherine, built the farm. Mr. Bamesberger was a
carpenter by trade.

Christian was fond of horses and farmed with horses until the drought years in
the early Thirties, when tractors were put into use.

He was active in community affairs, was a member of rural school boards for many
years. He was a member of the Board of Directors of the Java Equity Exchange. He
was active in the Lutheran church, and was treasurer at the time of his death on
June 30, 1942.

His wife Katharina continued to live on the farm until 1945, when she retired.
She lived with her father Johanas Krause until 1949, when she built her own
home. Katharina passed away Apr. 10, 1968.

Christian and Katharina (Krause) Haux of Java had six children. Robert of
Salmon, ID, deceased Apr. 18, 1998; Wilson, deceased 1934; Herman of Mobridge,
deceased 1998; Herbert deceased June 9, 1991; Evelyn (Haux) Johnle of Aberdeen;
and Bertha (Haux) Kasper of Whitefish, MT.

They have 9 grandchildren, 12 great-grandchildren, and two great-great-
grandchildren.

        Herbert J. Haux
Herbert J. Haux, born June 23, 1917, son of Christian and Katharina (Krause)
Haux. He married Esther V. Haux, daughter of Henry and Emma (Pleinis) Haux, on
Nov. 23, 1944.

They purchased the homestead, one mile north and one-half mile west of the Java
Lutheran Cemetery, in 1945 and farmed there for 35 years.

Esther, born Apr. 19, 1924, passed away Feb. 24, 1980, of cancer. Esther was a
housewife and helped Herbert farm. She was a member of the Lutheran Ladies Aid
and taught Sunday School.

To their union one child, Mercedes (Haux) Schilling was born July 23, 1950. She
married Bill Schilling Apr. 18, 1970. After Herbert and Esther's deaths,
Mercedes and her children, Shawn Wilson and Malinda Schilling, inherited the
homestead. They lease it out. They continue to live in Billings, MT and visit
when they can. Mercedes and Bill have one grandson, Tanner.

Herbert married Susanna (Wolf) Spiry on Nov. 28, 1980, and they continued to
live on the homestead until Herbert's death on June 9, 1991.

Herbert drove school bus for the Java school for 13 and one-half years, served
on the Equity board, school board, and St. Paul Lutheran Church Council and as
treasurer for many years.

He was awarded a plaque for farming for 50 years. When his health started to
fail, he and Susie traveled to AZ and later had a home in TX where they spent
the winters.

Susie passed away in Apr. 1993. They had 10 grandchildren and four great-
grandchildren.

        Ludwig and Margret (Hieb) Helm Sr.
Ludwig Helm, Sr. was born in 1863 and came to America in 1889, from Neudorf,
Russia. He died in 1940. He married Margret Hieb in 1886 at Neudorf. She was
born in 1863 and died in 1922.

They homesteaded six miles north of Java. In 1907, he bought a farm, which was
formerly known as the Rosella trading post, post office and store. He retired to
Java in a home he built on Helm Street.

Their children were:

Ludwig Jr., born 1887 in Neudorf, Russia, married Katie Hemrich in 1913, birth
unknown. Children: one baby died in infancy. Ludwig Jr. died in 1961.

(Photo:) Ludwig Helm Sr. Family. Mr. Helm, Ludwig, Jr., Christine, Caroline,
         Mrs. Helm, Christ, in front, wearing a "Vote for McKinley" button

Christina, married Jake Henne; Henry and Harry.

Christine, born 1891, married John L. Naasz, 1909. John Naasz died 1947.

Christ L., born 1893, married Rosie Lutz in 1913. Rosie Lutz was born 1893, died

        Christ L. and Rosie (Lutz) Helm
Christ L. Helm was born six miles north of Java, in Walworth County in 1893. He
married Rosie Lutz in 1913. She was born in 1893 and died in 1972. They were
married in the Peace Lutheran Church north of Java. He farmed in partnership
with his father, Ludwig Helm Sr., and in 1918, bought the farm from his father.
The farm site was known as Rosella, trading post, post office and store before
it was sold to Ludwig Helm in 1907.

In 1920, they moved to Java and bought a share in the Java Oil Co. In 1923, he
moved back to the farm.

(Photo:) Christ L. Helm Family. Ervin, Christ, Arthur, Violet, Mrs. Helm, Inez

In 1936, he moved to Java and oldest son, Arthur, took over the farm. In 1945,
he bought the Selby Livestock Sale Barn. In 1947, he moved to the new home he
built in Selby. In 1951, he sold the sale barn and bought a plot of land on the
east edge of Selby. Part of this plot was turned into a trailer court and part a
livestock yard, where he was a buyer for Armour Packing Co.

Christ and Rosie had five children.

Arthur, born 1914, married Frieda Sieler in 1935. (See Family History)

Ervin C. Helm, born 1919, married Elma Berreth in 1945. Children: Nel, born in
1948 and Dean, born in 1951.

Inez, born 1921, married Frank Huppert in 1941. Children: Ione, born in 1942
married John Hartman.

Violet, born 1925, married Edward L. Morris in 1941. Children: Paul, born 1946,
married Mary Victoria Roman in 1971.

Larry, born 1938, lives in Chamberlain.

        Arthur H. and Frieda (Sieler) Helm
Art was born July 12, 1914, to Christ and Rosie (Lutz) Helm on a farm eight
miles north of Java. His parents moved to Java in 1919. Art started school in
Java in a little schoolhouse where only 1st and 2nd grades were held. Art
started the 2nd grade in the new school that was built in 1921. This was in the
area where the Russell Bender and Lila Bieber homes presently are. In 1923, Art
moved back to the farm with his parents. He finished his eight grades in Holmes
Country School in the Highland District.

After graduating he continued to farm on the family farm with his father.

On Nov. 28, 1935, he married Frieda Sieler in a little country church north of
Java, called Peace Congregation. His parents were married in this same church.

Art and Frieda had four children.

Janice was born in 1936. She married Morris Kosters on Aug. 4, 1956. They have
four children, Frank, Curtis, Kelly, and Jane. Morris is a mechanic in Rapid
City.

Ruby was born in 1938. She married Hank Kosters in 1957. They have six girls,
Deborah, Daria, Donna, Dianna, Dawn, and Denise. Hank is employed with the Board
of Education in Pierre.

Dwight was born in 1952. He married Yvonne Mitchell in CA in June 1973. (See
Family History)

Leslie was born in 1956. He married Connie Weisz in 1975. They have three
children, Jason, Matthew and Melissa. They live in Redfield, where Leslie is
County Sheriff.

Art and Frieda moved to Java in 1988. Art continues to go to the farm each day
to help Dwight. A lot of changes have come about in his years of farming. Art
farmed with horses for many years and did a lot of hay stacking with a
pitchfork.

Before Java became a town, the family farm was a post office and a trading post
known as Rosella.

        Dwight and Yvonne (Barajas) Helm
Dwight Ervin Helm was born June 13, 1952, to Art and Frieda Helm, in Mobridge.

        Laurence and LaVerne (Hieb) Hettich
Laurence A. Hettich was born Oct. 4, 1925 SE of Roscoe to Fred and Roselia
(Kahler) Hettich. He attended school in Montpelier Township.

(Photo:) LaVerne and laurence Hettich

During World War II Laurence served in the Navy aboard the U.S.S. Chester CA27,
in the South Pacific and China Seas. After being discharged he attended Barber
College in San Francisco, CA and was employed at the Hartzell Barber Shop in
Ipswich. In 1948 he purchased the barbershop in Roscoe from Walt Penor. Later
that year, he built a new barber and beauty shop north of the post office.

Laurence married LaVerne H. Hieb on Oct. 2, 1949, at Roscoe. LaVerne H. Hieb was
born Dec. 2, 1929, at Bowdle to Fred J. and Christina P. (Werre) Hieb. She was
educated in the Hosmer area and attended the New York Hairdressing Academy
School of Cosmetology at Fargo, ND. She was employed at beauty shops in Milnor
and Casselton, ND, and at Armour and Company at West Fargo, ND, in the cashier's
office. In 1949 she purchased the beauty shop owned by Mrs. LeRoy (Linda Hieb)
Bieber. After their marriage, the Hettichs operated both businesses in their new
building.

In 1953 they moved to a dairy farm 10 miles north of Bowdle, where they now live
and are engaged in a grain and stock operation. Laurence and LaVerne have three
children.

LaDean, Class of 1969, Java High School,  grew up on a farm 11 miles east of
Java. He has two younger sisters LaNette Schlepp (1970 JHS graduate) and LaVon
Poyner (1977 JHS graduate). The first three years of his education were spent in
a rural school taught by Mrs. Frieda Schuh. He finished grades 4-12 in Java,
graduating in the spring of 1969. While in high school he was active in band,
football, track, and basketball and played American Legion baseball during the
summer months. Besides getting off to a great educational start with Mrs. Schuh
as his teacher, he enjoyed Mr. Ketterling's math classes and Mr. Besonen's
geography and social science classes. He attributes his strong interest in
basketball and baseball to his coaches Mr. Besonen and the late Mr. Floyd Biel.
After graduation, he attended NSU in Aberdeen, obtaining a BS in elementary
education with a minor in physical education.

(Photo:) LaDean and Joan Hettich

The first seven years of his teaching career were spent in the Bowdle Public
School system as a 6th grade and junior high departmentalized instructor. The
next seven years were spent in the Rosholt Public School system all in grades
6-7-8. His extra-curricular coaching was varsity girls' basketball. While in
Rosholt, he guided the Rams to two state tournament berths and regional
appearances in all seven years he coached there.

It was at Rosholt that he met his wife, Joan, who was teaching kindergarten in
the same system. They were married on Nov. 25, 1988, in Rosholt. Joan, who has
11 brothers and sisters, grew up on a farm NE of Wilton, ND. She is a 1978
graduate of Washburn High School. She received her teaching degree from NDSU and
Moorhead State University with a double major in Child Development and
Elementary Education in 1982. Her first assignment was a kindergarten position
beginning the second semester in Faith, SD.

The next teaching assignments for both were in the Glenburn, ND School System
for five years. Joan taught a combination 1st and 2nd grade for the first three
years and a self-contained 1st grade room for the last two years during the
stay. LaDean, who obtained his master's degree in Elementary Administration from
NSU during two summers while employed at Glenburn, was elementary principal and
taught departmentalized math classes for all five years. He also coached varsity
girls' basketball for two seasons and grade school boys and girls basketball for
three years.

The couple moved to Eureka in 1992. LaDean was elementary principal and varsity
girls' basketball coach for three years while teaching departmentalized math in
elementary and junior high. While employed at Eureka, LaDean reached the
milestone of 200 varsity girls' basketball wins in his career. Joan taught  the
basic skills program for four years.

Currently, the Hettichs live in Gwinner, ND. LaDean has been employed at the
North Sargent Public School as an elementary principal and middle school
departmentalized math for the past three years. This past year, he returned to
coaching girls' basketball. Joan has been employed during the same time at the
Milnor Public School as a kindergarten teacher.

LaDean's interests include returning all summers to work on the farm raising
limousin cattle, snow skiing, pheasant hunting with their dog, Stetson, and
following the Baltimore Orioles baseball team. Joan enjoys gardening, reading,
baking, cross-stitching, exercising and snow skiing.

LaNette, a 1970 graduate of Java High School, married Doug Schlepp, son of Elmer
and Erna Schlepp. (See Family History)

LaVon, the youngest child, attended grade and high school at Java, graduating
from Java High School in 1977. After graduation she attended school at USD,

were married May 23, 1987, one week after LaVon graduated from veterinary

(Photo:) LaVon, Russ, Lura, and Adam Poyner

They moved to Madison, WI in Aug. 1987, where Russ attended school at the

at small animal and mixed animal practices in Oconomowoc, WI, Portage, WI and

Russ obtained his Ph.D. in Dec. 1993 and continues to work at the University of
