        W.C. and Emily Hicks
W.C. Hicks came to Java from Treherne, Manitoba, Canada in 1904 to take over the
management of the First State Bank, which had been established by his brother E.
Hicks in connection with the First National Bank of Aberdeen.

The Hicks family, consisting of Mrs. Emily Hicks, sons George Wilson and Charles
Lewis and daughter Ethel, joined him some months later.

Mr. Hicks was president of the bank until his death in 1930. The rest of the
family is now also deceased: Ethel (J.K.) McGuire in Toronto, Canada in 1924;
George in Armour in 1973; and Lewis in 1965. Mrs. Hicks died in 1965. Mrs. Emily
Hicks brought up Ethel's daughter, Emma Ethel McGuire, in Java.

Christian and Katherina (Buechler) Himmerich

Christian Himmerich was born in the South Russian area and was married to
Katherina Buechler in 1870. Ten years later Christian and Katherina Himmerich
and family came to the U.S. In 1880, they arrived near the Java area and
homesteaded about 9 miles east of Java. In 1888, they moved three miles from the
homestead and built a farm. Much time was spent in raising cattle and grain so
they could have enough money to build some more to improve the farm.

(Photo:) Christian and Katherina Himmerich

In 1901, when Java had begun to grow as a town, Christian moved his family to
Java and got into business in partnership with Christian Wolff, which they
called the Mercantile and Grocery Store, which he operated until his death. The
Himmerich family had four children: Rosie, married Ted Kundert; Jacob, married
Kathrine Buechler; Maggie, married Henry Vaagen; and Kate, married Bert Jones.
All the Himmerich children are deceased.

        Jacob and Katherine (Buechler) Himmerich
Jacob Himmerich married Katherine Buechler on Nov. 9, 1909, at the Buechler
Church, which was located east of Java. The Himmerichs moved on his father's
farm six miles east of Java, and farmed for many years through the trying years
of drought, storms and grasshopper plague, trying to make a living for their
family. Jacob was active on the Spring Lake School board and also served on the
Telephone Co.

(Photo:) Jacob and Katherine Himmerich

The Himmerichs had five children, who were: Frieda married Edwin Oster and had 4
children; Elsie married Alvin Naasz and they had one son and one daughter;
Arthur married Lydia Oster; Violet married Otto Bauer and they had six children;
and Gertrude married Alan Oster and had three children.

In 1942 the Himmerichs bought a house in Java. Jacob passed away in 1969.

        John and Christina (Weiport) Hindemith
John Hindemith, born Mar. 19,1850, in Hoffnungstal, Russia, married Christina
Weiport of Gluckstal, South Russia. They were married in 1877 in the
Hoffnungstal area. In 1889, the John Hindemith family immigrated to the U.S. and
settled in the Java area, later homesteading four miles NE of Java. The first
schoolhouse in that area was called the Hindemith School until 1918, when they
changed it to the Norbeck School. Prior to the building of the schoolhouse, the
pupils had been taught by a Mr. Taylor in the Hindemith home. The first Lutheran
church was also built on the Hindemith homestead but later, fire over swept the
church and only a cemetery remained.

(Photo:) John Hindemith Family

John and Christina had 18 children.

        Simon Hirsch
Simon Hirsch, son of Anton and Elizabeth (Klein) Hirsch, was born on Dec. 20,
1856, in Friedenstal, South Russia. In 1878, Simon married Carolina Faul of
Friedenstal, South Russia. Two children were born and died in infancy. Carolina
Faul Hirsch died in 1881, and a year later, Simon was remarried to Elizabeth
Friemark, who also came from the Friedenstal area.

In the summer of 1884, Simon, his wife and two children, along with several
more immigrants, sailed to America. They arrived at New York City and then
traveled by train to  Dakota Territory. They came to Tripp, where they remained
with friends and relatives for some time before moving northward, where more
land was available.

The Simon Hirsch family arrived in the Sutley area near Campbell County, and
stayed with the Gottlieb Knodel family. A wagon box was turned upside down and
used as sleeping quarters until their sod house was built on the homestead.
Farming was done by hand-plowing and hand-seeding and supplies were gotten in
the fall of the year. Their main diet was food made from flour, meat, fruit, and
dried beans, which they raised themselves.

(Photo:) Mr. and Mrs. Simon Hirsch

In 1894 sorrow again struck this family when Elizabeth Friemark Hirsch passed
away, leaving Simon with six children to take care of. On Nov. 16, 1894, Simon
married Julianna (Mohr) Rieger, who lived in the Hosmer area and was born in
Bender, South Russia. Julianna's parents, Christoph and Willhelmina (Weigart)
Mohr, and brothers had been living in this territory before. Julianna, her
husband, John Rieger, married in 1878, and a family of seven children living in
Kassel, South Russia, came to America. Five children were born to Simon and
Julianna, which made a combined family of 18 children.

The children attended the Buckenberger School in the Thompson District. School
was held in six-month sessions.

Winters were very severe. In Dec. 1888, a strong three-day blizzard took place,
where many lives and livestock were lost. They also endured several years of
drought and experienced an Indian scare.

In 1919, Simon and his wife and three daughters moved to Eureka, but remained
there a short time and returned to the farm until 1920, when they moved to Java.
In 1941, they purchased the Henry Giese home and lived there until 1947, when
they moved in with their son Edward and wife, as their health was failing. Mrs.
Hirsch passed away in Aug. 1947, and Mr. Hirsch passed away in Feb. 1948.

The children of Simon and Elizabeth were: John, Karl, Jacob, Magdalina (John)
Fischer, Freidaricka (Mike) Kallas, and Mrs. Elizabeth Ritz. Children of
Julianna and John Rieger were: Eva (William) Kramlich, Philip Rieger, John
Rieger, Adolph Rieger, Whilhelmina (Andrew) Heining, Julia (Christian) Heinle,
and Maria (Otto) Kundert. The children of Simon and Julianna were: Gustav, Ida
(Christ L.) Lutz, Martha (Gust A.) Rau, Emma (Henry) Grenz, and Edward.

        Edward and Mary (Seif) Hirsch
Edward Hirsch, the second son of Simon and Julianna (Mohr) Hirsch, was born Oct.
6, 1897, at home in the Sutley community. Edward and his brother Gustav helped
their father with the farming until he retired, because their older brothers and
sisters were hired out, got married and moved to other areas.

Edward married Mary Seif, born Apr. 7, 1897 in OH, to Daniel and Katharina
(Bauman) Seif. She came to this area with her parents when she was 18 months
old. Edward and Mary were married on Oct. 19, 1920 by Rev. Klein of the Baptist
Church. The young couple lived with his brother, Gustav, on the Hirsch
homestead. In the spring of the year, the young couple bought a house and barn
and moved it a short distance from the homestead. Here they lived, farmed and
raised a family through drought and many bountiful years.

The Ed and Gustav Hirsch families worked together with the harvesting and
haying. They also got together at butchering time when meat was cured and
canned.

In 1928, they had the misfortune of losing their barn and some livestock in a
fire, but soon, with help from the neighbors, another barn was built and an
addition was built onto their previous house. They got their first radio and
telephone in the early 30's, got a wind charger and then installed an electric
six-volt system. The Hirsch family endured drought, dust storms, and a
grasshopper plague.

Edward did several different things during his lifetime. He was a County
Assessor for several years. He was also an auctioneer and shareholder of several
livestock sales barns. In his younger years, he had great interest in baseball
and in his retired years, he enjoyed hunting and fishing.

Early in the winter of 1939, the family moved in with his parents, but remained
a short time and returned to the farm, where they remained until 1941, when they
purchased a home from his parents.

(Photo:) Ed Hirsch Family: Standing: Irene, Glenn, Victor, Marion. Seated: Mr.
         and Mrs. Ed Hirsch

Four children were born: Glenn married Olga Buechler in 1948 and resided on the
home place. They had one son, Roger, who married Linda Kosters; Victor married
Allegra Biel in 1950; Irene married Harold Goetz in 1947 (See Family History);
and Marion, who was married to Harold Mueller in 1947, passed away in 1948 after
an automobile accident.

Edward passed away in Nov. 1964 and his wife Mary was living alone until 1974,
when she entered the Good Samaritan Nursing Home at Selby.

        Roger and Linda (Kosters) Hirsch

        Victor and Allegra (Biel) Hirsch
Victor Hirsch was born to Edward and Mary Hirsch on Feb. 21, 1926, on their farm
north of Java. He grew up on the farm with two sisters, Irene Goetz and Marion

(Photo:) Victor and Allegra Hirsch

        John and Katherine (Biel) Hochstatter
Johannes Hochstatter was born 8 Jan 1867 in Neusatz, South Russia, and Katherine
Biel was born 2 Jun 1867 in Colony Annental, South Russia. They married 14 Feb
1889 and departed Russia soon after, arriving in New York in Apr. They traveled
by train to Dakota Territory and Johannes signed an intent to become a U.S.
citizen on 6 July 1889, in the State of SD Circuit Court of Walworth County.
They homesteaded five miles NE of Java and lived under a header box until their
sod house was built with the aid of neighbors and friends. They farmed with oxen
and later, horses. They seeded grain by hand and harvested it with a sickle.
They had 9 children. John A., Sophia (Wells) Tyler, Fred (died young), Barbara,
Fred J., Katherine (Bill) Thurn, Christian, Magdelina (died young), and Lena
(John) Schlepp.

John A. was born Dec. 19, 1889. (See Family History)

Sophia married Wels Tyler and lived in Tacoma, WA. They had one son, Bruce. They
are all deceased.

Fredrick was born and died in 1893.

Barbara married Oscar Mortenson and lived in Tacoma, WA. They had no children.
Both are deceased.

Fredrich J. married Lydia Bauer. They had two sons, Irwin (died at 9 months) and
Vernon M., who married Esther Miller. (See Family History).

Katherine married William Thurn. They farmed five miles SW of Bowdle and had
four children. Violet was in the Air Force during WW II. She married Warren
Cowden. They live in Gardena, CA and have one daughter, Kim. Lillian married Leo
Riede and they live in CA. They have two sons: Jim, who is a Lutheran minister
in CA, and Robert. Donald, a teacher in Fairfield College in CA, married
Darlene. They had four daughters. Donald is deceased. Betty married George Nies,
son of Peter and Ethel (Ryan) Nies. They live in Palm Springs, CA. George was a
math professor at San Diego and owned a Real Estate business. They have two
sons, William and Peter (Tom), and one daughter, Peggy.

Christ married Rose Spiry. (See Family History)

Magdelina was the eighth child born to John and Katherine. She died as an
infant.

The ninth child, Magdalena (Lena), was born in 1903. She married John Schlepp.
They had five children. Lillian married Elsworth Randal. They lived in Selby and
had three children. Lillian is deceased. Delores married Alvin Bauer. They

        Rev. John A. and Lydia (Sayler) Hochstatter
John A. Hochstatter, the oldest child of Johannes and Katherine (Biel)
Hochstatter, was one of the first students to receive a high school education.
He attended Redfield High School, traveling by train and returning home on
weekends. He enrolled in Redfield College as a business student, but graduated
in 1912 with expectations of studying for the Christian ministry. In the fall of
1912, he entered Yankton College to begin work on a master's degree, which was
granted in the summer of 1913.

(Photo:) Rev. John A. and Lydia Hochstatter

Rev. Hochstatter worked his way through college as a postal employee and later,
as a student minister. While attending Yankton College he was licensed by the SD
Congregational Conference, enabling him to serve as a student pastor in the
Congregational Church in Lesterville.

While serving in this capacity, he met Lydia Sayler, who was superintendent of
the church Sunday school, and the church organist. They were united in marriage
in Lesterville on Aug. 25, 1913.

He then entered Chicago Theological Seminary and received his Bachelor of
Divinity degree in 1916. During this time, Mrs. Hochstatter attended the
Congregational Training School for Women. The Reverend Hochstatter carried a
heavy academic schedule and also served as a student minister, and a summer
vacation minister. Prompted by an enthusiastic desire to be adequately trained,
he studied Greek, Latin, Hebrew, German, and English in addition to his
theological courses. He graduated with honors and could claim Bachelor of Arts,
Master of Arts, and Bachelor of Divinity degrees.

Rev. Hochstatter served German Congregational churches in Plevna and Jordan, MT
until 1919. Their two children, Jonathan H. and Salome (Sally) Ruth Hochstatter
were born in 1917 and 1920 in Garfield County, MT. The couple homesteaded 160
acres eight miles east of Jordan and erected a sod house. It was in this house
that Salome Ruth was born, attended by a three-year-old brother, while the
father rode a horse to Jordan for a doctor.

The family moved from Jordan, MT to Hilda, Alberta, Canada in 1921, where Rev.
Hochstatter served as a public school principal and as a minister. From 1925 to
1930 he was the pastor of churches in Wapato and Qunicy, WA. His last official
charge was in Loveland, CO.

In 1942 he moved to Boulder, CO, where he was an active member of the First
Congregational Church and served several years as secretary of the Boulder
Workshop. He was employed in Boulder by the Rocky Mountain News and rented out
rooms in their large home.

Rev. Hochstatter died on Jan. 12, 1965 and his widow died on Sept. 27, 1968.
Both are buried in Mountain View Cemetery, Boulder, CO.

Their son, Jonathan, attended Yankton College in SD and graduated with a
theology degree and became a minister serving churches in OH and CA. He was
united in marriage, while attending Yankton College, to Ava Ruth Schmidt of
Tripp. They have three sons - Tim Blackwood (Madeline), San Jose, CA; Todd
Hochstatter, San Carlos, CA; and Ted Hilton (Hisako), San Diego, CA. His widow
resides in San Carlos, CA.

Their daughter, Sally (Salome), married Second Lieutenant R. Gordon Rudolph on
May 2, 1943. From Sept. 1944 to May 1946 she lived with her parents until Capt.
Rudolph returned from duty with the 103rd Infantry Division in the Third and
Seventh Armies in Europe. They have three children: Mrs. A.F. (Judith) Scully,
Rapid City; Grant K. (Victoria), Mill Valley, CA; and Mrs. Mark C. (Nancy)
Johnson, Moorhead, MN.

Great-grandchildren are: David, Mark, and Daniel Scully; Blake and Selena
Rudolph; Kayla and Katrina Johnson; Abram Blackwood and Alicia Hilton.

        Vernon and Esther (Miller) Hochstatter by Vernon M. Hochstatter
The first two years of our marriage, Esther (Miller) and I farmed near Java. In
the fall of 1951 we moved onto a farm near Alexandria, MN. In 1953 our cattle
got Bang's disease. That same year, Esther became sick with rheumatic fever. She
was in the hospital 86 days. Five doctors at the Alexandria clinic told us there
was nothing more they could do for her. Esther's mother encouraged us to go to
an Assembly of God church, as they believed in praying for the sick. Rev.
Morken, the pastor, came to the hospital and to the farm and taught us healing
scriptures. Several weeks later, Esther received a miracle in the hospital. She
was instantly healed. This is how we decided to go to the Assembly of God
Church.

In 1953 we sold the farm at Alexandria and moved to Minneapolis. For over two
years, I went from job to job, out of work much of the time. I joined Full
Gospel Businessmen. There I heard a testimony of a businessman who claimed for
his life Psalm 1, verses 1-3, which ends "Whatsoever he doeth shall prosper." I
started trying to meet the conditions of that Psalm and started claiming it for
my life. In 1955 I got a job hauling garbage for the Lake Harriet and Edina
Garbage Company. Three weeks later, I had a disagreement with the owner, so I
quit. Now, with no job and about out of money, I asked God for direction. I was
impressed that Psalm 1 promised God would bless whatever I do. I needed to do
something. I had brought a truck along from the farm and spent two days
soliciting customers for a rubbish hauling business. I bought a license and
started hauling. After two or three weeks my neighbor across the street took my
lawnmower as down payment for building a hoist for my truck. We were in this
business from 1955 to 1972. Small companies were going out of business. After I
lost my contract with the city of Robbinsdale, I went to work for B.F.I. in
1972. Our two sons, Duane and David, work for this company. We have two
daughters, Ruth and Lois.

Since 1987 Esther and I have had a housecleaning business, which we still
operate. We do not plan to retire. We feel the exercise is healthy and we find
good use for the money. Esther and I are thankful we found each other. We
believe all our children and grandchildren love the Lord. We feel very blessed.

Esther and I celebrated our 50th Wedding Anniversary July 17, 1999.

Ruth is married to Steven Lester, a chiropractor. They live in Bismarck, ND and
have two daughters, Marrisa and Jessica. Marrisa is married to Ephrain Makwe and
they have a daughter, born May 1999. He goes to college. They live in Bismarck,
ND. Jessica is in college. Vern and Esther's second child is Duane. He is
married to Coleen Pflepsen and they have two children, Daniel and Marria. They
are divorced. Duane remarried to Cynthia Stroh. They all live in Bloomington,
MN. Duane drives a truck for B.F.I. Lois, Vern and Esther's third child, never
married. She is employed at Elijah Counseling Center in Post Falls, ID. Their
fourth child, David, married Brenda Barrett. He is employed at B.F.I. They have
three children, Nicole, David, and Joshua and live in Bloomington, MN.

        Christ R. and Rose (Spiry) Hochstatter
Christ R. Hochstatter, the seventh child of John and Katherine (Biel)
Hochstatter, was born and raised near the Java area, and he was united in
marriage to Rose Spiry in Nov. 1919 at the Lutheran church of Java.

The young couple moved on the Spiry homestead and farmed for two years, then
moved to the Hochstatter homestead, which was located five miles NE of Java. The
young couple tolerated many hardships while they were farming. The Depression
and drought forced the Hochstatters to lose their father's homestead.

(Photo:) The Christ R. Hochstatter Family

In 1940, Christ, Rose, and their two children moved to Java where they bought a
home. In 1941, Christ entered the Reisch School of Auctioneering at Austin, MN,
and received his License in Auctioneering. Christ conducted many sales in SD and
ND.

In 1949, Christ was appointed as Chief of Police of Java and served on the force
for seven years. In 1967 the Hochstatters started an antique shop with their
son, Orville. Five years later it was sold at auction. Christ passed away in
Mar. 1971 and his wife, Rose, passed away in Nov. 1973.

Christ and Rose had one daughter and one son. Luella married Raymond Schuh, son
of John and Emma (Boehler) Schuh, and had Bonnie, Jon, and Hollie. Luella moved
to Spokane, WA and is now married to Mr. Hammond. Orville graduated from Java
High School and joined the Merchant Marines in World War II. He remained single
and also moved to Spokane after his parents passed away.

married Margaretha Biel, who was born Jan. 3, 1864 in Annental, South Russia.
The Hochstetter family came to the U.S. in 1889 and arrived in the Java area,

To this union eight children were born: Fred C., Fredricka (George) Wahl, Lena
(Wm.) Fiechtner, Margaret (John) Lutz, Kathryn (Ed) Gill, Louise (Leonard)

(Photo:) Christian Hochstetter Family

Christian passed away in 1909, and Margaretha remained on the farm with her
family until 1916 when she bought a home in Java and moved her family to town.
She resided in Java until her death on Aug. 26, 1931.

The farm they homesteaded was later occupied by a son, Fred, and in later years,
by Fred's son, Herbert, also deceased.

        Margaret (Hochstetter) and William Tretheway

        Johann Hoffer-Maria Rieger Family
Johann (John) Hoffer born in Wolseley, N.W. T., Canada May 19, 1898, to Jakob
and Eva (Schaeffer) Hoffer, newly arrived emigrants from Neudorf, So. Russia by
way of Port Halifax, Nova Scotia. They immigrated to the Reliance, SD area to
homestead. That same year Jakob and Katherina (Ritter) Rieger emigrated from
Gluckstal, So. Russia by way of Ellis Island, and homesteaded in the rocky hills
north of Akaska. Their youngest daughter, Maria ("Marie," "Mary") Rieger, was
born there Aug. 5, 1907.

Maria was working at the John Klein farm near Java, where she met John Hoffer.
They were married in a double-wedding ceremony with her sister Eva Rieger
(Kraft) Nov. 20, 1927, at Akaska and took residence on the Jake Helm farm NE of
Java. They lived there until the early Depression years when they moved to Java.

From this marriage were born one daughter and four sons: Frieda 0., Mar. 23,
1928; Marvin C., Jan. 3, 1936; Albert J., Jan. 31, 1938; Gary E., Dec. 4, 1943;
and Carl R., June 10, 1945. All children were born at home. They were birthed in
the bitter cold of winter and heat of summer with occasional help from midwife,
Mrs. Margarete Bratzel, and Doc George, practicing Veterinarian turned MD, just
like many "Javans".

We all attended that Java Elementary and High School, some with honors, some
without. Hard, but good years. In addition to public education, we absorbed some
formal Lutheran education from our church, St. Paul Lutheran, its many pastors,
Sunday school teachers, all very dedicated persons. Our thanks to all those men
and women, whom we grew to know, love, and respect.

Frieda left for college in NE, married and ultimately settled in FL, where she
resides with husband Carl Queen. Albert spent 20 years in the military, raised
three sons, J. Stanley, G. Keith, and G. Wayne, and lives near Cascade, MT with
his wife Ann. Gary H. married Fran after the military and "homesteaded" in
Madera, CA. Carl married Helen after the military and "homesteaded" in Clovis,
CA and has two daughters, Tamara M. and Kimberly K. Marvin C. married Jean and
they have three children, Christopher J., Amy A., and Timothy J. They reside in
Lewistown, MT.

John Hoffer died Feb. 21, 1963 at Bowdle, and Maria H. died Feb. 25, 1991 at
Selby. Both are buried at the Lutheran Cemetery, Java.

        Rev. Ralph Leonard Holmlund
Ralph Leonard Holmlund was pastor of St. Paul Lutheran Church from 1985 to 1992.
A native of southeastern Montana, Ralph was born Apr. 19, 1929 to Helen and
Ralph Walter Holmlund at Miles City. He was raised on his paternal grandparents'
homestead 35 miles NW of Miles City during the drought and Depression of the
1930's. He attended country grade schools and graduated in 1947 from Custer
County High School in Miles City. He attended Custer County Junior College in
1948.

With his two younger brothers, Ralph shared life on the homestead and in area
schools until the family moved, in 1951, to western Montana's Bitterroot Valley,
which is named for the Montana state flower, the roots of which provided food
for native Americans.

After attending Concordia College and the University of Montana, Ralph was
drafted for two years, into the Army, during the Korean War and served one year
with the Far East Military Command on the island of Okinawa.

After graduating in 1956 from Concordia College at Moorhead, MN, Ralph enrolled
at Luther Seminary in St. Paul, MN to prepare for parish ministry, graduating in
May 1960. He accepted his first pastoral call to Prairie City, SD Lutheran
Parish.

On June 7, 1958 at Gosen Lutheran Church, Erskine, MN, Ralph married Charlotte
Gjerstad, who had trained at Concordia College for elementary teaching. She was
substitute church organist and gave music lessons to piano students. In July
1983, at Wilmot, SD, Charlotte died of skin cancer, leaving to mourn her loss
her husband and two college-age children. Blessed be her memory.

The Lord gave them two children. Randey was married in 1995 to Joan Zieske. They
live and work in Fargo. Karyn Holmlund and Robert Heiden were united in marriage
by Pastor Holmlund on Sept. 1989, at St. Paul Lutheran Church in Missoula, MT.
In Jan. 1994, they named their first son, Aaron. Zachary, was born Oct. 1996.
Ralph's grandsons live with their parents at Plains in northwestern Montana.

Ralph and his family served parishes in SD at Prairie City, Midland,
Bridgewater, and Wilmot prior to coming to St. Paul Lutheran in Java. After more
than 30 years in parish ministry, Pastor Holmlund left Java to care for his
ailing parents at their Hamilton, MT home. In 1995 Pastor Holmlund retired from
active ministry after being on staff at Faith Lutheran Church, Hamilton, in
1994.

Ralph resides where his parents made their home for over 25 years, having moved
close to Hamilton in their retirement years until they were deceased in the mid
90's.

        Christian and Elizabeth Horst
Christian Horst, his wife, Elizabeth, his widowed mother Philiphina Horst, his
four sons and daughter came to SD in Mar. 1898. The sons were Rudolph, Louie,
Reinhold and Adolph, and the daughter was Rosina. Fred, the youngest son was
born south of Java, in 1903.

The Horst family left South Russia and came to America looking for a better
place to live. They came to New York by ship and traveled by train to Bowdle.
Mr. Horst filed claims on land south of Java. This was to be their homestead on
which they built a sod and rock house. Mr. Horst was also a blacksmith and had
his own shop on the farm and later was employed in a blacksmith shop in Java.

Christian Horst passed away on the farm in 1908. His mother passed away in 1909
and Christian's wife, Elizabeth, remained on the farm with her sons until the
farm was sold in 1910. Mrs. Horst moved to Java and 29 years later she passed
away.

(Photo:) Christian Horst family  in 1904. Front: Mrs. Philiphina Horst,
         Elizabeth, Christian Horst holding Fred. Back: Adolph, Reinhold, and
         Louie

Rosina Horst married Fred Dufloth in Feb. 1906. The young couple farmed south of
Java until 1920 when they moved to Java, where Mr. Dufloth and Louie Horst built
the Grand Theatre. They were in business for 10 years then sold it and moved to
Terry, MT. Fred Dufloth passed away in 1959 and his wife Rosina passed away in
1964.

Rudolph Horst married Rosina Dufloth in Feb. 1906 and this couple farmed on the
homestead until it was sold and then they moved to Java. He operated a dray line
and also was town marshal for a number of years. Rosina passed away in 1918 and
Rudolph married, in 1919, Magdaline Weisfenning. They moved on a farm north of
Java, where he remained until he passed away in 1929.

Louie Horst married Emilia Pressler and lived on a farm south of Java until 1920
when they moved to Java. Louie and Fred Dufloth built and operated the Grand
Theatre. Louie sold his share in the theatre and started working for the
Milwaukee railroad. He worked for the railroad until his retirement in 1958.
Mrs. Horst passed away in 1956.

Reinhold Horst was married to Magdalina Schock in 1916. Mrs. Horst passed away
in 1934 and Reinhold continued farming south of Java and later east of Java
until 1948 when they moved to Glenham. Reinhold remarried in 1936 to Ernestine
Pressler.

Adolph Horst married Christina Huber in 1920. They farmed in the Java area for a
number of years and later moved to Montana, where he farmed for several years
before returning back to Java. Both are deceased. They had two boys and two
girls.

Fred Horst was born on the family homestead in 1903. He lived and worked with
his brother, Reinhold all his life until his death in 1973.
