        Fredrick C. and Rosina (Bauder) Perman
For many decades, the Perman family lived in the colonies between the Dnjestr
and the Bug Rivers, located in the Black Sea area of South Russia. They, like
many generations before them, went to colonize at the invitation of Catherine
the Great. Ludwig Perman and his family left Busenbach, District of Karlsruhe,
Grand Duchy of Baden, Germany, in 1809. They were among the original founding
families of Kassel in South Russia.

(Photo:) Fredrick C. and Rosina Perman

In 1871, Alexander II introduced representative local government to the
colonists. This is the same year in which Fredrick Perman came into the world.
He was born Sept. 6, 1871 to Christoph and Katharine Weisert Perman, in the
village of Neu-Gluckstal. His mother died in an accident caused by run-away
horses when he was seven years old. His father later married Katharina Feickert.

At about the time he returned home from serving in the Russian Army, he heard
about the Homestead Act in the U.S. It provided that an alien, over 21, could
obtain 160 acres of land if he intended to live on it. For the landless farmer,
160 acres of land is a great attraction.

Fredrick married Rosina Bauder on Jan. 16, 1894, in Freudental, and soon
immigrated to America. The passport was in three languages: French, German and
Russian. After crossing Europe to Bremen, Germany, they boarded a steamship for
New York.  As they approached New York harbor, they could see the Statue of
Liberty, which was just 10 years old. They stopped at Ellis Island, "The Gateway
to the New World", which was used as an immigration station. From New York, they
took the railroad to Freeman, arriving on Mar. 18, 1894.

Fredrick was 23 and Rosina (nee Bauder) was 20 when the decision to leave was
made. They came with eight other families. Those listed were Rosina's parents
the Jacob Bauder family, Christoph Perman, his wife Katharina, their son
Christian 13, and Christoph 10, Adam Mertz, Jacob Mertz, John Feickert, Adam
Schlecht and Gottlieb Oster families.

Mr. Perman filed on a homestead in the southern part of McPherson County, where
a sod house was built. Three children were born here. Jacob F., Aug. 1, 1894;
Christoph F., May 2, 1896; and Katherine, Feb. 6, 1898.

In 1900, Fredrick purchased land in Glenn Township, 11 miles north of Hoven. Eva
(Feb. 12, 1900), Rosina (May 30, 1902), Edward F. (Aug. 25, 1904) and Emma (Aug.
26, 1906) were born here. In Mar. of 1907, they moved on what was known as the
Jergenson farm. Wilhelmina  (Sept. 6, 1908), William J. (Aug. 12, 1901) and
Henry G. (July 24, 1912) were born there.

In about 1912, they moved to Java and Mr. Perman went into the machinery
business with his brother-in-law, Henry Sonnenfeld. He later joined Jacob Merkel
in a blacksmith business and again, with Andrew Lutz, another brother-in-law, in
a tavern.

Their first automobile was a high wheeler International, two-cylinder with four
posts. Around 1925, they owned a Hupmobile touring car.

Fredrick and Rosina retired about 1928 when they built a home in Java. While
they lived in Java, they celebrated their Golden Wedding Anniversary.

Mr. Perman served the community in many ways through the years. He was one of
the early converts to power farming, purchasing one of the kerosene-burning Hart
Parr combustion tractors. They sold their home in Java in Mar. 1946, and moved
to Selby. Rosina passed away Jan. 1, 1959 and Fredrick on May 2, 1963.

Katherine married Adolph Rieger, Eva married Jake C. Bieber, Rosina married John
Goltz, Minnie married Albert Wahl, Christoph F. died Oct. 14, 1923, Emma Wagner
died Feb. 22, 1966 and Henry G. died Nov. 20, 1959.

        Jacob F. and Katherine (Thurn) Perman
One of the early businessmen of Java was Jacob F. Perman, the first child of
Fredrick C. and Rosina (Bauder) Perman, born Aug. 1, 1894, in McPherson County,
on the homestead 10 miles north of Bowdle. He lived there until he was about six
years old, when the family purchased a farm in Glenn Township in Walworth
County. He helped his father on the farm, went to school, and took religious
instructions, as was the custom. Later, he went to Eureka Lutheran College at
Eureka.

On Feb. 3, 1917, during a blizzard, which lasted several days, Jake and
Katherine Thurn were married at the Perman farm on the hill. In Oct., they moved
to Portland, OR, where Jake worked in the shipyards. While they lived there,
Eugene F. was born on Aug. 5, 1919. Jake, being a farmer at heart, came back to
help his father with the crops. They lived on the farm for three years. Harvey
was born Nov. 10, 1920 and Adeline, Apr. 4, 1922.

(Photo:) Jacob F. and Katherine Perman

The family moved to Lowry in the fall of 1922, where Jake sold farm machinery,
cars and grain. The business was sold to G.G. Schock in Dec. 1925, at which
time Jake purchased a building one block off Main Street in Java from the
Farmers Equity Exchange. This building was also used for community dances. As
the business grew, he moved to Main Street, across from the Bauer store, where
he had the International Harvester business, service station and auto
dealership. The house was moved from Lowry to Java. Genevieve was born there
Oct. 28, 1929. Jake served on the school board, and they were members of St.
Paul Lutheran Church.

The family operated the movie theatre during 1934 to 1937, and in the latter
part of 1937, they moved to Moorhead, MN, until the spring of 1940, when Jake
went into business selling parts and machinery in Eureka. They retired in 1946
and moved to Sacramento, CA.

Eugene F. married Irene Pudwill and had three daughters: Joan, Nancy and Carol.
Harvey H., married Lois Rosenow, and was an Orthopedic Surgeon. They had four
children: Guy, William, Barbara and Jimmy. Adeline M. married Harry Weston and
had two sons: Bradley C. and Craig D. Weston. Genevieve married Duane Euren and
had two sons: Barry and Richard Euren.

        Henry F. and Helena M. (Wolf) Perman
Henry and Helen Perman were lifelong residents of Walworth County. Henry was
born July 24, 1912, on the family farm 14 miles SE of Java, the youngest of 10
children born to Fred C. and Rosina (Bauder) Perman. Helen also was born near
Java on Dec. 8, 1913, the second oldest of four children of Jacob F. and Lydia
(Bauder) Wolf.

(Photo:) Henry F. and Helena Perman

Henry and Helen graduated from Java High School with the class of 1932. They
both attended college. They were married on Apr. 28, 1935, at St. Paul Lutheran
Church in Java, and made their home in Java, where Henry was employed at Perman
Implement.

They have three children: Nina (Don) Brockel of Selby; they have a daughter,
Debra, and a son, David. Terry, who married Janice Hoffman, lives in Camas, WA;
they have four children, Gary, Lisa, Todd and Julie. Wayne, who married Sally
Knecht, lived in Mobridge; they have three children, Mark, Troy and Kris. Wayne
passed away June 19, 1998.

In 1940, Henry opened the Java Implement, which he operated until 1946. Then he
was again associated with Perman Implement, which had moved to Selby some years
back. In 1948, the Permans moved their home to Selby to be closer to his
employment, where he worked until 1950, when poor health forced him to
temporarily retire. In 1954, his health improved and he accepted a position as
desk clerk at the Berens Hotel, where he worked for a year and then was elected
Walworth County Auditor for two terms. Helen worked with him as his deputy.
After Henry completed two terms as Auditor, Helen was elected to serve as
Walworth County Auditor, and Henry served as deputy Auditor. He also served as
secretary of the Upper Missouri Valley County Commissioners Assn. He was serving
in both of these positions at the time of his death, Nov. 20, 1959.

Helen was elected to serve as Walworth County Auditor in 1958. She was serving
her eighth term in office at the time of her death, July 5, 1973. She went to
work on that day, as usual, suddenly became ill and passed away at the office.

Henry and Helen were members of St. John Lutheran Church in Selby. They were
laid to rest in the Lutheran section of the Selby Memorial Gardens.

        Christ and Friedericka (Diegel) Permann
Christ Permann, who was born in the Colony of New-Gluckstal, South Russia, on
Dec. 8, 1868, spent his youth in Russia. He served for a short time in the
Russian Army. In 1891, he married Friedericka Diegel of the same Colony. She was
born Mar. 17, 1871. They made their home on a farm given to them by his father.

Six children were born to them in Russia, one dying at birth. In 1900, they
disposed of their property and got a passport for the U.S. on Feb. 9, 1900. They
arrived in Bowdle on Apr. 6, 1900, and for a time, stayed with the Fred Diegel
family of Java. He was a brother of Mrs. Permann.

These early settlers endured many hardships. Mr. and Mrs. Permann settled on a
homestead about six miles SW of Lowry, in Potter County. They left their five
children with the Fred Diegel family at Java. After going to the new homestead
with a team of horses and a wagon, they built their first living quarters the
hard way. They lived under an overturned wagon box during most of the summer of
1900. It was a happy occasion when they brought their children to their first
home in SD. They stayed on this homestead for 10 years. Seven more children were
born during this time, which included two sets of twins.

On June 25, 1906, Mr. Permann became a Citizen of the U.S. This also made his
wife and five children citizens.

In 1910, they bought a farm in Walworth County. Four more children were born on
this farm.

(Photo:) Friedericka and Christian Permann and Donnie Goetz

During all those years, from 1900 to 1914, they farmed with horses. They
acquired a herd of cattle and milked cows by hand. Because of a good crop in
1914, Mr. Permann bought his first threshing machine and tractor. Before the
purchase of the tractor, a two-cylinder Titon, they farmed 1100 acres, all with
horses. In 1916 they bought their first car, a used 1914 Model T Ford.

Religion always played an important part in the family life, and during the
early years, worship services were held in schools and often in homes. In 1901,
the Congregational Church at Lowry was organized. The Christ Permanns became
charter members.

In 1920, the Permanns moved to the town of Lowry and retired. They lived there
until 1934, when they moved to Java. In Nov. 1941, they celebrated their Golden
Wedding Anniversary. Three years later, Mrs. Permann passed away. Christ died in
June 1947. They are buried in the Java Cemetery.

        Fred and Katherine (Huber) Permann
Fred Permann, son of Christ and Friedericka Permann, and Katherine Huber,
daughter of Karl and Christina Huber, were married on June 9, 1919 at Lowry.

Seven children were born to this couple. One daughter died in infancy. Meda,
born in 1919, married Alex Schlepp. They had a son, Terry, who passed away Dec.
1999, and a daughter, Sharon. Meda lives at the Good Samaritan Center in Selby.
Melbert, born in 1921, died in 1983. He was married to Irene Reuer, and they had
two children, Curt and Bonnie. Allen was born in 1923 and died in 1957. He was
married to Phyliss Walton. Allen operated a barbershop on Java's Main Street for
many years. Clifford was born in 1926. He married LaVina Reuer. They have four
children. Cliff and LaVina now reside in TX. LaVina was Postmaster at Java for
many years. Juanita was born in 1930 and married Herbert Himmerich in 1949. They
had a son, Richard, and a daughter, Candace. Juanita lives in Selby, where she
sells Watkins products. She does not have her Mom's "Green Thumb". Sylvia was
born in 1938 and graduated from Java High School in 1956. She was a Snow Queen
in her Sr. year at Java High.

(Photo:) Fred and Katherine Permann

Fred and Katherine farmed in the Lowry area for many years. Their son Melbert
took over the farm. Fred, Katherine and daughters, Juanita and Sylvia, moved
into Java in 1945. They bought the former Jake Helm residence, which is now
owned and occupied by Jerome and Lanniko Lee and their daughter, Kleore.

The Permann family belonged to St. Paul Lutheran Church in Java. Fred, a member
of the choir, was noted for his deep bass voice, which blended well with others
in every hymn.

Fred owned Perman Plumbing and Heating on Java's Main Street in the 50's and
60's. He was a hard-working, honest man. He served on the Java City Council.
Fred had to give up his business when he became ill. He died in 1969.

Katherine was known as the "African Violet Lady". She crossbred African Violets
with the help of a friend, Mrs. Mary Hirsch. They advertised in magazines and
sold plants in many parts of the county. The west 2nd floor bedroom was the
African Violet room. The windows in that room were inundated with a colorful
array of Violets that were given tender loving care. Katherine had a great love
for flowers and was not afraid to let their blossoms have their way. She
propagated many new strains of flowers, which she named from the fruits of her
garden. She also had exceptional gardening skills and had a network of
strawberries that spread along the length of the driveway.

Katherine created many original recipes: nothing was wasted. She was a master
recycler before it became an environmental issue. She canned, froze, dehydrated,
and made many healthy drinks for the family with her electric juicer.

After Fred's death, Katherine moved to Selby to be closer to her family. She
later passed away at the Good Samaritan Center in Selby, in 1985.

        Adolph and Lydia (Schlepp) Pfaff
Friedrich Pfaff, Sr., is the father of Adolph Pfaff. He was born in New-
Freudental, Russia on May 31, 1854. He passed away June 17, 1911. He was married
to Magdalina Martha Bender.

In 1874, Friedrich came with his parents to the U.S. and settled at Yankton,
Dakota Territory. While making his home in Yankton, he was employed for several
months on the "Far West", a steamboat that was closely connected with the last
campaign of General Custer. The "Far West" brought the wounded men, who were in
the command of Reno, to Benteen at Bismarck, from the vicinity of the "Little
Big Horn" battlefield.

In 1877, Friedrich married Magdalena Bender. Friedrich received his Certificate
of Naturalization on Nov. 7, 1879. In 1888, they moved to Bridgewater, where he
managed a store and machine shop for several years. They resided on a farm near
Bridgewater for about five years. In 1890 they moved to Emmons County, ND. They
settled on a farm in the Sandcreek neighborhood, where Friedrich died at age 57.
He was the father of 12 children, seven sons and five daughters. Four daughters
and six sons survived him. His chosen occupation was farming at Linton, ND.

Adolph Pfaff was born Aug. 12, 1895 at Temvek, ND. On Jan. 9, 1917, he married
Lydia Schlepp. They moved to Crow Rock, MT. A son, Milton, was born at Crow
Rock. Adolph farmed with his brother John. They moved back to Java and resided
on the Jake Helm farm. Two sons, Herbert and Raymond, and one daughter, Verna,
were born there. They bought a home in Java and Adolph Pfaff bought the Java
drayline. He sold the drayline in 1946 to Adolph J. Horst. Adolph then worked
for the railroad and was a mail driver until he passed away on Nov. 12, 1945.
His wife Lydia was a mail carrier for a few years. Her other places of
employment were at Elmer Biel's Red Owl, Elmer and Erna Schelpp's Cafe, and at a
Selby cafe.

(Photo:) Adolph and Lydia Pfaff

Herbert married Claudia Kary and they had three children: Carol, Donald and
Dixie. Raymond married Doris Wolff and they had two children: Raymond, Jr. and
Shelly. Verna married Clifton Schnaible and they had three children: Dale,
Connie and Paul.

        Christian Pfitzer
Christian Pfitzer was born Sept. 8, 1863 in Hoffnungstal, Bessarabia, Romania.
His wife, Katharina Oster, was born Nov. 25, 1863 in the same place. Both were
confirmed in 1878 in Kloestitz and married Feb. 20, 1884, in Kloestitz. This
union was blessed with five children: Margaretha, Christ, Jr., Matheus (Matt),
Rosina and Julius. The first three were born in Romania and the last two were
born on a farm near Java.

After serving in the Czar's army, Christian Pfitzer moved his family to America,
landing at Port New York on June 18 1892, and received his final naturalization
papers in 1900.

They moved on a farm 15 miles NW of Bowdle, which was their town until the start
of Java in 1900. In 1909, they moved to Java so their youngest son, Julius,
could attend the Java school. Christ Jr., and Matheus (Matt) stayed on the farm.
Margaretha, the oldest, had already married Adam Eisenbeisz, and Rosina died in
infancy.

(Photo:) Mr. and Mrs. Christian Pfitzer

During the flu epidemic in 1918, Katharina Oster Pfitzer passed away. The
following year, Christian married Christiana (Oster) Goetz, a sister of his
first wife. He was among the members of the first St. Paul Lutheran Church in
1897, along with Karl Schnaible, George Haux, Sr., John Lutz, Sr., Fred Spiry,
Sr., Philip Spiry, Sr., George Wolf and Matheus Wolf. He was one of the eight
that built the first St. Paul Lutheran Church near Java, which later was moved
to town, being a member for 45 years. His first wife, Katharina, was also an
active and religious member.

Christian was recognized in Walworth and surrounding counties as one of the most
widely known cattle and livestock buyers in the territory, being associated with
the Pfitzer, Helm and Schlaht firm, which was well known by Commission firms in
South St. Paul. He was later associated with Jake Henne and Fred Spiry, and with
Jake Weil and Art Lane of Aberdeen, and Charlie Brown of Onida. He died Mar. 15,
1940.

His father, Johann Pfitzer was born Aug. 16, 1833, and his mother Margaretha
Pfitzer was born May 1, 1829.

        Matheus (Matt) J. and Maria (Hepper) Pfitzer
Matt J. Pfitzer, born in Hoffnungstal, Bessarabia, South Russia on Aug. 21,
1892, was the son of Christian and Katherina (Oster) Pfitzer. He migrated to
this country with his parents in 1893, and settled on a farm five miles NE of
Java. His brothers were Christian and Julius, and his sisters were Margaretha
(Adam) Eisenbeisz and Rosina Pfitzer, who passed away in infancy.

(Photo:) Matt J. and Marie Pfitzer

Maria Hepper Pfitzer was born June 20, 1894, at Gilead, South Russia. She
migrated to this country with her widowed mother, Mrs. Jacob Hepper, in May of
1909. Her brothers and sisters were John, Christina, Jake, Louise, Molly, Carl,
Philip and Rose. Shortly after coming to this country, her mother married Jacob
Berg and settled in the Swan Lake area.

Matt and Maria were united in marriage at Java, on Apr. 9, 1912 by Rev. George
Kirchdoerfer. After their marriage they settled on a farm six miles NE of Java.
In Nov. 1919 they moved in to Java. In Mar. 1920, Matt went into business with
his brother Julius, and brother-in-law, Adam Eisenbeisz. The business was
purchased from Carl Hepper and was known as the City Billiard Parlor and Barber
Shop. They operated this business until 1928, when the partnership was
dissolved. During the operation of this business, they also operated a Pfitzer
and Eisenbeisz threshing rig, and also did sidewalk farming. In the spring of
1931, they moved back to the Pfitzer farm and in 1952, purchased the Sam Oster
residence.

Eight sons were born to Matt and Maria. Art and Bernard died in infancy.
Gehbardt married Hulda Wolf, Chris J. married Lillian Zeller, Harold married
Helen Haux, Marvin married Betty Spiry, and Robert married Joyce Rosin. (See the
following Family Histories) Wayne, born Dec. 24, 1932, spent his boyhood years
in the Java area. He attended Java High School, participating in sports, and
graduating in 1951. After serving in the Korean War from 1952 to 1954, Wayne
moved to Minneapolis, MN, where he was employed at Anaka Gas Co. In June 1956,
he married Arlene Buechler in Bowdle. They have two sons and one daughter,
Perry, Kelly and Penny. They reside in Las Vegas, NV.

Maria Pfitzer passed away on March 23, 1958, and on October 16, 1958, Matt
married Louise Litz Pfitzer. They resided in Java until his death, Jan. 26,
1965.

        Gehbardt and Hulda (Wolff) Pfitzer
Gehbardt Pfitzer was born Feb. 8, 1912 in Java to Matt and Maria (Hepper)
Pfitzer. He worked in the Java post office for many years, farmed with his
parents for a while, and then rented more land and farmed that, as well. He was
a bus driver for Java Public School for seven years, and then became custodian
at the school, where he worked for 15 years before he retired.

Gehbardt married Hulda Wolff on May 13, 1945, in the Baptist Church at Java.
Hulda was born Nov. 21, 1916, to John and Marie Wolff. They lived in the Bowdle
area. After Hulda's father passed away, they moved into Java.

Hulda helped with the NYA (National Youth Assn.), which made clothing for needy
recipients. She also was a cook at the Girls' Dormitory in Java and worked at
the Java post office for a number of years. After retirement, Gehbardt and Hulda
enjoyed their garden and flowers at their home.

Their daughter, Lynda, born Dec. 12, 1948, attended Java school and graduated
from Java High School in 1967. She continued her education and became a
Registered Nurse. A victim of Multiple Sclerosis, Lynda continued in her
profession until she was unable to work. She lives in Oakdale, MN.

        Chris J. and Lillian (Zeller) Pfitzer
Chris J. (CJ) Pfitzer, born Apr. 3, 1917, married Lillian Zeller, who was born
Apr. 11, 1919. They lived most of their lives in Java. CJ went to college for
one year at USD in Vermillion, until he volunteered for the U.S. Army at the
beginning of World War II. He spent three years stationed in New Guinea and
Australia as a Second Lieutenant in Field Artillery. CJ returned home from the
Army and worked in the Java post office as a rural mail carrier until he
retired.

Lillian was a housewife and a mother of three children (Dennis, Neal and Karen),
as well as a rural schoolteacher. She had received a one-year teaching degree
from NSTC. The Pfitzers also owned and ran a cream station and a paint store in
Java for a number of years. CJ enjoyed fishing and showing Arabian horses from
his stable. Lillian enjoyed collecting antiques and studying history. Chris
passed away in 1986 and Lillian now lives in Lakewood, CO.

Dennis, born Aug. 3, 1942, married Cheryl Shroll (now divorced). He lives in
Lakewood, CO and works as an Engineering Project Manager. He has three sons, who
are Chris, Jason and Joel, two daughters-in-law, Angela and Kelli, and one
grandson, Taren.

(Photo:) Marlys, Erika, Nathan and Neal Pfitzer

Neal, born Feb. 15, 1946, married Marlys Schlepp on Aug. 30, 1968, at St. Paul
Lutheran Church in Java. Marlys was born June 18, 1947, to Erna (Fiechtner) and
Elmer Schlepp. The family lived on a farm SW of Bowdle until moving to Java in
1959. She attended farm school and was the only student in her class until
attending 6th grade at Bowdle Public School. Upon graduating from Java High
School, she continued her education at SDSU and received a BS degree in Early
Childhood Education and Social Work. Neal graduated from Java High School and
from SDSU with a BS degree in Parks Management.

Their first home was in Sioux Falls, but they moved to many locations while Neal
was in the Army. Their son, Nathan, was born in Columbus, GA on Jan. 3, 1971.
The small family moved to Berlin, Germany, when Nathan was five months old.
After fulfilling his military obligation, Neal was released from the Army and
the Pfitzers returned to the U.S. The family moved to CO and lived in Lakewood,
where Neal worked as the City Forester for five years, and Marlys managed a Day
Care Center. A daughter, Erika, was born to them on Dec. 10, 1975.

In Apr. 1978, Neal accepted a job as Park Superintendent for the city of Greeley
and held that position for 12 years. They live in Greeley, CO, and Neal owns and
operates a grocery store, the 12th Street Pantry. Marlys began working for an
ophthalmologist in Nov. 1978, where she is still employed.

Nathan attended college at SDSM&T and at the U of Northern CO. He has worked
eight years in a correctional facility as a criminal tech. Erika graduated from
the U of CO in International Business and is employed in Denver as a business
consultant.

Karen, born Aug. 23, 1946, married Jim Ruggles. They live in Vicksburg, MS,
where Karen owns and operates a local gift shop and Jim is an Oral Surgeon. They
have one son, Jon, and one daughter, Teri.

        Harold and Helen (Haux) Pfitzer
Harold Pfitzer was born May 7, 1920, to Matheus and Marie (Hepper) Pfitzer. He
lived in Java with his parents and his brothers Gehbardt, Christ, Marvin, Robert
and Wayne. Two of his brothers, Arthur and Bernard, died in infancy.

When Harold was 10 years old, his parents moved onto his grandfather's farm five
miles NE of Java. Harold went to country school through the eighth grade. At age
15, he went to the CCC camp in the Black Hills for two years. He then came home,
lived with his parents, and helped on the farm. On summers he worked for the
NYA.

Harold was drafted into the Army during World War II. He left Java in Apr. 1942
and served overseas in Hawaii, the Gilbert Islands and Okinawa, Japan, until the
end of the war, returning home Dec. 22, 1945.

Harold was united in marriage to Helen Haux on Aug. 1, 1942. Helen was born Aug.
30, 1924, to Jacob J. and Ida (Hetterle) Haux. She had one brother, Oscar, and
one sister, Frances. She lived at home and went to country school through the
eighth grade. Helen then went to Java High School through the 11th grade.

(Photo:) Harold and Helen Pfitzer

Helen and baby son, Rodney, lived with her parents while Harold was in the Army.
When Harold came home after the war, their small family lived with Helen's
parents, until Mar. 1946. They then rented a house in Java and Harold worked on
the railroad that summer. After working for the railroad, he worked for Ed Biel
during harvesting.

During Aug. 1946, the Harold Pfitzer family moved onto the farm of Matt Pfitzer,
Harold's parents, located five miles NW of Java. They farmed there for three
years.

Harold and his family moved onto the Jacob J. Haux farm, Helen's parents, on
Sept. 1949. The farm was four miles NW of Java. They later bought both the Matt
Pfitzer and the Jacob J. Haux farms and lived and farmed and added two more sons
to their family. In Apr. 1976, they sold everything and retired, buying a home
at the west end of Java.

Rodney was born Dec. 7, 1942. He married Shirley Mickelson Sept. 5, 1965. They
had three sons, Todd, Troy and Chad. Todd married Becky Fleming and they had a
son, James, on Mar. 23, 1998. They live in Fremont, NE, where Todd is an
engineer. Troy lives in Denver, CO and teaches art at a local high school. Chad
lives in Sullivan, IL, and is involved in agricultural business. Rodney later
married Suzanne Miller. He now lives in Madera, CA, and works as a heating and
air conditioning specialist.

Charles was born Oct. 6, 1946, and married Maureen Penry on Oct. 12, 1967. They
have three children, JoAnne, Matthew and Quenton. JoAnne married Toby Gonzales
and they have two children, Curtis and Davida. They live in Westminster, CO,
where Charles is a motorcycle mechanic and JoAnne is a beauty consultant. Matt
survived a devastating bicycle/car accident, which happened when he was just 11
years old. He now lives with his parents, after being on his own for several
years. Quenton married Jacqueline Flageolie and they live in Council Bluffs, IA.

(Photo:) Rodney, Randy, Helen and Charles

Randy was born Dec. 15, 1953, and married Debra Heagey on Jan. 13, 1979. They
have five children, Jeremy, Danine, Deidra, Brent and Dalicia. Jeremy graduated
from Tulare Union High School on June 1, 1998 and is attending the U of MO.
Danine, Deidra, Brent and Dalicia are all students in Tulare, CA. Randy is a
teacher and wrestling coach in Tulare.

Harold died Mar. 3, 1983, at the age of 62. Helen moved to Westminster, CO on
Aug. 14, 1984, where she lived with Charles and Maureen Pfitzer, until Aug.
1992, when she moved into an apartment. On Mar. 7, 1998, Helen moved to Tulare,
CA, where she now lives and is watching her youngest grandchildren grow up.

Harold and Helen have seven grandsons and four granddaughters, three great-
grandsons and one great- granddaughter.

        Marvin and Betty (Spiry) Pfitzer
Marvin Pfitzer was born June 22, 1928, in Eureka, to Matt J. and Marie Hepper
Pfitzer. He graduated from Java High School in 1947. His wife, Elizabeth (Betty)
Spiry was born Oct. 23, 1935, in Java, to Samuel and Hertha Hauck Spiry. Betty
graduated from Java High School in 1953.

Marvin and Betty were married Feb. 12, 1956, at St. Paul Lutheran Church in
Java. After the wedding, they moved to Minneapolis, where Marvin worked for
Standard Oil Company and Betty was employed at Dahlberg Hearing Aid Co. In 1962,
they moved back to Java, where they purchased the Red Owl grocery store from
Elmer Biel.

In 1966 they sold the store to Marvin's younger brother, Robert, and Marvin
began working as a rural mail carrier. Betty worked at the school as a teacher's
assistant.

(Photo:) Marvin Pfitzer Family

They had four children. Lori Ann was born Mar. 30, 1958 and passed away Mar. 25,
1961 after a struggle with cancer.

Ivy Lyn was born Jan. 3, 1960. She graduated from Java High School in 1978. She
married John Davis on Apr. 26, 1980 at St. Paul Lutheran Church in Java. They
resided in Sioux Falls until Aug. 1983, when they moved to Tempe, AZ. Ivy and
John have two sons - Joshua, born Oct. 20, 1982 in Sioux Falls, and Tyler, born
July 6, 1986 in Mesa, AZ. In 1988, Ivy graduated from Mesa Community College,
receiving her AA degree in electromechanical technology. In 1994, she graduated
from the U of Phoenix with a BSBA degree. She received her certificate from the
Institute of Natural Therapeutics as a licensed massage therapist in 1996. In
1990, Ivy and John divorced. Ivy has been employed at Motorola since 1984, has a

Gwen Marie, born Aug. 22, 1961, graduated from Java High School in 1979. She

court reporter and Will is employed as an investment broker. They love to play
golf, travel, and enjoy the many pleasures of beach living.

Kent Marshall was born Mar. 10, 1963, and graduated from Java High School in
1981. He married Holly Charney on Nov. 16, 1991. They have two children,
Chantell and Caleb. They are living in Moses Lake, WA, where Kent is employed
with Inflational Systems.

In 1982, Marvin and Betty moved to Sun City West, AZ, where they are currently
residing. Marvin is a part-time golf instructor, and Betty is a secretary/
receptionist at Palmbrook Country Club in Sun City.

        Robert and Joyce (Rosin) Pfitzer
Robert Pfitzer was born Apr. 5, 1930, in Java to Matt J. and Maria (Hepper)
Pfitzer. His boyhood years were spent in the Java area. He attended Java High
School and participated in many sports. After serving in the Korean War from
1952 to 1954, he returned to farming north of Java.

Robert and Joyce Rosin were united in marriage on July 26, 1954, at St. Paul
Lutheran Church in Java, with Pastor Ernest Haacke performing the ceremony.
After their marriage, they settled on the farm six miles NE of Java. The farm
was sold a year later and Bob was employed in several towns around the area
until 1960, when he was employed at his brother's Red Owl Store in Java. In
1966, Robert and Joyce purchased the Java Red Owl, which they owned and operated
until 1986. Merle and Florence Noess purchased the store and the Pfitzers moved
to Mobridge in 1987, where Robert managed the meat department at the Mobridge
Red Owl. In 1990, Robert developed heart problems and retired.

(Photo:) Joyce and Robert Pfitzer

In 1992, Robert and Joyce entered into a partnership and opened a salvage
grocery store in Mobridge. The following year, two more stores were opened, one
in Eagle Butte and one in Gettysburg. In 1996, they closed the Eagle Butte store
and opened another in Eureka. Robert and Joyce purchased Robbs, Inc., a salvage
grocery store in Mobridge, in 1997, and presently are operating that and a store
in Gettysburg. They reside in Mobridge. Two children were born to Bob and Joyce
Pfitzer.

Craig Allen, born Feb. 1, 1956, married Rona Reinschmidt and they had one
daughter, Nicole Ann. Craig is presently married to Sandra Meier and they have
one son, Kyle. Sandra is a Nurse at Avera St. Luke's Hospital in Aberdeen, where
they live. Craig owns and operates a salvage grocery store at Redfield.

Tamara Kay, born June 21, 1959, married Dwight Goheen. They had a daughter,
Mikell Cherae. Tamara and Mikell reside in Las Vegas, NV, where she owns and
operates Design Dimensions, an interior design firm that specializes in model
home merchandising and custom residential homes. Tammy also owns and operates a
1950's antique shop.

        Julius and Amelia (Fiechtner) Pfitzer
Julius Pfitzer, born Sept. 9, 1902, on his father's homestead five-and-a-half
miles NE of Java, was the youngest son of Christian and Katharina Pfitzer. In
1909, Julius started school, but was detained because of his mother's death in
1918. He also missed quite a bit of school, because of the flu epidemic, but had
finished the first year of high school.

In 1919, Julius and his brother, Matt, and brother-in-law, Adam Eisenbeisz,
bought the City Billiard Parlor and Barber Shop. In 1921, he went to the Twin
City Barber College and completed a course in Tonsorial Arts, which profession
he followed for 14 years. The Pfitzer and Eisenbeisz partnership also did crop
farming and custom threshing for several years.

In 1925, Julius was united in marriage to Amelia Fiechtner, who was born Dec.
13, 1903, to Gottlieb II and Karolina Fiechtner. She grew up in the Java area,
attended rural school and later, attended and graduated from Java High School in
1925.

(Photo:) Julius and Amelia Pfitzer

Julius was appointed Java Postmaster on July 19, 1935, and took office on Aug.
16, 1935. He held this office until his retirement on Oct. 31, 1969. Previously,
he had served as a sub rural mail carrier since 1931. Julius was City Police
Officer for a number of years, a member of the Java Board of Education for 15
years, a member of the City Council for 12 years, Justice of Peace for a few
years, and was City Auditor of Java, 1959-1975. He was Chief of the Java
Volunteer Fire Dept. for 20 years and President of the Java Chamber of Commerce
for 14 years. In 1960 he was named to the SD Baseball Hall of Fame for the
contribution to the sport, as manager of the city and Legion teams for nearly 40
years. This recognition and honor was given him at the Fourth Annual Meeting
Night at Faulkton, with 300 in attendance at the SD Amateur Baseball Hall of
Fame Dinner. Of this honor he was very proud, being a born lover of baseball.
Julius served as chairman of the Walworth County Zoning and Planning Commission.
He was a Civil Defense Director, passing a test and holding a certificate in
Civil Defense from USD at Vermillion. Julius and Amelia, life-long members of
St. Paul Lutheran Church in Java, were also members of the church choir.

Three children were born to this couple. Julius passed away in 1981 and Amelia
in 1996.

Gerald graduated from Java High School in 1949. He married and had six children:
Merle, David, Donna, Mark, Cindy and Daniel, and 12 grandchildren. Gerald lives
in Aberdeen.

Orville was born July 29, 1938 at Java, where he completed all 12 years of
school, graduating in 1956. He graduated from NSC in 1960 with a Bachelor of
Science Degree in Secondary Education, majoring in Physical Education and
Science. In 1960-61 he started teaching, and coached all sports at New Effington
High School, where he remained for two years. In 1962, he married Carol Becker
at Webster. Orville taught science and coached all sports at Brentford High
School for two years. In 1969, the Kidder High School consolidated with the
Britton High School, where Orville and Carol taught until their retirement in
1994, after spending 35 years each in the teaching field. They have two
children. Judy lives in Britton and is employed at Sheldahl, Inc., and Debra is
married and presently living in Garretson, SD and teaching in Hartford, which is
called West Central School. Her husband is an instructor at the South East
Technical College in Sioux Falls. They have four children. The Pfitzers have
been active members of the First Presbyterian Church in Britton, the Marshall
County Sportsman Club, Lions Club, Jaycee and Jaycee-ettes, the Britton Swimming
Pool Committee, Retired Teachers Organization. Orville is presently serving his
second three-year term on the Britton School Board and is actively involved in
the Community Education Program.

(Photo:) Carol and Orville Pfitzer

Julie Ann was born Sept. 23, 1944, in Mobridge. She attended school in Java,
graduating with the class of 1962. After graduating from NSC in 1967, with
majors in Business Education and Physical Education, she taught school in Java
and Mobridge. In 1970, Julie moved to Aberdeen. She was employed at Herberger's
Dept. Store. Other employment included child-care, Holgate Jr. High School and
Rogers Benefit Group Regional Ins. In 1990 she accepted a position at the
Aberdeen American News and Farm Forum, where she is presently a graphic
designer. Julie has been active in the Brown County 4-H program as a 10-year 4-H
leader. She is a member of Bethlehem Lutheran Church, where she served a term on
the Education Committee and taught Bible School. In 1972, Julie married James
Leibel, son of Aloysius and Elizabeth Leible of Glencross. Their three children
are: Steven, now attending Baylor Law in Waco, TX; Lisa, a student at NDSU in
Fargo; and Laurie, a student at Central High School in Aberdeen. The Leibels
live two miles north of Aberdeen.

(Photo:) James, Julie, Steven, Lisa and Laurie Leibel

        Lillian Pies
Lillian (Aadland) Pies, born Oct. 6, 1911, at Loreburn, Sask., Canada, to Osmund
and Louise (Anderson) Aadland, was the oldest of three children.

She attended the Willdon School, a country elementary school, where she finished
the 8th grade at age 13. There were no busses in those days, and schools were
not consolidated. The children not in the town districts had to pay tuition if
they could attend. Most of them stayed at home or went to work. Further
education was not considered to be important unless the children had a strong
desire to become a teacher, nurse, doctor, etc. As a result, the country boys
became farmers and the girls became homemakers.

Lillian was married to Henry Pies on Oct. 15, 1941, at her parents' home. They
made their first home at Pequot Lakes, MN. Later they moved to Bristol and then
to a farm SE of Webster.

Henry and Lillian had one daughter, Luella (Vaughn) Spiry of Java, and one son,
Neil of Watertown. Neil is married to Nina Raines.

Henry passed away Jan. 6, 1958. Lillian and the children continued to live on
the farm. After her graduation from Webster High School in 1960, Luella went to
NSC in Aberdeen and became a teacher. In Aug. 1965, Neil joined the U.S. Air
Force. When he returned from the service, he attended the Vocational School in
Watertown and started working at Codington County Implement.

Lillian moved to Webster in Nov. 1972, and to Java in July 1979, where she still
resides. She has four grandchildren: Twyla and Arvyn Spiry, and Tanya and Wendy
Pies.

        Jacob and Magdalena Pleinis Sr.
Jacob Pleinis, Sr., and his wife, Magdalena Landenberger, were emigrants from
Russia. They, and their two oldest daughters, Marie and Magdalena, landed in New
York May 3, 1889, on the ship Marsala.

Mr. Pleinis filed for land five miles north of Java and with the help of his
brother-in-law, Carl Schlepp, who had come to this area two years before, was
able to buy an ox and a cow; he borrowed Mr. Schlepp's break plow. He then broke
up a few acres of sod and planted wheat, potatoes and other vegetables. He dug a
well and built a two-room sod house in three days, with the help of neighbors.
The timber for the roof was obtained from the Missouri river area, a two-day
trip by horse and wagon, which was 25 miles west of the homestead.

When the railroad came through Java, Jacob was a carpenter's helper and helped
build some of the first buildings in the new town, such as the Hofmeyer Store,
the Hotel, and the Cook and Lakeman Store. He was a school board member and
served as a county assessor and a county commissioner. After he moved to town in
1924, he was the janitor of the Lutheran church, and served as town marshal for
several years.

(Photo:) Jacob and Magdalena Pleinis, Sr.

Mr. and Mrs. Pleinis were the parents of 10 children: Marie (Martin) Fiedler,
Magdalena (Fred) Rosin, Margaretha (Christ) Nusz, Katherina (Gottlieb) Leidholt,
Martha (Charley) Spiry, Mathilda (John) Flemmer, Emma (Henry) Haux, and Ruth
(John) Warner. The two sons, Jacob, married to Emily Kalmbach, and John, married
to Marie Kalmbach, were the musical members of the family; both played violins
as well as other instruments.

Magdalena passed away in 1918, and Jacob passed away in 1943 at age 84.

        Andrew and Theresa (Bertha) Raba
Steve Raba was born near Budapest, Hungary. Mrs. Raba died in 1887, leaving her
husband with seven small children. Finding it hard to make a living for his
family, because of Hungary's over-crowded population, Steve decided to come to
the new land. He left his five youngest children with their grandfather; when
their grandfather died, an aunt took them in. Steve Raba and his oldest
daughter, Julia, started for the U.S. Landing in 1890, they came directly to
this part of the country, where he homesteaded on land in Walworth County and
made plans to prepare a home for his family.

(Photo:) Theresa and Andrew Raba

In 1893, he sent for his four remaining children: Agnes (13), Andrew (11), John
(9), and Rosie (7). His son, Mike, came over earlier with a friend. Mr. Raba
lived on his farm SE of Selby until 1909, when he sold it to his son, John. In
1910 Steve Raba moved to Canada, where he died some years later at age 86.

Andrew Raba was born at Oberwarth, Hungary, Sept. 10, 1881, and in 1893 he, a
brother and two sisters sailed to the U.S. to join their father. He married
Theresa Bertha June 5, 1906; they were the first couple married in St. Anthony's
Catholic Church at Selby. They lived to celebrate their 50th Wedding
Anniversary.

When they were first married in 1906, they homesteaded 11+ miles SE of Selby.
Their first child, Theresa, was born there. In 1908, they moved and lived with
his father-in-law, Ladislaus Bertha, on a farm 10 miles SE of Selby. They were
blessed with five more children: Martin, Gabriel, Ladislaus, Anna and Paul.

Andrew and Theresa built a new modern home, along with complete farm buildings,
in 1918, and moved there with horse and buggy in the spring of 1919. It was in
this new home that the family was completed with four more children: Philip,
Mark, Katherine and Irene.

The Rabas were the first in the community to have electric lights. Andrew
enjoyed horses, so he traded and sold a lot of them. He farmed with horses until
1943, when he bought his first tractor.

Andrew lost his wife on May 3, 1961; at the time of her death, he still resided
on his farm. When Andrew passed away on June 14, 1970, he had 75 grandchildren
and 50 great-grandchildren. Today there are 171 great-grandchildren and 90
great-great grandchildren.

His grandson, Martin Andrew Raba, now owns the Andrew Raba farm, with all
original buildings.

Theresa was born June 11, 1907. She married Peter Kosters on Sept. 25, 1929.
(See Family History)

(Photo:) Kate and Martin Raba

        Christ W. and Louisa (Biel) Rau Jr.

        Gust and Martha (Hirsch) Rau
Gust Rau was born May 12, 1895. He lived with his parents on the farm they had
homesteaded north of Java. When Gust was four years of age, his mother passed
away and a year later, his father remarried.

Gust has many memories of his father and mother, traveling with the buggy, and
delivering cream, butter and eggs to a little town near by. He also remembers
the daily chores that he and his brother, Christ, would have, and 'slopping' the
hogs. Helping his blind stepmother in the kitchen was another achievement for
Gust, as he was very handy in cooking, especially after his sister was married
and left home.

(Photo:) Gust Rau Family

Albert Lange's store, creamery and post office, located near the Rau farm, was
moved into Java when the town began. Gottlieb Freimark, the mailman, delivered
the mail; his deliveries were to Eureka and back, until the post office was
moved to Java. A small schoolhouse was located near the Rau farm, which was
attended by Gust and the neighboring children. Their first teacher was Fred
Krause, who taught there for a number of years. Gust finished the fifth grade
before he quit school.

In 1917, Gust started to farm for himself and started to build himself a little
home, but was obstructed by the draft. At the age of 21, he was drafted into the
Army and on June 3, 1918, he left for Camp Funston. On July 7, the 89th Division
arrived in London. Their Division was shipped to Camp Descouge, France, for more
training and later served in the front lines for three months, until Armistice
was signed. Gust's Division was sent to Speicher, Germany, until May 9, and sent
on to France, where they received their orders to be shipped back to the U.S. He
arrived in Camp Mills, NY, on May 24, 1919, and then was sent to Camp Dodge, IA,
where he received his discharge.

After returning home, Gust built a small home with some help from a friend, John
Weller, and relatives. In a short time, Gust bought himself a new Ford car and
escorted the girls around.

On Dec. 14, 1919, the Rev. Nusz united Gust and Martha Hirsch in marriage in the
Reformed Country Church. The young couple remained just a short time on the
small farm before moving to the farm presently owned and operated by the Leslie
Rau family.

Thirteen children were born to this couple: One child died when 5 weeks old;
Merilda (Rodger) Christenson; Lavida (Rueben) Eberhardt; Adeline Schnabel;
Lorraine (Albert) Metzger; Ruth (Marvin) Mutschler; Janice (Lloyd) Sieler; Ervin
married Lenora Renz; Stanley married Viola Aman; Perry married Bernice Ehresman;
Harvey married Yvonne Jeschke and lives in Eureka; Leslie married Ramona Kezzler
and lives north of Java; Clarence (deceased), married Meta Holzworth.

Gust and Martha's prayers were answered many times, living during the Depression
and drought, trying to raise a large family. In 1949, Gust and Martha bought a
home and moved to Eureka.

        Alexander Riede

        Dr. Sigmond Rosenthal
Dr. Rosenthal was a physician at Java for many years. He was born in Botosani,
Romania on Jan. 15, 1862. When he was a young man, he went to Vienna, Austria to
study, receiving his dentistry degrees there. From Vienna, he returned to his
birthplace, practiced dentistry, and married Sophie Hildebrand. In 1889, the
couple came to New York City; two years later they moved to Minneapolis, where
he studied medicine. He received his degree from the U of MN. They later came to
SD and made their first home in Eureka, then Evarts and finally, Java. In 1920
they moved to Aberdeen, where he practiced until 1931, when he retired.

Dr. Sigmund Rosenthal died at the age of 71 on Dec. 1933, in Aberdeen. He was
survived by his widow, Sophie Rosenthal, a son and two daughters: Charles A.
Rosenthal of Memphis, TN, Mrs. Francis Young of Sioux City, IA, and Mrs. Stella
Mannes of Aberdeen. Two daughters preceded him in death.

Interesting events occurred while Dr. Rosenthal was practicing medicine in Java.
In 1904, Dr. Rosenthal helped Dr. Edwards, of Bowdle, recover a bullet from the
shoulder of Hugo Schwartz, after Hugo's brother-in-law shot him. In 1916, Dr.
Rosenthal, as Coroner, held an inquest on the death of a Lowry man, only to
learn that the man died from too much alcohol consumption. Dr. Rosenthal
attended to farm accidents, suicides, and accidental shootings, along with his
general medical practice. He opened the Java Medical Drug Store in 1901.

        John and Christina (Schick) Rosin
John Rosin was born Mar. 25, 1858, at the village of Hoffnungstal, Kherson
District, South Russia. Here he was baptized and confirmed in the Evangelical
Lutheran church by Pastor Becker, and grew to young manhood.

On June 18, 1877, John married Christina Schick, daughter of Mr. and Mrs.
Wilhelm Schick.

After seven years of married life, the Rosin family left South Russia and
immigrated to America, settling at Scotland, Dakota Territory. Later the family
moved northward, settling NW of Bowdle, and for some years lived on a farm three
and one-half miles NE of Java, which in later years was the farm of the John
Naasz family.

The Rosins were members of the Neu-Glueckstal Church (also known as Buechler
Church), east of Java, and John was also a charter member of St. John
Evangelical Lutheran Church of Bowdle.

Being desirous of owning his own land, and hearing of the inducements offered by
the Canadian government to attract settlers to Canada, John chose to move to
Canada, and on Mar. 8, 1909, at public auction, sold his personal property. On
Mar. 16th of that year, he boarded the train at Java, with his family and
others, to begin the journey to Canada. They soon arrived at Olds, Alberta,
Canada. During that summer, they moved to their homestead in Alpha School
District in the Hand Hills, near Hanna, Alberta, Canada.

(Photo:) The John Rosin Family

In 1924, Christina passed away, and in 1930 John Rosin moved into the town of
Hanna, where he lived until his passing on Sept. 9, 1937.

Mr. and Mrs. Rosin were the parents of 12 children. Two great-grandchildren of
the John Rosins live in the near area, Mrs. Adam Lutz of Artas, and LeRoy Bender
of Java.

        William and Dorothy (Stoecker) Rosin
William Rosin was born Feb. 21, 1880, in Hoffnungstal, South Russia. His wife,
Dorothea Stoecker, was born in the same village on Mar. 13, 1882. They were
married there in Oct. 1906.

(Photo:) William and Dorothy Rosin

Mr. and Mrs. Rosin and their two small children, Tillie and John, left Russia on
Dec. 9, 1909, as Mr. Rosin wanted to escape from the compulsory military
service. Having served four years in the Russian Army and the Russo-Japanese
war, he was anxious to find a better place for the family to live.

On Dec. 15, they, with Mrs. Rosin's sister, Rosina Stoecker, and Mrs. Rose
(Christ) Gab, boarded the ship Estonia and arrived in New York on Jan. 1, 1910.
They came to SD by train, settling north of Java, in Walworth County, making
their home that winter and the first summer with his brother, Fred and family,
who had come to America a few years earlier.

Making a living for his family was not easy, as they had very little to start
with. In the fall of 1910, they rented a farm near Java and resided there for
four years, after which they moved to a farm north of Selby, where they lived
until 1943, when they retired and moved to Selby.

Mr. Rosin passed away Dec. 1952. Mrs. Rosin lived in Selby until her death Nov.
1968.

Their five children were Tillie (William) Sauer, John, William, Clara (Harold)
Fiedler of Aberdeen, and Fred. They had 16 grandchildren.

        George W. and Mary Anna (Zindel) Ryan
George W. Ryan was born in Fairview, Erie County, PA, on Jan. 30, 1851. He was

State Normal School in PA and the National Normal School at Lebanon, OH. He
taught 13 terms in PA. On June 14, 1881, he married Mary Anna Zindel, who was
born Mar. 12, 1854, at Tionesta, Forest County, PA, to Conrad and Elizabeth
(Babendorf) Zindel. A daughter, Mabel Abigail, was born Apr. 19, 1882. George
sold his farm in Erie County Apr. 1, 1883 and started for Dakota Territory.

(Photo:) Mary Anna Ryan

From the Diary of Geo. W. Ryan:
  Apr. 17  Tuesday, 1883: Started for Dakota Territory.
  Apr. 18  On the road. Arrived at Chicago at 8 a.m. Left Chicago at 9 a.m.
  Apr. 20  Friday: Arrived at Ordway, D.T. Then went to Aberdeen. Visited R.E.
           Kirk. Put up at Park House at $2 a day.
  Apr. 24  Started for Swan Lake.
  Apr. 25  On the road to Swan Lake.
  Apr. 28  Saturday: Arrived at Swan Lake, or Theodore, at 5 o'clock a.m. The
           whole town consists of one tent and two small shanties. Met R.E.
           Kirk. Squatted at, or settled on, Section 25 Town 122 Range 75. I
           took SE Quarter, Geo. Zindel the NE Quarter, J. Chisholm the NW
           Quarter, and commenced our improvement in Walworth County, Dakota
           Territory, April 28, 1883.
  May 1    Plowing and building sod house.
  May 2    At work at our sod houses and dugouts.
  May 7    Monday: I got ready to start for Aberdeen. We attended meeting at the
           town. Rev. Johnson preached. This was the second meeting at the town
           of Theodore.

Aberdeen was a little frontier town with streets full of mud, no sidewalks, with
only some planks scattered around. The sod house near Theodore was built by
digging down about three feet and building up with sod. Mrs. Ryan and their
daughter, Mabel, came to Dakota in June 1885. Mr. Ryan purchased two sections SE
of Java, one of which is the present Wayne Schnaible farm.

George W. Ryan represented Campbell, Walworth, Potter, Hyde, and Hand counties
in the last territorial legislature in Bismarck, D.T., in 1889. He was Auditor
of Walworth County from 1903 to 1907, at Bangor. The Ryan family lived in Bangor
during this time, later moving their house into Java. He was elected State
Senator in 1911, serving Walworth and Edmunds counties for two terms. He
belonged to the Farmers Alliance, a fraternal Equitable Union, which faded away;
was a charter member of the Knights of the Maccabees; a stockholder in the
Walworth County Building Assn.; a charter member of the Java Equity Exchange;
secretary/treasurer of the Equity Union; and president of the elevator company.
Mr. Ryan was also president of the Java Presbyterian Cemetery Assn., and served
26 years as treasurer of Ryan School District.

Mary Anna and George had five children, two of whom passed away in infancy.
Mabel, born in PA, married Robert Wagy in 1899. They had 15 children. Mabel
passed away in 1967 and is buried in the Presbyterian Cemetery east of Java.
Ethel E. was born Oct. 1, 1886, in Walworth County, D.T., on her father's farm
SE of Java. She completed the 8th grade and then attended Normal Teachers
College in Aberdeen, after which she taught several terms of school in the Swan
Lake School. She married Peter L. Nies, son of Charles and Louisa Nies, in 1911.
They had eight children. Ethel passed away in 1974 and is buried beside her
husband in the cemetery SW of Selby. (See Family History) Helen Belle was born
Aug. 23, 1890, attended high school in Java, and was the first to graduate in
the old school in 1909. She also attended Normal Teachers College and taught at
Ryan, Spring Valley and Swan Lake rural schools. Ethel and Helen were members of
the Lady Maccabees. Helen married Joseph S. Zarka on Mar. 5, 1918. They were
long-time residents of Java. Helen passed away in 1972 and is also buried beside
her husband, in the Presbyterian Cemetery east of Java.

The Ryan house that was moved from Bangor into Java in about 1908 is still
standing. Marge and Rueben Boehler and family lived in the house for many years.
Marge is a granddaughter of George Ryan. Pete and Ethel (Ryan) Nies occupied the
house until their deaths, and it is now the home of Iris Neumiller.

Mary Anna (Zindel) Ryan passed away Feb. 2, 1933 and George W. passed away Nov.
18, 1938. Both are buried in the Presbyterian Cemetery east of Java.

        Reinhold and Katie (Sauer) Sackman
Reinhold Sackman married Katie Sauer, daughter of Christian and Louise
(Fiechtner) Sauer, on Oct. 13, 1931. They farmed in the Java area for 14 years.
To supplement their income, Katie did sewing, house-cleaning and baby sitting.
In 1945, they purchased a house in Java and Reinhold started working for the
railroad. Katie began working as a clerk at the sale barns in Selby, Herreid,
Gettysburg and Linton, ND. Later, she was employed as a head cook at the Java
school, retiring after seven years. Katie was a very active member of St. Paul
Lutheran Church in Java, where she served the American Lutheran Church Women as
president and treasurer. She belonged to the Altar Guild and sang in the church
choir for 50 years. She also was the Sunday school treasurer for 17 years.

(Photo:) Katie and Reinhold Sackman

Reinhold passed away Sept. 10, 1985. Katie continued to live in Java until 1996,
when she entered the Mobridge Care Center. Katie passed away Oct. 6, 1998, at
the age of 93.

        Herman and Emma (Leidholdt) Sackman
Herman Sackman was born Oct. 30, 1909, at the homestead west of Bowdle, to

Boeing Aircraft and later went to work as Maintenance Supervisor for the Wichita
Board of Education. They retired to Mobridge in 1972. Herman passed away on

(Photo:) Linda, Dennis, Della, Myrna, Emma and Herman Sackman

        Christian and Louise (Fiechtner) Sauer
Christian Sauer was born Sept. 6, 1878, in Bersola, South Russia, the first son
of Christian Sauer, Sr., a carpenter, and his wife, Carolina Fiechtner. Very
early in his life the family moved from Bersola to Hoffnungstal, where young
Christ was baptized. A later move was made to Kassel, where he received his
religious instruction and was confirmed at 14.

(Photo:) Christian and Louise Sauer

In 1891, the elder Christian passed away. Two years later, Caroline Sauer, with
her sons, Christ and Jacob, immigrated to the U.S. Their first location was
Bridgewater, SD, where they stayed just four months, relocating to a farm three
miles north of Java. They stayed here for a short time, but a transient life
seemed inevitable for this family, and they moved again.

The next move, in 1894, was to Santa Rosa, CA. They stayed there for several
years, and the widowed mother remarried. In 1897, they returned to Walworth
County and homesteaded land six miles SE of Java.

During these years, Christ was employed at various neighbors' farms. It was
while helping in this way that a serious accident occurred that had some
pleasant consequences. A barn, containing horses, was afire and Christ bravely
attempted their rescue, incurring first-degree burns on his hands, and lesser
burns on other parts of his body. He was taken to the home of Mr. and Mrs.
Gottlieb Fiechtner and was nursed by their daughter, Louise. She became his
bride in 1901.

Christ and Louise homesteaded the farm six miles east of Java, and encountered
the severe trials and hard times familiar to most pioneer families of this
period.

During those years, there was never-ending, back breaking work to do, and a
farmer had to be skilled in many trades if his farm was to prosper. Christ met
the requirements with capable versatility. He had learned from his father the
basics of carpentry; he could butcher meat to the satisfaction of his neighbors;
and proved himself many times as a competent emergency dentist.

Although the farm demanded long hours and hard work, the spiritual life was not
neglected. Christ served as a deacon in the church, and in the absence of the
minister would read the sermons and conduct the service.

Christ and Louise were blessed with a family of six children: Rose (Christ)
Sulzle was born in 1902. She had five children and 19 grandchildren. Christ,
Jr., was born 1903 and had six children and 15 grandchildren. Katie, born in
1905, married Reinhold Sackman. William, born in 1907, farmed the land
homesteaded by his father. He married Tillie Rosin and they had four children
and 15 grandchildren. Louise, born in 1908, arrived in the world under unique
circumstances. Assisting her mother during the birth was her great-grandmother,
Louise Spiry, for whom she was named. Louise married John Rosin of Selby and had
two children and three grandchildren. Viola, born in 1915, married Henry Humann
(deceased) of Eureka, and they had five children and six grandchildren. Viola
resides in Timber Lake, and her 2nd husband, Alf Malloy, is deceased.

Christ Sauer was active in community affairs and enjoyed the high regard of his
neighbors. He lived a full and productive life until his death, Nov. 6, 1933.

His widow stayed on the farm with her son William and his family until 1935, at
which time she married Adolph Stangl of Java. Mr. Stangl died in 1968, and
Louise Sauer Stangl is also deceased.

        William and Tillie (Rosin) Sauer
William Sauer was born July 27, 1907, on the family farm east of Java, to
Christian and Louise (Fiechtner) Sauer. He married Mathilda Rosin, daughter of
William and Dorothea Rosin of Selby, on Oct. 1, 1929. The couple had four
children: Raymond married Gay Sizemore and is a retired project manager of
Phillips Petroleum. They live in West Columbia, TX, and have four children and
eight grandchildren; Marilyn married Clarence Bauman and is retired from the
restaurant business. They live in Bismarck, ND, and have four children and three
grandchildren; Donald married Helen McDaniel and operates a kennel business on
the original Sauer farm. They have four children and five grandchildren; Velma
married Larry Bonen and operates a collectibles business. They live in Bowdle
and have three children and six grandchildren.

William farmed the land homesteaded by his parents, until his death in 1991. His
wife, Tillie Rosin Sauer, resides in Java. The farm remains in the family and is
operated by their son, Don. Their four children, 15 grandchildren and 22 great-
grandchildren reaped the benefits of the disciplined work ethic William had
learned from his own parents. The grandchildren are pursuing careers in
business, teaching, music and education in SD, ND, SC, NM and TX. The good
example of their grandparents' devotion and hard work remains as a strong
influence in their lives.

        Jacob and Frieda (Wolff) Sauer
Jacob Sauer was born on Jan. 21, 1890, at Hoffnungstal, South Russia, the son of
Christian and Carolina (Fiechtner) Sauer. His father passed away when Jacob was
two years old. Shortly after his death, Carolina, with her two children, Jacob
and Christian II, came to America in 1892, and lived with her father and mother
for a number of years.

(Photo:) Jacob and Frieda Sauer

Jacob grew to manhood while living in the Java area, where he stayed with his
older brother, Christian II, and his family. On Nov. 15, 1910, Jacob married
Frieda Wolff, daughter of Matheus G. and Fredricka (Jenner) Wolff, who was born
on Dec. 21, 1888, at Marienberg, South Russia. Frieda came to America with her
parents, who homesteaded two miles NE of Java.

The young couple moved on a farm near her parents, which was then the Link
Hughes homestead. Farming and raising livestock was their livelihood, and this
young couple endured many hardships. Three boys were born to Jacob and Frieda
while living on this farm. Five years later, the couple moved on a farm NW of
Java, where a fourth son was born. Three years later, misfortune struck the
family when Jacob passed away. Shortly after Jacob's death, Frieda and her four
small children moved to Java, where she purchased a home. Frieda encountered
many conflicts trying to support her children. She became a seamstress and
provided her family with all the necessities. They all received their education
at the Java Public School. Later, her sons married and left to make their homes
elsewhere. Jacob and Frieda's children are:

Gerhardt, born May 1, 1912, married Josephine Dusel and resided at Eugene, OR.
They had two sons, Roger, and Dennis (deceased), who was in the service and died
of a drowning accident while stationed at Seattle, WA. Gerhardt is deceased.
Arnold, born June 16, 1913, married Ellen Aman and lived at Minneapolis, MN.
They had two sons, Loren of Fargo, ND and Gerald, and one daughter, Sharon
Hartman of Minneapolis. Ellen Aman Sauer is deceased. Walter, born Dec. 16,
1914, married Lois Best and resides at Bellevue, WA. They have one son, Robert.
Herbert, born May 8, 1917, married Leota Wolf. Herbert is deceased. They had one
son, Jim, and one daughter, Lynda (Jim) Burh.

        John and Barbara (Mutschler) Schadler
John Schadler was born Jan. 28, 1891, in McPherson County, and grew up in the
Eureka area. He managed grain elevators in Eureka, Hillsview and Goodrich, ND,
before coming to Java in 1928, to manage the Bagley Elevator. When that closed
in the Thirties, he opened a private Phillips 66 gas station. When the Java Co-
op went into the gas and fuel business, he managed the station and later, the
bulk truck delivery. He and his wife operated a cream-buying service for several
years. He later worked at a lumberyard in Selby, until illness forced his
retirement. He served on the Java City Council and was treasurer of St. Paul
Lutheran Church.

(Photo:) John and Barbara Schadler

On June 27, 1916, John married Barbara Mutschler at Eureka. Barbara was born in
McPherson County on Mar. 18, 1895. She was a homemaker, active in the Ladies'
Aid of her church, and a member of the West Side Sewing Club.

John died Dec. 21, 1965 and Barbara died Feb. 1, 1975. They had two children:

Herbert, born at Eureka on Mar. 19, 1917, graduated from Java High School in
1935 and attended USD at Vermillion for two years. He taught schools and coached
basketball before and after serving in the Army Air Corps during World War II.
He owned a grocery store in Tolley, ND, and was postmaster there and at New
Town, ND, until he retired. He married Minerva Schammel in 1942 and Mellicent
Helsted in 1966, both deceased. He is living at Minot, ND. There are two
children from the first marriage - Steven of Minot, and Pamela (Ed) Willet of
Omaha, NE, and three grandchildren.

Viola, born at Goodrich, ND on Jan. 28, 1922, married Gerhardt Fiedler. (See
Family History)

        Jacob and Katherine (Zweigardt) Schafer
Jacob Schafer was born in Russia in 1877, and came to the U.S. with his parents
and family at the age of 13. They settled in the Pierre area. Several years
later, they moved to a homestead east of Java, where they lived in a sod house.
He met a schoolteacher, Katherine Zweigardt, and married her a few years later.
His parents and brothers and sisters moved to Alberta, Canada, but Jacob and his
bride moved to Java, where he operated a jewelry and clock repair shop. He was
also the Java Sheriff for some years. While in Java, four children were born.
Frederick died at 10 months, Rosina only lived a few days, and Gerhart and Emma
grew to adulthood. The family moved to Tolstoy to operate a lumberyard. There,
two more were added to the family. Loretta died soon after birth and Ella was
born in 1918. In the fall of 1918, the family moved back to the Java area, where
they farmed. They attended Hoffungstahl Lutheran Church. In 1923, they moved to
a farm a mile east of Java and joined the Lutheran Church, where they were
members until Jacob's death, in 1953.

While on the farm, Jacob supplied the Java residents with water, using a 250-
gallon tank and a team of horses. He hauled water from his well and filled their
cisterns, which had a tendency to get dry during that time. He received $2 a
load, delivering in fair weather or during snowstorms.

(Photo:) Jacob and Katie Schafer

Emma Schafer graduated in 1927 and married George Goetz. George operated a dray
line with his brother, Fred. Four children were born to George and Emma.
Kenneth, Carol, Betty and Gary. The Goetz family moved to Onida and while they
were there, Emma passed away. The four children returned to Java to live with
their grandparents, Jacob and Katherine Schafer. George was killed in an
accident. Kenneth graduated from Java High School and attended NSTC. He then was
in the Air Force, where he spent time in Germany. After his term in the service,
he returned to Madison, WI, where he attended the U of WI and became a doctor,
specializing in heart research. He now lives in Kansas City, KS and has received
many awards overseas. Carol and Betty moved to Aberdeen to live with their aunt,
Ella Schafer Buechler; Gary remained in Java until 1956, when he and his
grandmother moved to Aberdeen to be near Ella. Gary had his trek in the Army and
now resides in Stillwater, OK, where he is Manager of Mercury Motors.

Ella graduated from Java High School in 1936. In 1940, she married Ted Buechler,
who passed away in 1963. She married Matt Thomas in 1974, and they farmed near
Westport, until they retired in 1972 and moved to Aberdeen, where they still
reside.

Gerhart married Rose Goetz, sister of Emma's husband. He worked as a meat cutter
for Hepper's Market in Java. They later moved to Watford City, ND, and operated
their own Meat and Grocery Market. They have one son, Delbert, who resides in
Watford City with his wife. Gerhart passed away in 1989 and Rose still lives in
her own home in Watford City.
