        Jacob and Margaret (Rosin) Schlaht
Jacob Schlaht was born Sept. 6, 1873, in the village of Neu-Gluckstal, Odessa
District, South Russia, the son of Michael and Magdalena Opp Schlaht.

In 1885, young Jacob left South Russia with his parents and brothers and
sisters, and immigrated to America, settling on a homestead SW of Eureka, Dakota
Territory.

Hardships were great during those first years in a new land, coupled with a
six-year drought in the 80's and 90's; yet the family survived. During this
period, Jacob grew to young manhood and, early in 1902, along with brothers,
George and John, established a business in the booming new town of Java, the
business being a saloon, pool hall, and refreshment parlor, known as Schlaht
Brothers.

(Photo:) Jacob and Margaret Schlaht

On July 18, 1905, Jacob was united in marriage with Margaret Rosin, second
eldest daughter of Mr. and Mrs. John Rosin of near Java, with the Rev. George
Kirchdoerfer performing the ceremony, at Java.

In June of 1907, the Schlaht Bros., Jacob and John, built a new, modern business
building, and remodeled an existing building, adding up-to-date fixtures, and
generally expanding the business. They completed it just in time to hold a Grand
Ball in conjunction with the usually fine and gala Fourth of July celebration,
staged by the City of Java. Also in July 1907, Mr. and Mrs. Schlaht began
building a fine new residence in the east part of town.

On Jan. 23, 1909, the partnership of Schlaht Brothers was dissolved, and Jacob
continued the saloon business until Feb. 25, 1910, when he sold his business
holdings in Java.

The family remained in Java until 1911, when Jacob and Margaret moved to a farm
in Campbell County, 9 miles east of Mound City, and resided there until 1939,
when they moved to Eureka. In 1944, they again moved, this time to Aberdeen.
Later, however, Jacob was forced to retire by an increasingly painful hip
ailment.

The family circle was broken on Dec. 9, 1955, when Margaret passed away, at the
age of 71. She was born Nov. 8, 1884, at Scotland, Dakota Territory, and grew to
young womanhood in the Bowdle and Java areas. Jacob remained in Aberdeen, living
in the family residence until his passing on Apr. 11, 1958, reaching the age of
85.

Margaret and Jacob were the parents of two children, Alvina Bender of Aberdeen,
and Edmund Schlaht, both deceased. There are two grandchildren - Mrs. Adam Lutz
of near Artas, and LeRoy Bender of Java.

Jacob and Helen (Schuh) Schlaht
Jacob Schlaht was born on a farm about 15 miles NE of Java, where he grew to
manhood and farmed with his parents. In 1917, he was united in marriage to Helen
Schuh, who was born Mar. 3, 1897. She grew to womanhood in the Java area.  After
their marriage, they made their home in MT, in the Miles City area, where they
lived for some time. Three sons, Wilbur, deceased, Robert, and Reuben were born
to them. After a time, the family left the farm and moved to CA. Jacob and Helen
are both deceased.

(Photo:) Jacob and Helen Schlaht

        August C. and Ottilie (Bauer) Schlepp
August C. Schlepp was born on a farm five miles north of Java on Aug. 20, 1890,
to Karl and Katherine Schlepp. He moved to Java at the age of 18 and worked for
Bauer and Stoller General Merchandise for two years. He then entered Molar
Barber College in Minneapolis, MN, graduating as a master barber in 1910. He
operated a recreation parlor and barbershop for many years, converting it to a
drug store and barbershop in 1927.

(Photo:) August C. and Ottilie Schlepp

During his lifetime, he was active in many civic affairs, serving as treasurer
of the Java School District, City Assessor, City Auditor, and City Mayor.

He was instrumental in obtaining the waterworks and sewer systems in Java during
his term as Mayor. He also served as president of the Java Chamber of Commerce,
treasurer of St. Paul Lutheran Church for many years and, in 1950, was the
chairman of the executive committee for Java's Golden Jubilee Festival. In 1961,
he was elected Chairman of the Walworth County Executive Committee for the
Dakota Territory Centennial.

In 1956, he was elected Walworth County Treasurer and served for two terms, and
as Walworth County Register of Deeds for two terms, until Dec. 31, 1964, when he
retired.

August C. was an accomplished violinist, playing with various musical groups and
organizations during his lifetime. He conducted the school band and orchestra
for a number of years, directed the municipal band for 20 years, and was a
charter member of the Civic Symphony Orchestra at Aberdeen, serving many years
as concertmaster.

August and Ottilie (Bauer) Schlepp were united in marriage on Apr. 21, 1912, at
the Congregational Church in Java. They resided in Java all of their married
life. August passed away June 23, 1966 and Ottilie passed away Apr. 6, 1971.

They had six children, all of whom are deceased. Lenore married Jack Bieber and
they had James, Jeanette, Sally, Peggy, Julie and Lenora Kay. Gilbert G. married
LaRayne Job and they had Barbara and Carolyn. (See Family History) Percy married
Vera Schanzenbach and they had Dennis. Lawrence married Joyce Vojta and they had
Kenneth, Rebecca, Greg, Debbie, Connie and Todd. Juliet married Milton Wendling
and they had Michael, Jackie and Elizabeth. Kathleen Mewing has Paul, Colleen
and Glen.

        Gilbert G. and LaRayne (Job) Schlepp
Gilbert Schlepp was born Aug. 11, 1918, to August C. and Tillie (Bauer) Schlepp.
He attended the Java Public School, graduating with the class of 1935. Gilbert
was employed at the family-owned drugstore in Java. He enlisted in the U.S. Navy
in Dec. 1942, the day after Pearl Harbor, and received his training at Great
Lakes Naval Station. He served in the Medical Corp, aboard a hospital ship in
the Pacific, until his discharge in the fall of 1946. Gilbert played trumpet
with a Naval band during the term of his service. He had played for many dances
in the Java area in earlier years.

Gilbert married LaRayne Job of Java on June 8, 1947, at St. Paul Lutheran Church
in Java.

LaRayne was born north of Java to John and Justina (Doerr) Job. She attended
country school and graduated from Java High School in 1945. LaRayne was employed
at the Java Cafe, owned by her sisters, Tillie and Minnie Job, while attending
high school. She worked in Washington, D.C. for the FBI, as a typist.

Gilbert and LaRayne made their home in Java and owned and operated the G & L
Store for 10 years. Gilbert also served as part-time band instructor from 1950-
1957. He was appointed Walworth County Treasurer and served in that capacity for
a short time, when he was hired by the State Department of Legislative accounts.
He held this position until his death on Jan. 23, 1973.

LaRayne was employed in the Register of Deeds office of Walworth County. She
also worked as a legal secretary at the Robbins and VonWald Law Office at Selby
for a number of years, until her appointment as Walworth County Clerk of Courts
in 1975. She served in this capacity until her retirement in 1984.

Two daughters were born to Gilbert and LaRayne.

Barbara Ann graduated from Java High School in 1970, and from NSU with a degree
in music. She later obtained her Masters of Business Administration degree from
Moorhead State University. She is married to Michael Carroll and resides in MN.

Carolyn Jane graduated from Java High School in 1973, and from SDSU at
Brookings, with a BS degree in Nursing. She has followed that profession and is
presently pursuing a Nurse Practitioner degree. Carolyn married Joel Jorgenson
and lives in Willmar, MN. They have Katie and Zachary.

(Photo:) Carolyn, Barbara, LaRayne and Gilbert Schlepp

        John J. and Magdalena (Miller) Schlepp Sr.
John J. Schlepp, Sr., born in Hoffnungstal, South Russia, in 1837, he grew to
manhood and was united in marriage to Magdelena Miller, who was born in 1840,
also in the South Russian area.

(Photo:) John J. Schlepp, Sr. Family

This young couple made their home in South Russia, where John worked in the
carpenter trade and Magdelena was a midwife, a service she continued for the
early pioneers after migrating to America.

In 1889, John, Magdalena and sons David and Adolph, and a married daughter,
Fredricka (Schlepp) Schuh, her husband and a son, John, left their home in
Russia and migrated to America. They landed in New York, made their way
westward, and homesteaded in the Java area, where farming became their
livelihood.

In 1909, the Schlepps purchased a home in Java, where they retired until their
death. John, Sr., passed away in 1913 and Magdalena died Mar. 27, 1927.

        John J. and Helena (Doebele) Schlepp Jr.
John J. Schlepp, Jr., was the eldest son of John J. and Magdalena Schlepp Sr. He
was born May 28, 1863, at Hoffnungstal, South Russia. On Dec. 12, 1885, John was
married to Helena Doebele at Kloestitz, South Russia. In June 1889, John, his
wife Helena, their eldest daughter Pauline, and their infant son immigrated to
the U.S. The son died enroute and was buried at sea.

John was one of the earlier settlers in the Dakotas. The family homesteaded in
Emmons County near Linton, ND. In 1891, they moved to Walworth County and made
their home on a farm seven miles NE of Java.

(Photo:) John J. Schlepp, Jr. Family

To the John J. Schlepp, Jr., family 13 children were born: Pauline (Reinhold)
Naasz; the infant son who died at sea; Helena (Rudolph) Walther; Samuel married
Nathlia Schlepp, deceased, then married Christina Wolf, deceased, then married
Magdelena Goetz; Magdelena (John) Pfaff; Rosie (Fred) Obenauer; Edward married
Justina Wolf; Lydia (Adolph) Pfaff; John Schlepp married Elizabeth Wolf; Anna
(Mike) Schmierer; Kathryn (Ted) Spiry; Jacob married Elizabeth George; and
Mathilda (Benjamin) Halverson Webber.

John and Helena and family resided on their homestead seven miles north of Java
for 33 years. He had filed his claim in 1891 and to retain their claim,
improvements had to be made. John and his family plowed the fields with a one-
horse plow. They had to dig a well by hand with a spade and build a sod house
for shelter. In order to obtain supplies and materials necessary for
improvements on the land, they traveled by wagon to Eureka, the nearest town.

In 1922, the parents retired from active farming and moved to Java, where they
made their home. The homestead was left to sons, Edward and John, to continue
farming.

The Schlepps celebrated their Golden Wedding Anniversary in 1936, after having
survived the many hardships and the Depression. They contributed a great deal to
the settlement of the Java area before John died on Apr. 6, 1938 and his wife,
Helena, died in 1952.

        Samuel Schlepp
Samuel Schlepp was the oldest son of 13 children born to John J. and Helena
(Doebele) Schlepp, Jr. He was born in rural Walworth County, Java, on Dec. 31,
1891, attended rural school in this area, and married Nathalia Schlepp on Jan.
25, 1914. She died on Oct. 27, 1918 and he then married Christina (Wolff) Aman
on Sept. 21, 1919. He helped raise her small son, Erven Aman. On Apr. 21, 1928,
twins Clarence Richard and Gloria Mureen were born to them on a farm one-half
mile south of Java.

Life was difficult because there were droughts and hailstorms. Sam worked for
the WPA when the road was built south of Java. Sam and his wife worked side by
side in the fields. After retiring from fieldwork at the end of the day, there
were cows to be milked. The laundry also had to be washed and this was done on a
washboard, as there was no electricity and there were no washing machines.
Clothes were ironed with flat irons that were heated on the cook stove. All of
these chores had to be done in the evening. Baking bread and all other baking
had to be done in the evening, in the cook-stove oven. There was always a large
garden that supplied vegetables for the winter months. There was no
refrigeration, so vegetables had to be canned or dried. Hogs, ducks, geese and
chickens supplied the meat for the family. Cream and eggs were sold to purchase
the other necessary supplies. Sam had a threshing machine and did threshing for
other farmers.

Christina passed away Jan. 10, 1954. Sam then married Magdalena (Goetz) Schlepp,
on Sept. 29, 1957. They purchased a home in Mobridge. She passed away Nov. 3,
1980. Sam farmed in the Java area most of his life. He became ill and passed
away Nov. 24, 1983. He had three brothers, John J., Edward and Jacob, and eight
sisters, Paulina Naasz, Helena Walther, Magdalena Pfaff, Rosie Obenauer, Lydia
Pfaff, Anna Schmierer, Kathryn Spiry and Mathilda Halverson Weber.

(Photo:) Erven and Violet Aman Family

Erven J. Aman was born in the Java area on Nov. 14, 1916, to John E. and
Christine (Wolff) Aman. His father passed away when Erven was very young and his
mother married Sam Schlepp, who helped raise Erven. Violet Neumiller was born
May 26, 1924, to Christ and Louise Neumiller, at Heaton, ND. Erven and Violet
were married Sept. 20, 1949. Their children are: Warren, born Apr. 20, 1950,
graduated from Java High School in 1968. He married Louella Goedtke on Jan. 13,
1979, and they have Terri and Michael and live in Volga, SD; Elaine was born
Feb. 2, 1952 and graduated from Java High School in 1970. She married David
Morrison and they had Jason. She married Allan Schiebner on Sept. 13, 1980 and
they live in Yuma, AZ and Ouray, CO; Anita, born Feb. 20, 1955, married Myron
Rau on Aug. 7, 1976, and they have Kristin and Adam. They live in Pierre; Leslie
was born Mar. 4, 1958 and married Brenda Dybdahl on June 30,l 1990. They are the
parents of Drew and Mitchell and live in Gayville, SD; Norma was born Dec. 21,
1960 and married Gregg Wolff on May 22, 1982. They have Joshua and Nicole and
live in Watertown.

        Emanuel and Lydia (Schuh) Schlepp
Emanuel Schlepp, born in Hoffnungstal, South Russia on May 11, 1895, came to
America with his parents, Jacob and Katharina Schlepp. The family came to the SD
and homesteaded three miles NE of Bowdle.

(Photo:) Emanuel and Lydia Schlepp

On July 24, 1918, Emanuel was drafted into the Army, serving in the Belgium and
France sector during World War I. A few years after his discharge, he married
Lydia Schuh, who was born Sept. 3, 1903, to John and Fredericka Schuh, at their
home located five miles NE of Java.

After their marriage, Lydia and Emanuel lived in Bowdle, where he was employed.
Three years later they moved to Mahto, SD, where they farmed for 14 years. They
returned to the Java area and farmed five miles NE of Java. A few years later
they bought a farm four miles east of Java, where they farmed until 1952. They
sold their farm and moved to Java, where they purchased a home. In 1953, they
purchased Schlepp's Cafe, which they operated until 1960, when they retired.
Four daughters were born to the Schlepp family; they all received their
education in the Java school.

Agnes married Virgil Haskell (deceased) and had four children (See Family
History).

Juanita attended rural schools and Java High School, graduating in 1946. She
attended National Business College in Rapid City, after which she went to work
for International Harvester Company in Aberdeen, where she an employee, Bill
Johnson. Bill was born and raised in Scranton, ND, and served in the Air Force
as a P51 fighter pilot and instructor. Juanita and Bill were married in 1949 and
lived in Aberdeen until 1957, during which time Juanita began her Civil Service
career with Internal Revenue Service. They were transferred to Oakes, ND, by
IHC, where they lived until 1960, when Bill entered Civil Service and they moved
to Albuquerque, NM. With the exception of about three years, when they were
transferred to Washington, D.C. with Bill's job, they lived in Albuquerque until
they moved to Rapid City to retire, in 1984. Bill passed away in 1987; Juanita
lives in the home they built outside of Rapid City.

(Photo:) Juanita and Bill Johnson

Sallie married Harvey Weisgram and they live in Bismarck, ND. (See Family
History)

Gail married Robert Goeman on Jan. 3, 1960. She has worked for Aman Collection
Service, Inc., for the past 30 years, as Administration Manager. Bob is
self-employed as an insurance agent, and has sold for TMG Life Insurance Co.,
for 36 years. They have resided in Aberdeen for the past 35 years. Two children
were born to this marriage, a son, Michael Anthony, born July 15, 1960, and a
daughter, Mary Gail, born Sept. 3, 1963. Mike attended NSU with a basketball
scholarship. He married Bobby Hladky on Aug. 23, 1996. They have a daughter,
Taylor, and a son, Nicholas. They reside in Aberdeen, where Mike is a Regional
Manager for Budget Motels, Inc., and Bobby is an RN for Brown County Health.
Daughter Mary was married to Michael Prior on May 18, 1985. She and her husband
both graduated with RN degrees from SDSU at Brookings. After working as a
Critical Care Nurse in Sioux City, IA,  Mary went back to school and graduated
in 1995, with honors, from Arizona State University, with a Law degree. They
reside in Phoenix, where she specializes in malpractice law with the firm of
O'Connor and Cavanaugh. Mike is a self-employed Nurse Anesthetist currently
working with Indian Health at Tuba City, AZ.

        Elmer and Erna (Fiechtner) Schlepp
Erna E. Fiechtner, daughter of Gottlieb IV and Christina (Naasz) Fiechtner, was
born on Aug. 1, 1922. They lived on a farm east of Java, which is currently
owned by Marlow and Marge Schaffer. Erna attended Java Public School. During her
senior year, she worked at the Java Printing office through a school program,
and graduated in 1941.

Erna married Elmer W. Schlepp on Sept. 11, 1942. Elmer, born June 15, 1921, was
the oldest son of eight children born to Adam and Eugenia (Dubs) Schlepp. They
farmed in the Bowdle area. Elmer served in World War II in the Pacific Theatre,
which included Australia, the Philippine Islands and Japan. During the three
years that Elmer was overseas, Erna lived with her parents and worked at A.C.
Schlepp's drug store.

(Photo:) Erna and Elmer Schlepp

Elmer returned home from the war and the couple moved on a farm 10 miles south
of Java. It was a struggle during those years. In 1949, they moved on a farm SW
of Bowdle. In 1947, the couple was blessed with a baby girl they named Marlys.
Their son, Doug, was born in 1952. Marlys married Neal Pfitzer.

In 1959, the Schlepp family moved to Java to operate the cafe that they had
bought from Elmer's uncle "Slippery". Elmer and Erna operated Schlepp's Cafe for
25 years, retiring in 1984. Elmer and Erna have participated in community
projects while living in Java. Elmer served on the building committee when St.
Paul Lutheran Church was built. He also served on the Church Council and was
church and city treasurer. Erna was on the city council. The couple has served
on several boards and committees. They now enjoy wintering in CO and AZ, near
their children and grandchildren.

Douglas and LaNette (Hettich) Schlepp reside at Tucson, AZ. They have two
children, Larissa age 18, and Jonathan age 14. Douglas and LaNette both
graduated from Java High School in 1970.

Douglas attended SDSM&T and graduated in 1974 with a BS Degree in Metallurgical
Engineering. He also attended the executive program at Stanford Business School.
Doug was a highly regarded basketball player at SDSM&T, and still holds a number
of records at the school. He went to work for Krebs Engineers in 1974 as a sales
engineer. Doug held various positions at Krebs Engineers during a 24-year
career, culminating with his promotion to President, CEO, and Chairman of the
Board of Directors in 1994. Krebs Engineers is a 52-year manufacturing company
with its corporate headquarters in Tucson and various international subsidiary
companies scattered throughout the world.

LaNette attended NSU and graduated in 1972 with a BA Degree in Business. LaNette
worked for Hoya Optics as electro optics manager for six years prior to starting
her own bookkeeping business in 1979. LaNette sold a part of her business, when
the family relocated from the San Francisco Bay Area to Tucson in 1995, but
continues to travel to the San Francisco Bay Area monthly, and is actively
involved in the business to this day.

LaNette and Doug have two children. Larissa Anne was born at Stanford, CA, on
Dec. 22, 1980. She attended Menlo High School in Menlo Park, CA, and graduated
in 1998 from Catalina Foothills High School in Tucson. She is currently a
student at the U of AZ. During high school, Larissa was actively involved in
soccer, music, and drama. Larissa is undecided about her major but has strong
interests in foreign languages and music. She currently sings with two of the
college choirs. Jonathan Adam was born at Stanford, CA, on May 17, 1984. He is
currently attends Palo Verde Christian School in Tucson, AZ. Jonathan has been
active in soccer, baseball, and basketball, and is currently on the Palo Verde
junior varsity basketball team. He also enjoys skiing, snowboarding, drawing,
music and golf but most of all, he loves animals, especially his pet cat, Ezra.

        John Schmeichel
John Schmeichel was born Jan. 6, 1859, at Gluckstal, Russia, where he grew to
manhood. He married Sophia Straub and eight children were born to this couple.
The Schmeichel family came to America and settled in the Mound City area.

(Photo:) The John Schmeichel Family

After his wife's death, John married Elizabeth Quenzer and seven children were
born to this couple. The Schmeichel family homesteaded seven miles SE of Mound
City.

In 1900, the Schmeichel family moved to Selby, where John went into partnership
with John Nusz and Albert Lang. In 1905, the family moved to Java, where John
went into partnership with Philip Spiry and owned and operated The German State
Bank. The Schmeichel family remained in Java for four years, until 1909, when
the family moved to McLaughlin, where they remained until their deaths. John
passed away Feb. 1923 and Elizabeth died in 1966.

        Michael and Katherina (Kirschenmann) Schmierer
Michael Schmierer, Sr., was born July 21, 1862, in Klein-Neudorf, Russia. His
wife, Katherina Kirschenmann, was born Aug. 8, 1866, in Neu-Gluckstal, Russia.
They were married in 1889; their first daughter, Elizabeth, was born in
Neu-Gluckstal. They came to America in 1892 and lived in Naper, NE for four
years. A son, Gustav, and a daughter, Emma, were born during this time.

In 1896, the family loaded their belongings onto one wagon and moved to SD. They
homesteaded 10 miles NE of Java, in Adams Township. The plow was unloaded to
break sod, from which the house was built. Within the next eight years, three
more sons were born - Michael, Jr., in 1898, Emil in 1902, and John in 1904.

(Photo:) Mr. and Mrs. Michael Schmierer

The family bought the Fred Eisenbeisz place and moved one-half mile farther
east. Michael, Sr., died there in 1911 and Katherina continued to live on the
farm with her children. The flu epidemic of 1918 claimed the lives of daughter,
Emma, and son, Emil.

John, their youngest son, entered the seminary and became a pastor of the
American Lutheran Church. He served parishes in both ND and SD and retired after
serving 45 years in the ministry. He was married to Marie Bieber in 1930. They
are deceased.

In 1920, Michael, Jr., married Anna Schlepp. He took over the home place and in
the course of years, a few more quarters of land were added. Katherina moved to
Bowdle, residing there until her death in 1943.

Three sons were born to Michael, Jr., and Anna: The oldest Reuben (deceased),
moved to Java, where he was married to Eileen Fiedler; Theodore, the youngest,
married Erna Goetz and moved to Aberdeen. He passed away July 1, 1962; Elmer
(deceased) married Martha Lorenz. The Schmierers also raised Alvina Walther, a
niece of Mrs. Schmierer, who came to live with them at the age of six, after her
mother, Mrs. Rudolph Walther, passed away. She married Albert Quenzer of Artas.

In Sept. 1970, the Michael Schmierers moved to Bowdle. Both are deceased.

        Karl and Elizabeth (Oster) Schnaible
Karl Schnaible was born Mar. 31, 1857 at Hoffnungstal, Bessarabia, Romania. His
wife, Elizabeth Oster, was born in the same locality. They were married Feb. 15,
1879. They wanted to get away from Russian rule, so they, with three children,
came to the U.S. in 1885. They settled on a farm near Freeman, where they lived
for four years.

In 1889, they came to Walworth County and bought land NW of Java, where they
resided for 10 years. Their first home near Java was a sod house, which was
replaced by a larger, roomy home some years later.

(Photo:) Karl Schnaible Family. Back: Christ, Pauline. Mid: Karl, Rose, Mary,
         Elizabeth. Front: Henry and Lydia

They moved to Java in 1909, where they resided until his death Aug. 1930, at the
age of 73. He was thrifty and not afraid of hard work; he had large herds of
sheep and cattle. After moving to Java, he continued to help at the farm. He was
a resident of Walworth County for 41 years.They celebrated their 40th Wedding
Anniversary in Mar. 1929.

Elizabeth Schnaible continued to live in the Java home until unable to care for
herself. She moved to the Eureka Nursing Home, where she passed away at the age
of 93.

There were 9 children in this family, and one adopted child. Three passed away
in infancy and are buried in a small family cemetery north of the original farm:
Magdalena and Elizabeth in 1895, and Henry in 1896. Christ married Magdalena
Naasz; Pauline married Fred Krause; Rose married Christ Wolf; Mary was the wife
of Emanuel Baer; Lydia married George Wolf; Henry married Elizabeth Zeller; and
Edward (adopted) married Rose Wolf.

        Christian and Magdalena (Naasz) Schnaible
Christian Schnaible was born Nov. 2, 1879, at Hoffnungstal, South Russia, a son
of Karl and Elizabeth (Oster) Schnaible. He spent his early boyhood in Russia.
At the age of five he came to the U.S. with his parents and settled near
Freeman. After five years, the family came to Walworth County and homesteaded
north of Java, where he grew up and acquired what schooling he could, which
would be equivalent to the present day third grade.

On Mar. 22, 1903, he was united in marriage to Magdalena Naasz of Java.
Magdalena was born in Hoffnungstal, South Russia on Oct. 22, 1882, where she
resided until May 5, 1893, when her parents came to the U.S. and settled on a
homestead near Java.

(Photo:) Christian and Magdalena Schnaible

Christian and Magdalena operated a grocery and dry goods store in Java for a
number of years, and in 1924, the family, now consisting of four sons, moved
onto a farm north of Java. Later in 1939, they moved back into Java because of
Magdalena's health. Christian was then employed as a carpenter for some years.
Magdalena passed away Mar. 9, 1947.

After her death, Christian continued to reside in Java, and in 1950 was given
the position as custodian of St. Paul Lutheran Church in Java, and caretaker of
the cemetery. He was conscientious in carrying out these duties until his death,
Aug. 19, 1954.

They were blessed with five children - sons Berthold, Otto, Arnold, and
Traugott, and a daughter, Delilah, who passed away in 1919 at the age of seven.

The Schnaibles were members of St. Paul Lutheran Church; Magdalena was one of
the organizers of the Ladies Aid, which is now known as WELCA. Christian was
also a member of the Java City Band.

        Berthold and Lydia (Haux) Schnaible
Berthold was born May 26, 1907, to Christian Fred and Magdalena (Naasz)
Schnaible. Berthold, better known as "Big Snip", was the oldest of three sons
and one daughter. He went to grade school in Java and then worked on the Stangl
Farm, as well as other farms, for some years when he was very young. He worked
in the shipyards and forests in WA, for a while. He was a boxer and wrestler in
his younger years and was known for his strength.

(Photo:) Berthold and Lydia Schnaible

He married Lydia Haux Jan. 20, 1935; their reception was held at the Jacob and
Margaret Haux (parents of the bride) farm and, due to blizzard conditions, they
took their guests to and from the farm by horse and sled. Lydia was born Jan. 7,
1911, to Jacob and Margaret Haux of Java. She was employed by different couples
as a cleaning lady and helped with new babies. She was very active in her
church, always donating both time and food.

Big Snip was employed by Walworth County Highway Dept. for 40 years as "Cat"
Operator and finally, as Foreman. He retired in 1969. The family continued to
live in Java. Snip was the baseball Catcher for the Java team for many years and
was always an avid baseball fan. He enjoyed playing cards and was quick to
correct anyone who made an error in playing, especially his partners.

After a stroke and surgery, Snip moved to the Selby Good Samaritan Center in
July of 1990. Lydia also was a resident for two months, and then passed away in
Sept. of 1990.

Born to this union were four children: Ruby, Roger, Ray and Bob. They had eight
grand children (two are deceased).

Ruby was born July 27, 1936, in Java, and graduated from Java High School in

now known as Norwest Bank. In 1956, Ruby and her husband, Chuck, moved to Selby
after Ruby was offered a position at the First National Bank of Selby. She
worked for this bank 39 years as bookkeeper, teller, head teller, cashier and
finally, Assistant Vice President, retiring in 1995 after 41 years in banking.
(First National Bank of Selby became a branch of Pierre in 1985 and is now
Bank West.) Ruby married Charles W. (Chuck) Birkholt in Java on June 26, 1955.
Chuck was employed at Cam Wal Electric for 45 years, retiring in June 1997. He
started in the office, became a lineman promoted to Foreman, then to Line
Superintendent, and then, General Manager in 1989. He held this position until
he retired. To their marriage one daughter was born Apr. 3, 1965 and she died at
birth. Chuck and Ruby enjoy retirement and taking care of their remaining
parents, Berthold Schnaible and Viola Birkholt, in the Selby Good Samaritan
Center.

(Photo:) Chuck and Ruby Birkholt

Roger was born June 24, 1938. He graduated from Java High School and entered the

Raymond Lee was born Sept. 12, 1944. He graduated from Java High School and

        Otto and Betty (Scott) Schnaible
Otto Schnaible was born Nov. 13, 1909, at Java, a son of Christian and Magdalena
(Naasz) Schnaible. He grew up and attended school in Java along with his
brothers, Berthold, Arnold and Traugot (deceased).

On Sept. 21, 1934, he was united in marriage to Alice Overseth, with Rev. George
Kirchdoerfer performing the ceremony at St. Paul Lutheran Church in Java. During

Two children were born to them.

(Photo:) Betty and Otto Schnaible

Dean Melvin was born on May 21, 1935, at Java. He married Maralyn Merkel of

retired after 41 years of teaching. Maralyn is employed with Adrian Public

Beverly Joyce was born Apr. 16, 1938, at Sundance, WY. She married Gary Buck of

During World War II, Otto was employed at the Kaiser Shipyard in Vancouver, WA,
until 1947, when he returned to Java. He was employed at the Java Equity
Elevator until 1951, when he became Manager of the McCabe Elevator in Java.
After the McCabe Elevator was sold, he worked at the Java Equity Oil Station
from 1959 to 1962. After working as a truck driver for Walworth County from 1962
to 1965, he later was employed as manager of the Java Equity Elevator until his
retirement in 1974. Throughout his working career, he also farmed in the Java
area until 1980.

On June 5, 1949, Otto married Elizabeth Scott of Letcher, SD. She was a former
teacher in the Java School and later, a secretary in the school for 24 years.
After their marriage, they lived in Java. Three daughters were born to this
union.

Peggy Lee was born on Oct. 26, 1949, at Mobridge. She was married to Doug Erhart
at Bismarck on Aug. 30, 1974. They have one son, Jade. Peg is employed with Job
Service ND, in Bismarck. Doug is employed with Burlington Northern Santa Fe
Railroad in Mandan.

Barbara Jean was born on Feb. 5, 1954, at Mobridge. She was married to Tom
Goehring at Java on July 28, 1973. They have two sons, Corey and Chad, and a
daughter, Christal. Barb is a Nurse at Avera St. Luke's Medical Center and Tom
is a postman for U.S. Postal Service in Aberdeen.

Ruthanne Marie was born Mar. 14, 1957, at Mobridge. She is employed as a
Probation Officer II for Clark County Nevada in Las Vegas.

The Schnaibles are members of St. Paul Lutheran Church of Java. Otto is a
charter member of St. Paul. He was chosen king of the 1998 Kuchen Festival in
Java. The Schnaibles celebrated their Golden Wedding Anniversary in 1999.

        Henry and Elizabeth (Zeller) Schnaible
Henry Schnaible was born Nov. 14, 1892, to Karl and Elizabeth (Oster) Schnaible,
on the family homestead near Java. Elizabeth Zeller was born Oct. 8, 1893, to
George and Rosina (Grenz) Zeller, on the family homestead near Sutley. They were
married Jan. 9, 1913, at Java. Henry and Elizabeth established their home on his
parents' farm when they retired and moved into Java.

Henry and Elizabeth seeded, harvested and tended the livestock together. They
prospered. Then came the Thirties with drought, dust storms and grasshoppers,
causing crop failures. They were grateful to harvest enough grain for seed the
next year. The pastureland dried to a crisp and soon, the livestock dwindled
down to a few. The family's livelihood depended on the yield of the garden, and
money from the sale of eggs and cream.

(Photo:) Elizabeth and Henry Schnaible

Most of the Java residents depended upon cisterns filled with water, caught from
a house rooftop, for their water supply. When the water was consumed, they would
call Schnaibles to buy a tank full of water. Schnaibles' well water was known to
be of excellent quality. When the town people heard a bell ringing, it was Henry
driving down Java Main Street on the water wagon, pulled by his best team of
horses, with a bell attached to their best harnesses, delivering well water to
his patrons. The water income was added to the cream and egg money.

Their social life was in the home. They played and sang together. They played
games of skill. Some games were made by Elizabeth, such as nails of various
values nailed onto the end-board from an apple box, and fruit jar rings to toss.
They also had bowling pins, horseshoes, dominoes and an Old Maid deck. Their
neighbors frequently came by for a visit and a game of Whist. The most enjoyed
times were Sunday evenings, when friends came to gather around the parlor organ
for a songfest. Elizabeth also enjoyed singing in the German Church Choir. Their
sons, Richard and Clifton, did well in sports and Elizabeth and Henry cheered
and supported them through every game.

At the end of the 1930's, it rained once again. The grain and crops grew. The
wildlife and flowers came back. They prospered again.

After World War II, the R.E.A. brought electricity to the farms. This enabled
the farmers to have running water in the house, electric lights, appliances, and
much more.

In Jan. 1963, in spite of blizzards and sub-zero weather, the family from CA and
Canada came to join the Java area family and friends to help Elizabeth and Henry
celebrate their Golden Wedding.

Henry died Oct. 24, 1966. He lived his entire life on the home place. After
Henry's death, Elizabeth lived with her son, Clifton. On a quiet moonlit night
in Jan. 1967, Elizabeth's home was robbed of her prized possessions. The robbery
has never been solved. One windy summer day, Elizabeth had a mishap that broke
her hip, compelling her to live in the Good Samaritan Center in Selby, until her
death on Aug. 9, 1974.

(Photo:) Richard and Clifton

Henry and Elizabeth had two sons. Richard Karl married Beulah Swift. They had
two daughters, Patricia and Rita. After Beulah's death, Richard married Agnes
Chesky. Agnes has one son, Jack. Richard died Jan. 21, 1993. He is buried in the
Black Hills National Cemetery near Sturgis. Clifton George married Verna Pfaff.
They had two sons, Dale and Paul, and one daughter, Connie.

        Clifton and Verna (Pfaff) Schnaible
Clifton and Verna Schnaible of Java were recognized in 1992, at the SD State
Fair, for owning a 100-year farm. They received the Century Farm Award,
sponsored by the SD Dept. of Agriculture and the SD Farm Bureau, for the
Schnaible Homestead, located about a mile north of Java.

Karl Schnaible staked the original homestead in 1889. An emigrant from Odessa,
South Russia, he built a house on the same location as the present one. His son,
Henry, who was born and raised a mile north of the original house, was the
second-generation farmer.

Henry's sons, Dick and Clif, farmed the land together before Clif bought the
property. "I've farmed all of my life. I've been on this land for 69 years,"
Clif said.

Clif and Verna married in 1944, and moved to their first house on the original
homestead site in 1947. Clif said the central part of their first house was the
original house and several additions were added later. In 1961, the Schnaibles
tore down and moved another house onto the same spot. They purchased the house
from Raymond Schuh and moved it several miles.

(Photo:) The Clifton Schnaible Family

The Schnaibles operated a grain and dairy farm with about 60 cows. "We had a
diversified farm. In 1987, we quit milking, when we went into the dairy
sellout," said Clif. They began to participate in the CRP program two years ago.

Clif and Verna raised three children. The oldest son, Dale, and his wife, Cathy,
live in Belle Fourche and manage a pizza business at a truck stop. They have two
children. Briana Kindsfater of Rapid City has a daughter, Mazie. Dale and
Cathy's son, Ben, and his wife, Abbie, live in ID, and manage a pizza business.
Connie, the second child of Clif and Verna, lives in Sioux Falls, where she
teaches for the Sioux Falls School District. Their youngest son, Paul, and his
wife, Julie, live in Sioux Falls and work for City Bank.

When the Schnaibles weren't farming, they enjoyed participating in sports. Clif
started playing baseball in 1935 with the Eureka Legion team, and then joined
the Selby Legion team in 1937. He continued playing amateur baseball for many
years. He played left field and was catcher for the last 15 years. He also
helped coach Midgets, Teeners, and Junior Legion when his sons played. In 1975,
the Java Legion Team won the State B Championship, and Paul was on that team.

Connie played basketball in high school and played for four years at SDSU at
Brookings. When she was a sophomore, the team was in national competition at
Normal, IL. Clif said the competition was keen because college leagues were not
yet classified according to size, so small schools competed against the bigger
ones. The playing also was very physical, with one player receiving a
concussion.

Verna said, "We always took time for sports. I don't know how we did it."
Sometimes going to the games meant little rest at home. "If we had a nickel for
every mile we traveled for sports, we could retire," Clif had said. The
Schnaibles continued going to local games as fans and to watch their grandson
play football, basketball, and wrestling.

Clif started out farming with horses, but when the tractor arrived, he didn't
miss the horses. His favorite part of farming is cultivating corn. Clif, who has
survived cancer, misses being able to work as much as he used to. The cancer was
on his voice box, so he speaks with the help of a trachea.

Verna Pfaff Schnaible passed away on Mar. 2, 1999, and Clif continues to reside
on the farm.

        Edward and Rosina (Wolf) Schnaible
Edward Eisenbeisz Schnaible, born in Russia, came to America at the age of six.
He lost his mother on the journey across the Atlantic. The Karl Schnaible family
of rural Java adopted Edward upon his arrival to SD. Edward worked as a farmhand
most of his young, adult life. He was drafted into the military during World War
I. After his discharge from the military, Edward married Rosina Wolf, daughter
of Friedrich Wolf, Jr., of rural Java. They lived on Friedrich's farm, where
they became the parents of one son, Cornelius, and later moved to a farm near
Sitka.

(Photo:) Ed and Rosie Schnaible

Edward and Rosina farmed near Sitka until Cornelius became a young adult. They
then bought a farm north of Java, where they farmed until their retirement. They
built a home in Java and lived there until their deaths.

        Cornelius and Loretta (Schuh) Schnaible
Cornelius Schnaible, the only child of Edward and Rosina (Wolf) Schnaible,
married Loretta Schuh, the only daughter of John, Jr., and Emma (Boehler) Schuh.
She had two brothers, Ellsworth and Raymond. Three sons were born to Cornelius
and Loretta: James, Patrick, and Thomas.

James married Judith Fiedler of Java. He teaches Automotive Technology at
Western Dakota Technical Institute and Judy is a program specialist for the
Dept. of Social Services. They live and are employed in Rapid City.

Patrick, an F.A.A. certified aircraft and engine mechanic, is farming north of
Java, innovative in organic farming techniques.

(Photo:) Cornelius and Loretta Schnaible

Thomas married Kristi Giese of rural Selby. They farm north of Java and are the
fourth generation on this farm. They are the parents of two sons, Thomas J. and
Johnathan E.

        John and Mary (Weber) Schnaible Sr.
John Schnaible, Sr., was born Oct. 30, 1871, at Hoffnungstal, Bessarabia, South
Russia. On Jan. 29, 1893, John was united in marriage to Mary Weber, who was
born Jan. 26, 1873, at Kloestitz, South Russia. The young couple had two
children who died in infancy. In 1902, a daughter, Mary (W.J.) Roesler was born
in the South Russian area.

One year later, John, Sr., his wife Mary, and baby, undertook the long journey
to come to America. Influenced by his older brother, John and his family came to
Dakota Territory and came to Java, where he lived with his brother for a short
time.

The Schnaible family rented a farm east of Java, which was owned by Deable.
While making their home on this farm, two sons were added to this family. They
were John, Jr., and Oscar. A few years later they moved to a farm south of
Bowdle, where they again were engaged in farming. Another son, Emil, joined the
Schnaible family, before they moved on a farm 10 miles south of Java.

In 1911, the Schnaible family bought the Henry Baer farm, where they farmed
until they retired. Many hardships were endured during the Depression and
drought. Three more children were born: two daughters, Lily (Emanuel) Sieler,
and Olga (Oscar) Fiedler, and one son, Fred. Lily, the only child remaining of
John and Mary, is residing in Aberdeen.

John, Jr., married Erna Schlepp and they had Luella (Lou), who graduated from
Java High School in 1948. She then graduated from Rapid City Business College,
in Sept. 1949. Lou married Leo (Lee) Cyr in 1954. She held various secretarial
jobs, but stayed home until their sons, Kerry and Brian, were in college. She
then worked another 19 years before retiring, in 1996, from her position as
Accounts Payable Manager. Lee was in the U.S. Army for 20 years and then worked
with the U.S. Government in a civilian capacity. They are now enjoying their
retirement and living in Culpeper, VA.

(Photo:) Lou and Lee Cyr

In 1943, John, Sr., and Mary bought a home in Java and moved to town. John died
on May 3, 1945, and his wife, Mary, passed away five years later, on July 2,
1950.

        Oscar and Ottilie (Bieber) Schnaible
Oscar was born at home on the family farm 12 miles south of Java, to John and
Marie (Weber) Schnaible, Sr., on Dec. 28, 1906. Ottilie (Tillie) was also born
at home on the family farm about eight miles south of Java, to Frederick and
Rosina (Hausauer) Bieber, on Dec. 17, 1909.

Oscar and Tillie were married Mar. 2, 1930, at her parents' home on a day with a
raging blizzard. The minister came from Java, by sled and horses, to the
farmstead, now owned by Clinten and Sharon Bieber. They moved onto a farm near
by. Crops were good the first two years, but prices were low, wheat at 25 cents
a bushel. The dry years came in 1934-35-36. Some grain never came up. The
continual hard work was interspersed with visits with friends, baseball games,
listening to the radio, and an occasional dance. Oscar was a great baseball fan
and played catcher for a local team for a number of years.

In 1939, they bought the Ryan farm, now owned by their son and his wife, Wayne
and Beverly. The years of World War II were extremely busy, with unique
pressures and challenges to farmers. The need to produce food was great, but
hindered by rationing of materials, lack of new machinery, and scarce hired
help. The crops, however, were good.

Oscar and Tillie had three children: Delores Rosina married Russell Hendrick and
currently lives in Fridley, MN; Wayne Stanley married Beverly Stiegelmeier and
lives on the "home place" south of Java; Janice Marie passed away in 1984. She
was married to Carl Stracener and lived in Steilacoom, WA. Oscar and Tillie have
10 grandchildren and 13 great-grandchildren.

(Photo:) Oscar Schnaible Family. Back: Wayne and Delores. Front: Oscar, Janice
         (deceased) and Tillie

In 1963, Tillie and Oscar built their retirement home in Java, across the street
from their church, St. Paul Lutheran. They were very busy with church
activities. Tillie taught Sunday school for over 20 years, served on many
positions of the Ladies Aid, including president, and the church Altar Guild.
She was a beautiful quilter and seamstress, had a large vegetable and flower
garden, earned many ribbons for flower arrangements, and was a member of the
Java Garden Club.

Oscar continued farming with their son for several years before final
retirement. He also was active in the church, serving on various committees,
including the church council. He was the treasurer of the 1975 Java Jubilee
Executive Committee. Both of them very much enjoyed bowling in their retirement
years. Tillie died in 1986, Oscar in 1989.

        Wayne and Beverly (Stiegelmeier) Schnaible
Wayne S. Schnaible was born Feb. 5, 1936, at Bowdle, to Oscar and Tillie
Schnaible. He grew up 10 miles south of Java on the Ryan Homestead. He attended
rural grade school at the East Ryan School and then went on to Java High School,
graduating with the class of 1954. After graduation, Wayne was drafted into the
military service from June 1954 through June 1956. Upon his honorable discharge,
he returned to the family farm to begin grain and livestock farming.

(Photo:) Perry, Kelly, Beverly and Wayne Schnaible

Beverly J. Stiegelmeier was born Sept. 14, 1939, at Eureka, to Ben and Emma
Stiegelmeier. Beverly grew up in Java and attended grade and high school there.
She graduated from Java High School with the class of 1957. In Dec. of 1960,
Beverly graduated with a BS Degree in Education from NSC in Aberdeen. She taught
school in Sioux Falls and in Selby.

Beverly and Wayne were married June 25, 1961, and lived in Java one year, before
moving to their present home 10 miles south of Java.

Beverly and Wayne are parents to a son and a daughter. Perry married Roxane
(Rubida) and they live in Clear Lake. They are parents of two sons, John and
Matthew. Kelly married Michael Grieben of Aberdeen.

Over the years, Wayne has served on the school board and the church council.
Beverly taught Sunday school and served as officer in Ladies Aid (WELCA) and
school PTA.

        Peter and Katherina (Fuhrman) Schneider Sr.
Peter Schneider, Sr., was born Mar. 1856, in Rohrbach, South Russia, to Jacob
Peter and Catharina Schneider.

In 1877, he was married to Katherina Fuhrman, who was born May 16, 1857, in
Rohrbach, to Heinrich and Margaretha (Boehler) Fuhrmann. Peter and Katherina had
13 children, five of whom died in infancy.

Peter, Katherina and three small children left their home, family, and friends
in Russia and immigrated to the U.S. in 1887. They lived on a farm at Freeman
before they came to Eureka, to the farm home of Katherina's sister, Margaretha
(George) Feiock, where they stayed until Peter acquired land and built a two-
room sod house on Section 34, Township 125, Range 75. They applied for a patent,
according to the Homestead Act of President McKinley, on Nov. 27, 1895, on their
160 acres of land. Later they built their first wood frame house in the
community, and the sod house was made into a summer kitchen and used until the
early 1950's.

Peter, Jr., their oldest son, married Pauline Mauch and was the only one of
their eight children who moved and settled in Canada, in 1904. Kathryn married
John Hoffmann and had three children. They retired to Eureka. John passed away
in 1955 and Kathryn in 1960. Margaretha married Edward Blumhardt at the Odessa
Sutley Reformed Church. They moved to ND and farmed. They had 14 children, five
of whom died in infancy. Edward passed away in 1958, and Margaretha in 1972.
Henry was born on the farm north of Java. He married Katherine Hauck, daughter
of Carl and Elizabeth (Steinbach) Hauck. They had seven children. (See Family
History) Elizabeth was born on the farm eight miles north of Java. She married
Fred C. Hochstetter and they had 10 children. (See Family History) John was born
on the farm in 1892. He married Lydia Kary and they had four children. (See
Family History) William (Bill) was also born on the family farm in Campbell
County. He married Emma Werre and had seven children. (See Family History)
Johanna was born Oct. 12, 1900, at the farm. She married Jacob Naasz at the
Odessa Reformed Church, with Rev. Nuss of Artas officiating. They lived on a
farm six miles NE of Java, and had three sons, Harold, Howard, and a son who
died in infancy. Johanna passed away at the Mobridge Railroad Hospital on Aug.
16, 1934. She is buried in the Lutheran-Reformed Cemetery at Java. Jacob married
Martha Guthmiller and they had two sons. Jacob passed away in May 1971.

Peter, Sr., died on Sept. 22, 1917, and in 1920, Katherina moved to Java, into
what is now the Nettie Kast house.  Because of a lot of snow and no roads, she
had to have her things moved with a team of horses and sled. She passed away on
June 27, 1942. They are both buried in the Odessa Reformed Cemetery at Sutley, 9
miles north of Java.

        Henry and Katherine (Hauck) Schneider
Henry Schneider was born to Peter Schneider and Katherina Fuhrman on Sept. 20,
1888, at Java.

(Photo:) Henry and Katherine Schneider

Henry Schneider was married to Katherine Hauck on Sept. 14, 1911, at the Sutley
Reformed Church. Henry and Katherine lived on a farm eight miles north of Java
after their marriage. Seven children were born to them and all lived on farms in
the Java-Selby community. They moved to their new home in Selby in 1949.

Their children were: Albert, John J., Edna (Oscar) Himrich, Emma (Ervin) Haux,
Rinel, Irene married Rueben Bieber (deceased) and later married Art Fiedler, and
Theodore (Ted).

Henry passed away on Nov. 13, 1966, and Katherine on June 2, 1979. They were

Church Cemetery at Java.

        Albert and Lena (Ackerman) Schneider
Albert Schneider was born Nov. 14, 1912, to Henry and Katherine (Hauck)

Albert married Lena Ackerman on Mar. 12, 1937. They moved to a farm north of
Java, which was the former Mike Kary farm.

Albert was active on the Ackerman School board and also was on the building

(Photo:) Albert and Lena Schneider

Two daughters were born to them. Shirley was born Nov. 24, 1942, and attended

Albert and Lena retired and moved to Mobridge in 1963. Lena helped care for her

of surgery. Lena passed away on Dec. 18, 1985, at the Mobridge Hospital. Both

        Rinel and DeLila (Stiegelmeier) Schneider
Rinel and DeLila (Stiegelmeier) Schneider both grew up in the Java area and were
raised on farms. Rinel, the son of Henry and Katherine Schneider, was born Sept.
29, 1920; he attended the Kundert School. He later served his country from 1942
to 1946 in World War II. He received a bomb head-wound in France. Rinel was
later an interpreter and cared for 500 German prisoners. He received a Purple
Heart and, after being discharged, returned to the farm.

(Photo:) DeLila and Rinel Schneider

DeLila was born Mar. 8, 1930, to Jacob and Katie (Berg) Stiegelmeier, the
youngest of four children. After graduating from Java High School, she taught
school for three years.

On Aug. 2, 1949, Rinel and DeLila were married at St. Paul Lutheran Church in
Java. They farmed in the area for 35 years. It was a very enjoyable life. In
1954, a daughter, Rebecca, was born and in 1956, another daughter, Pamela, was
born. Rebecca is married to Allen Walth. Their son, Steven, and daughter,
Kristi, attend college at Brookings. Pamela is married to Bob Seyer. Pam and Bob
have two daughters, Kelly and Heidi. Kelly is a student at NSU. Their son Cody,
passed away Oct. 12, 1998, after an accident. Rebecca and Pam are both married
to farmers and live in the area. Pam is a Nurse and Becky is a Home Economist.
Their husbands are both graduates of SDSU.

Rinel and DeLila farmed most of their lives. They retired in 1984 and built a
home in Mobridge, where they have spent the last 15 years. They enjoy their
grandchildren, fishing, and doing a lot of gratis work.

        Herbert and Amanda (Job) Schneider
Herb was born to John and Lydia (Kary) Schneider in Campbell County on May 1,
1919, on his parents' farm. He attended the Kundert School near their home.
After his schooling, he farmed his Dad's place with his brother, Ruben.

He was inducted into the Army in Apr. 1942, and was in the 665th AAA Machine Gun
Battery. He was stationed in the U.S. and in New Guinea. Upon his discharge,
Herb returned to SD. He married Amanda Job on Feb. 17, 1949, at St. Paul
Lutheran Church in Java. They lived and worked on their farm north of Java,
until they retired and moved to Mobridge in 1984.

(Photo:) Amanda and Herb Schneider

Herbert passed away June 22, 1990, at the age of 71, and is buried in the
Greenwood Cemetery at Mobridge. Amanda remained in their home in Mobridge until
July 1999, when she had a stroke. She resides at ManorCare in Aberdeen, where
she attends nearly all of the many activities. Her sister, Margaret Anderson,
also resides there. Herb and Amanda had three sons.

Dean, born Aug. 8, 1950, attended a rural school during the 1st grade. He then
continued his education at the Java school, graduating from Java High School in
1968. He joined the Air Force and was stationed in Biloxi, MS; Goosebay,
Labrador; Tacoma, WA; and Germany. Dean moved to Denver because he heard that's
where the girls were. He met Kathleen Howard and married her on Aug. 21, 1977,
after a three-year courtship. Kathy was raised in Arvada, CO, and graduated from

(Photo:) Scott, Kathy, Justin and Dean Schneider

Dean started his business, Film/Video Equipment Service Company, shortly after
arriving in Denver. His business has expanded from 400 square feet to 52,000

Dean and Kathy have two sons. Justin was born in 1980. He was editor-in-chief of

Scott was born in 1983. He attends high school, where he is producer of the

Dennis was born Feb. 1, 1952, graduated from Java High School in 1970, and lives
on the family farm north of Java. He is married to Jeanne Boehler. (See Family
History)

Jerry, born Aug. 13, 1954, graduated from Java High School in 1972, and from
SDSU at Brookings in 1976. He was employed at F & M Bank in Aberdeen until 1978,
when he moved to Denver and joined his brother Dean in Film/Video Equipment
Service Company. Jerry married Kathleen Maltese nee Braband on Sept. 19, 1987.
Kathy is a homemaker and is involved in various activities. She is a volunteer

(Photo:) Jerry and Kathy Schneider

        Dennis and Jeanne (Boehler) Schneider
Dennis was born to Herb and Amanda (Job) Schneider on Feb. 1, 1952. He attended
school in Java, graduating from Java High School in 1970. He served in the U.S.
Army from 1971 to 1973, with the 207th MP Company stationed at Ft. Riley, KS,
where he was a guard and counselor. After his honorable discharge, he was
employed at Northern Farm Supply in Aberdeen, as Construction Foreman serving ND
and SD. Dennis later was the elevator manager at Java and Selby, and then took a
position as Commercial Construction Superintendent for Missouri Basin Builders
in Mobridge. In 1981, Dennis partnered with his father in the farming operation,
raising grain and cattle. Herb retired and Dennis became the sole operator of
the farming business. He opted out of the cattle business in 1992, replacing the
cattle with a Payloader and gravel truck, for custom work. Dennis, an avid Jets
fan, enjoys his annual male-bonding trip to Vegas with the Biel Boys, Fiedlers
and several other area men. He also enjoys golf, bowling and visiting. He was an
active member of the Java Community Club, serving as Treasurer, Vice-president
and President for four years each.

(Photo:) Dennis and Jeanne Schneider

Dennis married Jeanne Boehler on Feb. 17, 1984, the daughter of Marge and Rueben
Boehler of Java. Jeanne was raised in Java and spent a large amount of time at
her grandparents' farms south and west of Java. She recalls the family's move to
Mobridge in 1955 as being at least 2,000 miles away from home. Jeanne moved back
to Java in 1983, after over 20 years in CA, when her Dad became seriously ill.
The initial transition from urban to rural life was exceptionally difficult, but
being of hardy stock, she made the best of it and now can't imagine living
anywhere but in a rural area. Jeanne is a charter member of KITT Club and served
as president. She was owner/operator of a craft business for some time,
attending fairs throughout the state. In 1990, Jeanne opened an office services
business on Main St. in Mobridge, where she also managed the H & R Block office.
In 1992, she learned that Toyotas couldn't fly, when she went off the bridge
between Java and Selby and landed on the railroad tracks. In that same year,
Dennis and Jeanne entered a partnership in Mobridge and opened a salvage grocery
business. Later in 1992, Jeanne was diagnosed with a rare cancer and was flown
to Rochester, MN, for surgery. After her recovery, she moved her office business
onto the farm north of Java, where she continued bookkeeping services for four
more years. Jeanne, an eight-year cancer survivor, is the Editor of the Java
Centennial Book. In her spare time, she enjoys playing the piano, is an avid
reader, a member of GRHS, a jazz and classical music fan, spends many warm-
weather days searching for artifacts and fossils, and loves three out of four SD
seasons. Living near her parents is one of her many blessings.

        William and Emma (Werre) Schneider
William Schneider was born on Sept. 13, 1893, to Peter and Katherina (Fuhrman)
Schneider, Sr., north of Java in Campbell County.

He attended rural school and college at Eureka. He farmed with his parents until
he was called to serve his country during World War I, in 1917. A short time
after he had left, his father had a stroke and was bedridden until his death on
Sept. 21, 1917. At that time, William was discharged so he could help his mother
run the farm.

His mother continued to live on the farm with William, until he got married. She
then moved to Java to make her home. Nettie (Leon) Kast now owns the house.

William married Emma Werre at Eureka on Jan. 13, 1920. They lived on the family
farm that was homesteaded by William's father. In 1949, they bought a home in
Java and retired.

Seven children were born to this couple. Raymond (deceased) married Ernestine
Kurle (deceased). They had two daughters and one son. Vernard married Ella Mertz
and they had one son. Erwin married Lydia Buechler and had one daughter and two
sons. Hilda married Merle Wahl and has one son. Meta married Elmer Lang and they
have one daughter and one son. Della married Leland Berndt and they have six
sons and two daughters. Delbert married Joan Nelles and they have three sons and
one daughter.

(Photo:) William Schneider Family. Back: Meta, Vernard, Raymond, Ervin, Hilda.
         Front: Della, William, Emma and Delbert

Emma passed away Mar. 5, 1958. William continued to make his home in Java until
1973, when his health began to fail. He became a resident at the Good Samaritan
Center at Selby. He passed away on Feb. 12, 1978 and is buried beside his wife
in the Lutheran Cemetery at Java.

        Henry J. and Marie (Baer) Schreter
Henry J. Schreter was born in Hoffnungstal, South Russia, on Nov. 27, 1885. He
came to America with his grandmother, and uncle John Schnaible, at a young age.
His grandmother became very ill on the ship. She died and was buried in Canada,
so young Henry was on his own. He worked for his uncle Karl to pay for his trip
to America. After that, he worked a number of years for Ed Jerguson SW of Java.

In 1907, he was united in marriage to Marie Baer. Pastor Geo. Kirchdoerfer
performed the ceremony in the Lutheran church at Java. Marie was born Oct. 16,
1886, in Russia, a daughter of John H. and Margaretha Herman Baer. She came to
America with her parents in 1893. The Baer family came to Freeman and later
moved to Walworth County and filed claim on the land now owned by John
Schnaible, Jr., south of Java. After Henry J. and Marie were married, they lived
on a farm south of Java owned by Helen Riecks (relatives of I.C. Pratton). They
later moved on a farm four miles north of Lowry, which they later bought from
Jake and Wm. Schott.

To this union seven children were born: Henry E. married Magdalene Bieber; Marie
married Gustave Bieber (deceased) and lives in Mobridge; Esther married Lester
Reed; Lillian married Gerhardt Walz; Albert married Janet Caswell; Herman
married Irene Derwald; and Elsie, who passed away in 1937 at the age of 15.

(Photo:) Henry J. and Marie Schreter

Henry J. was a charter member of Zion Lutheran Church of Lowry and helped build
the church in 1914.

Marie and Henry moved to Java in 1948 and were members of St. Paul Lutheran
Church. Henry passed away on Nov. 11, 1950 and Marie passed away Jan. 4, 1959.

        Henry E. and Magdalene (Bieber) Schreter
Henry E. Schreter was born to Henry J. and Marie (Baer) Schreter on Dec. 10,
1907, on a farm 12 miles south of Java. Later, his parents bought a farm four
miles north of Lowry, where he was raised and went to a country school. On Nov.
3, 1929, Rev. George Kirchdoerfer performed the ceremony uniting Henry and
Magdalene Bieber in marriage.

Magdalene, daughter of Fred and Rosina (Hausauer) Bieber, was born five miles
north of Eureka on Sept. 25, 1908, in a sod house, where her Bieber grandparents
lived. When the house was seen in Aug. of 1997, it had been modernized and a
family was living in it. Magdalene moved with her parents to a farm seven miles
south of Java in 1911. She received her education at East Ryan School, where
they had from 20-30 pupils and all grades. A teacher didn't have it too easy
those days.

After marriage, they moved on a farm seven miles east of Lowry, near Swan Lake,
which was known as a duck-hunting lake. Many a hunter, local and out-of-state,
got their share of ducks. It was the beginning of the Dirty Thirties and drought
when Henry and Magdalene learned what cow chips were used for.

(Photo:) Donna, Harold, Jeral, Karen, Magdalene and Henry Schreter

To this union four children were born. Harold married Ann Witlock, Donna married
Calvin Wolff, who passed away Mar. 2, 1998, Jeral married Dolores Meier and
Karen married Ronald Schneider.

In Nov. 1967, Henry and Magdalene moved to Java, and their son, Harold, took
over the farm. Henry helped out on the farm for a number of years. After
retiring completely, he spent a lot of time fishing.

After being married 65+ years, Henry passed away from cancer on June 13, 1995,
at the age of 87. Magdalena continues to reside in their home in Java.

        Harold and Ann (Witlock) Schreter
Harold was born Sept. 21, 1930, to Henry and Magdalene Schreter. He lived in the
Lowry area. Harold attended high school in Java and graduated from Java High
School in 1948. He married Ann Witlock on Nov. 11, 1951. Ann was born June 20,
1931, to John and Louise Witlock. She attended high school in Java and graduated

He was then sent to Fairbanks, AK. Ann always says she was in the Army because
she went with him. Harold decided to be a farmer and they have farmed 15 miles
south of Java for 47 years. They have lived on the home place for 31 years.

Timothy married Penny Bieber and they live in Broomfield, CO, with their two

        John and Fredricka (Schlepp) Schuh Sr.
John Schuh, Sr., was born Sept. 23, 1864, in Hoffnung-stal, South Russia, where
he grew to manhood. On Dec. 10, 1887, he was united in marriage to Fredricka
Schlepp, who was born in Hoffnungstal on Mar. 31 1868. This couple made their
home in Russia for about two years, where the oldest son, John, was born.

(Photo:) John and Fredricka Schuh, Sr. Family

On May 16, 1889, the family, along with several other families, left Russia and
migrated to America to seek new homes. They landed in New York City; plans had
been made before leaving Russia that, upon arriving in America, they would
continue west to the Dakota Territory. From New York, they journeyed by rail as
far as Bowdle. In this area, relatives and friends, also from Russia, had
arrived and settled some time earlier.

The Schuh family homesteaded five miles NE of what is now Java, in Adams
District, Walworth County. Here a farm was built and grain and livestock farming
became their livelihood. Among other hardships and tragedies, these pioneers
experienced a severe diphtheria epidemic in 1900 that took the lives of many of
their children. The home of the Schuh family was also saddened by the death of
three children within a few days, caused by the epidemic. A tornado swept
through the area in the early years, doing considerable damage to some of the
farm homes. Distance from towns and lack of fast transportation caused hardships
during the long cold winters. The pioneer spirit, however, prevailed and as time
moved on, conditions improved.

As more and more families arrived from the old country and settled in the area,
people realized that, even though visiting pastors would occasionally hold
church services in the homes, provisions for their spiritual needs had to be
provided for with the community. Some of the families formed a Lutheran
congregation and built a church in 1897, which was called Hoffnungstahl
Gemeinde.

Twelve children were born to the Schuh family, six boys and six girls: John,
Java, deceased; three epidemic victims were: Magdalena, Jacob and David;
Elizabeth Wolf, McLaughlin, deceased; Helen Schlaht, Lodi, CA, deceased; Fred,
Java, deceased; Adolph, Java; Lydia Schlepp, Java; Christ, Lodi, CA, deceased;
Ida Perman, Java, deceased; and Bertha Kunz, Watertown, deceased.

Adding to the homestead, the family remained on the farm until 1922, when the
parents retired to a home, built in Java. Here, Fredricka passed away in 1928
and John, Sr., passed away in 1934.

        John and Emma (Boehler) Schuh
In 1889, John Schuh, Jr., eldest son of John and Fredricka Schuh, was 9 months
old when his young parents began their journey across the Atlantic Ocean from
their native Russia to their new home in America.

John's parents staked out their claim eight miles NE of Java in Walworth County.
He and his brothers and sisters attended country school here and grew to young
adults. When John was a teenager, one of his favorite pastimes was to pedal his
bike along the bumpy country road to the town of Java, where he would purchase
an ice cream cone. On these excursions, he was often accompanied by his cousin
and neighbor, Sam Schlepp.

In April 1913, when John was 25 years old, he married Emma Boehler, the oldest
daughter of Gottlieb and Eva (Wolf) Boehler. Shortly afterwards they moved their
home a few miles east of his parents. He had purchased this small farm, known as
the Adam place, from his father. He leased the adjoining land. To supplement his
meager farm income, he worked each fall for a threshing rig.

Emma had worked since she was 12 years old, sometimes as a cook's helper, and
also as a housemaid for families in the area. At one time, she worked for the
family of the late E.B. Adams, an early Walworth County attorney.

The young couple worked hard to improve their home, but was hampered by drought,
crop failures and Depression. In 1936, when all the surrounding land was sold to
a neighbor, the Schuhs were forced to give up their home and move to a rented
farm.

(Photo:) John and Emma Schuh, Jr. Family

In 1950, they moved to their home in Java. Here, Emma died suddenly in Oct.
1953, at the age of 57. John lived alone until a paralytic stroke caused him to
become bedridden and his last two years were spent in the Selby Nursing Home,
where he passed away in 1965 at the age of 77.

John and Emma were parents of two sons, Ellsworth and Raymond, and one daughter,
Loretta. Ellsworth, deceased, and his wife, Freida lived on a farm east of Java,
which was the George Naasz homestead. Raymond, deceased, lived in CA, near the
oldest of three children. Loretta and Cornelius Schnaible live in Java and have
three sons, James, Patrick and Thomas. (See Family History)

        Ellsworth and Freida (Frazier) Schuh by Freida Schuh
The Meeting: Ellsworth Schuh met Freida Frazier on a Sunday evening in the fall
of 1934, when he was playing his accordion at a dance in the old building called
"The Shack", NE of Java in the Horse Shoe Lake area. He was a local boy and she
had come from Mobridge to teach in the Hartman School in Adams School District.
"The Shack" was a fitting name for this gathering place as it was a deserted old
building and had been left to the ravages of Mother Nature and the elements;
however, it served as a shelter of sorts, and many a romance began there.

(Photo:) Ellsworth and Freida Schuh

Ellsworth: Ellsworth was born at his home NE of Java on May 11, 1914, the first
son of John Schuh, Jr., and his wife Emma Boehler Schuh, and also the first
grandchild of John Schuh, Sr., and his wife Fredricka Schlepp Schuh, and the
first grandchild of Gottlieb Boehler and his wife Eva Wolf Boehler.

He was raised on his parents' farm and attended the Horse Shoe Lake School in
Adams School District through the eighth grade. As many other farm boys, he was
needed at home, so was not able to attend high school. He had a younger brother,
Raymond, now deceased, and a little sister, Emma Loretta, now Mrs. Cornelius
Schnaible, and who lives in Java. Ellsworth called her "Sisterli."

The family loved music and dancing, and Ellsworth started playing on a
dilapidated twelve-base accordion. He was encouraged by an elderly school
teacher who boarded at the Schuh home. After he was able to save enough money,
he bought a used 120 base accordion and was soon playing for gatherings and
parties. Raymond also learned to play the accordion, and then Loretta took
lessons from Mrs. Lena Hicks and became a very fine musician. She plays not only
the piano, but organ and accordion as well. In later years Ellsworth purchased
an electronic organ and played for many dances and parties.

Ellsworth was a self-taught repairman and mechanic. He did repair work and
welding for his neighbors. He also repaired accordions and organs and at one
time he bought three broken down organs for $10 and worked on them during the
winter, and made a good-sized profit.

Freida: Freida was born to Pete Frazier and Josephine Boutiette Frazier on June
6, 1913, at Mobridge. Her parents were one of the first families to settle in
Mobridge. They moved from Evarts. Pete was a well-known horseman, and built and
ran one of the first livery stables in Mobridge. Sisters Georgia and Joy, and
one brother, Edward (deceased) were born in Evarts. Olive (deceased) was the
first baby girl born in Mobridge, and Frances is the youngest of the family. All
the Frazier kids attended and graduated from Mobridge High School. Freida
borrowed money from A.H. Brown, a Mobridge businessman, and attended NSTC for
one year, which certified her to teach in any rural school in the state. She
worked for her board and room, and kept track of all of her expenses, which
amounted to $197 for one year of college! She attended College Summer School and
took extension courses until she had enough credits to graduate with a Bachelor
of Science Degree in Elementary Education.

Together Then Alone: Ellsworth and Freida were married in Timber Lake June 21,
1939. They lived with Ellsworth's parents the first three years, then lived on
rented farms, including I.C. Krause's, where Harlan now lives, north of Java. In
1957, they bought a farm five miles east of Java. Freida continued to teach in
area rural schools and 20 years in the Java Public School. She had taught a
total of 40 years when she retired in 1977.

Ellsworth's health had been declining and he became unable to keep up the farm,
so they bought a small house in Java in 1982. He still enjoyed going to the farm
where it was quiet and where he could "putter."

Ellsworth passed away Sept. 29, 1984. They were married 45 years.

Freida has continued to be active in the community and church. She taught Sunday
school and Vacation Bible School. She has been active in Lutheran Church Women
and served as an officer, and on various committees. She sang in the Lutheran
church choir for 37 years and served as its director for 16 of those years. She
has been active in Lutheran Brotherhood and has served as a branch president for
10 years. Through her leadership, Missouri River Branch has earned superior
ratings for 10 consecutive years. She is a charter member of Java Senior
Citizens, and a charter member of Java Arts Council, which hasn't been active
since the Java school closed. She was hostess to many artists in school and to
members of the cast of Missoula Children's Theater.

Recently Freida sold her house in Java and is presently living in an apartment
in Mobridge. She says that she misses Java and her friends. [Written May 1998]

        Fred and Katherine (Rieger) Schuh
